skills.name: Cassette Futurism
skills.thesis: The future is a machine with visible switches: every function has a physical control, a label and a status light, and the casing shows the wear of use.
skills.summary: Bulky hardware from a future imagined on tape: CRT monitors, membrane keys, toggle switches and beige casings, with amber or green phosphor text. It draws on Syd Mead's industrial futures and Japanese bubble-era electronics. The look is functional, worn and a little cramped.

pack.why: Square, blocky glyphs match the panel symbols and the pixel screens of the period.

ground.why: Cassette futurism lives on a phosphor screen with visible scan lines and a dark bezel.

use_cases: developer tools with a terminal character

skills.name: Punk Zine
skills.thesis: Anyone can publish: make the page with scissors, glue and a copier, and show the seams on purpose.
skills.summary: Photocopied black and white, cut-and-paste letters, typewriter text, tape and hand scrawl. It came from the punk scenes of London and New York and shows that anyone can make a page.

pack.why: A rough, marker-like line with uneven form that reads as a hand drawing.

ground.why: A zine is a photocopy: heavy toner grain, black blocks and a strip of tape.

skills.name: Usenet Thread
skills.thesis: A discussion is a tree of plain-text replies, and each reply quotes the part that it answers.
skills.summary: A thread of plain-text posts in a newsgroup, read in a terminal newsreader: a tree of subject lines, quoted lines that start with >, and a signature under each post.

pack.why: Square pixel icons fit a character grid.

ground.why: A terminal screen: dark rows of glyphs with faint scan lines.

use_cases: developer mailing list and changelog pages

skills.name: Memphis Design
skills.thesis: Good taste is a convention, and a loud, cheap, playful object can carry as much meaning as a serious one.
skills.summary: Clashing primary and pastel fields, squiggles, confetti dots and black-and-white pattern on irregular geometric forms. Ettore Sottsass and the Memphis group launched it in Milan in 1981 as a joke against good taste.

pack.why: Bold forms with a hard offset tone: the flat pop geometry of the laminate.

ground.why: Memphis scatters small loud shapes, squiggles and dot fields over a white ground.

corner_radius.note: The token rounds one corner only. The knob is that corner; the square corners stay square.

skills.name: ANSI BBS Art
skills.thesis: A picture is a grid of characters: every shape must fit an 8 by 16 pixel cell and one of 16 colours.
skills.summary: Pictures and menus made of 80-column text blocks in the 16 ANSI colours: shade characters, box lines and wide logos. Dial-up bulletin boards showed them, and art groups released them in monthly packs.

pack.why: Pixel icons share the square cell of a text-mode screen.

ground.why: The ground is a field of 8 by 16 pixel cells, as on a text-mode screen.

use_cases: game and tool launch screens in text mode

skills.name: Kaomoji and Emoticon
skills.thesis: A face needs no picture: a few characters of one text font, in one colour, carry a whole feeling.
skills.summary: A face made of punctuation and letters, set in a line of plain text. It came from 1980s bulletin boards: the sideways :-) in the West and the upright (^_^) in Japan.

pack.why: A pixel family fits faces built on a character grid, with square terminals.

ground.why: A kaomoji lives on the plain paper of a text line, so the ground stays flat.

use_cases: friendly empty states in a CLI

skills.name: Cyberdelia
skills.thesis: The computer is a consciousness machine: use acid colour, fractal repetition and raw early software effects to show a mind that has gone into the network.
skills.summary: The psychedelic side of early cyberculture. It joins cyberpunk with acid colour: fractals, kaleidoscopes, posterised Photoshop collage, early 3D type and rave flyers. It takes its name from the club in the film Hackers (1995).

pack.why: Heavy solid forms with a thick edge match the loud shapes of a rave flyer.

ground.why: Cyberdelia mixes rave flyer spirals with screen colour in one turning field.

use_cases: club, festival and music event pages

skills.name: Grunge Editorial
skills.thesis: Legibility is not the same as communication, and a page can carry the mood of its content by looking as rough as the content feels.
skills.summary: Layered, distressed type, overprinted photographs and broken columns, set by hand in early Macintosh software. David Carson at Ray Gun and the Emigre studio made it the look of 1990s alternative music and youth magazines.

pack.why: A doubled, off-register line: the look of a bad print run.

ground.why: Grunge layouts are scanned and copied again until the grain and the dirt are part of the type.

skills.name: Net Art Browser
skills.thesis: The browser is the material: show its defaults, its errors and its source as the work itself.
skills.summary: Art made inside the browser from raw HTML: default grey ground, blue links, Times text, broken frames and visible code. The net.art artists of the 1990s used the window as the canvas.

pack.why: Plain square pixel marks keep the raw, unstyled feel of default HTML.

ground.why: The ground is the bare browser window with no pattern.

use_cases: art project pages and festival sites

skills.name: GeoCities Homepage
skills.thesis: Every person owns a page, and the page shows what its owner loves, with no care for taste.
skills.summary: A personal page with a tiled star or marble background, rainbow rules, animated GIFs, a visitor counter, a guestbook and an under-construction sign. Free web hosts such as GeoCities made it common.

pack.why: Pixel icons match the 32px GIFs of a homepage.

ground.why: The ground is a tiled background with scattered coloured marks, like a stars-and-marble tile.

use_cases: nostalgic fan pages and personal sites

skills.name: Bulletin Board Forum
skills.thesis: A forum is a club with rooms; each member carries a visible rank, a picture and a signature from post to post.
skills.summary: A web forum in tables: a list of boards in categories, topics with reply and view counts, and posts with a user column that shows an avatar, a rank, a post count and a signature.

pack.why: Small filled icons match the folder, pin and lock icons of a topic list.

ground.why: A forum is ruled tables: thin lines between the rows.

skills.name: Portal Table Layout
skills.thesis: One page holds the whole web: pack every service, link and ad into a clear table of boxes.
skills.summary: A dense start page in HTML tables: a search box, a link directory, news boxes, banner ads and a blue and orange palette. Web portals of the late 1990s used it to keep a user on one site.

pack.why: Small square marks match the 16px GIF icons of a portal.

ground.why: The ground is white with thin grey rules between table cells.

use_cases: directory and news pages in a retro style

skills.name: Y2K Aesthetic
skills.thesis: Technology is friendly and the future is shiny, so an interface should look like a new gadget that is already finished.
skills.summary: Chrome and translucent plastic, bubble shapes, silver and electric blue, and small pixel and tech type on cold gradients. It came from the dot-com boom and the first iMac in 1998, and it pictured the year 2000 as a clean, shiny future.

pack.why: Pixel-grid forms: the screen technology of the period shows in the icon.

ground.why: Y2K screens float glossy colour spheres behind frosted panels.

skills.name: Flash Intro Site
skills.thesis: A site is a performance: control every pixel and every second, and make the visitor wait for it.
skills.summary: A full-window site built as vector animation: a loading bar, a 'skip intro' link, tiny pixel type, custom cursors, sound and transitions between sections. Macromedia Flash made it possible.

pack.why: Pixel icons match the tiny pixel navigation of a Flash site.

ground.why: The ground is a dark stage with faint light rays, like the opening scene of a Flash intro.

skills.name: Japanese Dense Web
skills.thesis: Density is hospitality: show all the options at once, so the visitor never has to search.
skills.summary: Dense pages with many links, small type, bright accent colours, banners, ranking lists and tight grids. It grew from portals such as Yahoo! JAPAN and Rakuten and makes a page rich in choice.

pack.why: A compact, solid family that stays clear at 16px beside 12px to 14px text.

ground.why: Dense Japanese portals sit on a ruled grid with a colour bar across the top.

skills.name: Apple Aqua
skills.thesis: The screen is a liquid, tactile surface: every control is a glossy drop that invites a click.
skills.summary: Translucent blue gel buttons, pinstripe backgrounds, glossy droplets and brushed-metal windows. It came with Mac OS X in 2000 and made the screen look like water and candy.

pack.why: A solid, soft-cornered family with volume that matches the glossy, filled look of gel controls.

ground.why: Aqua windows sit on fine grey pinstripes, with a glow of blue light under them.

use_cases: app landing pages with a friendly tone

skills.name: Anonymous Imageboard
skills.thesis: Nobody has a name, so only the post counts; the newest reply keeps a thread alive.
skills.summary: An anonymous board where each thread starts with an image: a pale page, posts with no account, post numbers, green quoted lines and threads that bump to the top and then fall off.

pack.why: Small pixel icons match the 16px pins and flags of a board.

ground.why: A stock HTML page: a flat tinted ground with nothing on it.

skills.name: Myspace Profile
skills.thesis: A profile is a bedroom wall: the owner decorates it, and the decoration says who they are.
skills.summary: A user profile page that the owner restyled with pasted CSS: a wallpaper, glitter text, a music player, a Top 8 friends grid and a mirror-selfie photo. Myspace made the page a personal stage.

pack.why: The pop style of this pack matches the cut-out stickers on a profile.

ground.why: The ground is a dark wallpaper with a few bright spots, as on a custom profile.

skills.name: Demotivational poster
skills.thesis: Turn the cheerful office poster into a dry joke: the same frame and layout, with a bleak caption.
skills.summary: A black poster with a thin white frame, a photo, a large serif capital title and a small line of sad or dry text. It parodies the office motivational poster and spread on web forums from 2004.

pack.why: A thin outline family that stays quiet beside the serif title.

ground.why: The ground is black with a thin white frame, as on the poster.

skills.name: Frutiger Aero
skills.thesis: Technology belongs to nature and the human world, so a digital interface should look clean, glossy, alive and pleasant to touch.
skills.summary: Glossy glass buttons, aqua and grass-green gradients, water, sky and bubble imagery and humanist sans type. It grew from Y2K gloss into the Windows Vista, Mac OS X Aqua and Web 2.0 look of the late 2000s.

pack.why: Soft, filled forms with round corners that sit well in a glossy round container.

ground.why: Frutiger Aero shows clean water bubbles over a green hill and a bright sky.

skills.name: Web 2.0 Gloss
skills.thesis: A site is a friendly tool: make every control look glossy, round and easy to press.
skills.summary: Glossy rounded buttons, vertical gradients, reflections under logos, big friendly type, star badges and a 'beta' tag on a clean white page. Social and tool start-ups used it after 2004.

pack.why: Rounded filled icons with two tones match the glossy tiles of the first social web.

ground.why: The ground is a pale sky gradient above a white page, as in a start-up landing page.

use_cases: parody of the first social web

skills.name: Reddit Thread
skills.thesis: The crowd ranks every post and every reply; the best answer floats to the top.
skills.summary: A link or a text post in a topic group, with a score that the crowd votes up or down, and nested comments sorted by votes, each level marked by a thin line at the left.

pack.why: Bold outline arrows and bubbles match the vote and comment icons.

ground.why: A plain grey page under white cards, with nothing behind the content.

skills.name: Impact image macro
skills.thesis: Make the caption the picture: one setup line on top, one punch line below, in a font that stays legible at any size.
skills.summary: A square photo or a cartoon with white capital text in a thick black outline at the top and the bottom. The Impact typeface and the format spread on forums and 4chan from 2006.

pack.why: A sharp solid family with hard corners that matches thick outlined capitals.

ground.why: The ground is the raw photograph; the page shows no designed surface.

skills.name: Unboxing Video
skills.thesis: The viewer owns the first touch by proxy: show the opening of the box in real time and let the object, not the frame, carry the interest.
skills.summary: A fixed top-down shot of a table. Two hands open a box and lift out a product, and a voice names each part. The look is plain on purpose, so the object is the star.

pack.why: A plain outline family with round terminals fits the neutral labels and chips of a product shot.

ground.why: The ground is the plain, pale table that every unboxing shot starts from.

skills.name: Skeuomorphism
skills.thesis: A screen control is easier to learn when it looks and behaves like a physical object that the user already knows.
skills.summary: Interfaces that copy real objects: leather, linen, wood, felt, glass and brushed metal, lit from above with gradients and layered shadows. It has roots in 1980s desktop icons and peaked in iOS 1 to 6, until iOS 7 replaced it in 2013.

pack.why: Full solid silhouettes of real objects. The container supplies the material and the light.

ground.why: Skeuomorphic apps put their panels on a woven linen texture with a top light.

use_cases: games with a table or board

skills.name: Rage comic
skills.thesis: Tell a small daily frustration in a few crude panels, with stock faces that every reader knows.
skills.summary: A short comic of 2 to 8 panels drawn in MS Paint with a set of crude faces that show one fixed emotion each. It began on 4chan in 2008 and filled Reddit and 9GAG until about 2015.

pack.why: A hand-drawn pop family with uneven strokes that match crude panel art.

ground.why: A plain copied white sheet matches the paint-program ground.

skills.name: Reaction GIF
skills.thesis: A looped second of a real face says a feeling faster than a sentence, so the clip is the reply.
skills.summary: A short looped clip from a film, a show or a sport, sent in place of a sentence. The frame is small, grainy and often carries a one-line caption in heavy white capitals.

pack.why: A solid, rounded family fits the small action glyphs under a clip.

ground.why: The dither and compression grain of a looped clip read as a coarse dot field behind the page.

use_cases: social posts and newsletters with a joke
empty and success states with a human face
meme walls and tag search pages

skills.name: ASMR Video
skills.thesis: Slow the image to match the sound: a calm frame, a soft light and a close mic make the viewer relax.
skills.summary: A soft, close picture with a mic near the subject. Slow hands tap, brush and whisper. The look is dim, warm and quiet, with almost no text, because sound carries the work.

pack.why: A thin outline family with round terminals matches the soft, quiet frame.

ground.why: The ground is a dim room lit by one warm lamp, and the vignette keeps the eye on the subject.

skills.name: Glitch GIF
skills.thesis: A fault in the signal is an image: show the error, do not hide it.
skills.summary: A looped clip with torn bands, split colour channels and repeated frames, as if the signal failed. Artists on Tumblr and in net art circles made it common after 2010.

pack.why: Hard pixel glyphs match the block noise and the square terminals of a broken signal.

ground.why: A glitch loop shows the scan lines of the failing video signal.

use_cases: title cards for dark, edgy content

skills.name: Instagram Vintage Filter
skills.thesis: One tap turns a plain phone snapshot into a keepsake: the filter, the frame and the vignette supply the age that the photo does not have.
skills.summary: A phone photo in a square 1:1 frame with a one-tap filter: warm fade, lifted blacks, a dark vignette and a thick white border. It made a phone snapshot look like an old print.

pack.why: A line family that matches the thin, round app icons of the first photo apps.

ground.why: The ground is the white print border: a frame around a square photo.

skills.name: Let's Play Facecam
skills.thesis: The game is the stage and the face is the audience: put the reaction next to the action, and the viewer follows the player, not the game.
skills.summary: Game footage fills the frame and a small live window of the player's face sits in one corner. The face reacts, and loud captions and zoom cuts push the mood.

pack.why: A thick, solid family matches the loud, high-contrast captions and the bold game frame.

ground.why: The ground is a dark monitor image with fine scanlines, the screen that the game runs on.

use_cases: game launch trailers with a host

skills.name: Metro UI
skills.thesis: Content is the interface: remove chrome, use type and motion for hierarchy, and let flat colour tiles carry the brand.
skills.summary: Flat colour tiles, large light typography, a strict grid and content before chrome. It came from Windows Phone 7 in 2010 and drew on Swiss signage and airport wayfinding.

pack.why: A plain 2px line glyph with sharp joins that sits well inside a thin circle.

ground.why: Metro is a wall of flat live tiles in solid colour on a black field.

use_cases: internal tools with a clear tone

skills.name: Pixel Art Web
skills.thesis: Limits are the style: few pixels, few colours and a hard grid make a clear, playful picture.
skills.summary: Blocky sprites, a limited palette, hard pixel edges, bitmap type and game-style panels. It borrows from 8-bit and 16-bit games and makes a page feel like a game screen.

pack.why: A pixel family drawn on a strict 24px grid that fits bitmap type.

ground.why: Pixel art draws a night sky of single pixels over stepped hills on a coarse grid.

skills.name: Unicode Emoji
skills.thesis: A picture becomes a character: the same small yellow face can enter any text on any device.
skills.summary: A set of small colour pictures that sit in text as characters: yellow faces, hands, food and flags. Japanese phone makers drew the first sets; Unicode 6.0 added them to the standard in 2010.

pack.why: A filled, rounded family sits close to the flat colour glyphs of an emoji set.

ground.why: An emoji sits on a plain light field, so the yellow and the other glyph colours carry the page.

skills.name: Wojak and feels
skills.thesis: Reduce a mood to one drawn face and a short label, so that a reader sees the feeling at once.
skills.summary: A bald, line-drawn face in grey and cream with an exact emotion, set in a flat panel with a caption. It started on imageboards around 2010 and now stands for many roles. This entry covers its neutral drawing form only.

pack.why: A plain hand-feel outline family that keeps the flat drawn tone.

ground.why: A soft flat field keeps one muted colour behind the figure.

skills.name: Chat Sticker Pack
skills.thesis: A character with a big face says what a sentence cannot: the chat gets a mascot with a voice.
skills.summary: A set of 8 to 40 drawn characters with a pose, a big face and one short word, sent in a chat as a picture. The LINE messenger made the form common in Asia from 2011.

pack.why: A chunky, cartoon family matches the heavy outline of a sticker.

ground.why: A sticker pack is a sheet of small shapes, so the ground scatters confetti behind the grid.

use_cases: messenger sticker sets and brand mascots
merch and social posts with a mascot

skills.name: Cinemagraph
skills.thesis: The image is still, and one small motion makes the viewer look longer.
skills.summary: A still photograph in which one small part moves in a seamless loop: hair in wind, steam from a cup, a blink. Two New York artists named it in 2011 during fashion week.

pack.why: A fine outline family suits a quiet page where the photograph leads.

ground.why: A cinemagraph needs a quiet field, so the page ground is a soft dark wash that leaves the photograph alone.

use_cases: product pages with one moving detail
ad banners that need calm motion

skills.name: Livestream Overlay
skills.thesis: A live show needs a control room on screen: the frame holds every live signal in fixed slots, so the viewer always knows where to look.
skills.summary: A frame around a live game or camera. It has a facecam slot, a chat panel, an alert box and a name bar. Neon edges and animated panels show that the stream is live.

pack.why: A solid family with square terminals fits the cut-corner panels and the small alert marks.

ground.why: The ground is a dark control screen with scanlines, the room where a live show is run.

skills.name: Seapunk
skills.thesis: Put the early web underwater: its 3D shapes, clip art and gradients float on a sea of turquoise.
skills.summary: Turquoise and aqua water, dolphins, shells, floating 3D shapes and tie-dye, with 1990s web graphics. It started as a joke tweet in 2011 and grew into an ocean theme in music and fashion.

pack.why: Rounded, filled icons match the glossy, bubble-like shapes of 1990s 3D water graphics.

ground.why: Seapunk floats glossy shapes in water, so the ground is a field of bubbles on a water gradient.

skills.name: Bohemian Web
skills.thesis: The page is a lived-in, free-spirited space: natural, layered and warm.
skills.summary: Earth tones, hand-drawn florals, macramé and woven patterns, arched shapes, warm photography and relaxed script type. It shows a free-spirited, natural and craft-based taste.

pack.why: A soft, rounded family with a two-tone fill that suits warm, crafted layouts.

ground.why: Bohemian pages sit on warm hand-made paper with soft washes of dyed colour.

skills.name: Clickbait Thumbnail
skills.thesis: The still has one second to ask a question: show one clear shock, one object and 3 words, and make it readable at the size of a thumb.
skills.summary: A small still that must win a click at 168px wide. It has a huge face with an open mouth, a red arrow or circle, bright colours and 1 to 3 words in a thick outline.

pack.why: A heavy, solid family matches the thick arrows and circles of a thumbnail.

ground.why: The ground is a burst of rays behind the face, the oldest way to pull the eye to one point.

use_cases: ad creatives that need a fast hook

skills.name: Flat Design
skills.thesis: A digital interface is honest when it shows itself as pixels and type, and does not imitate physical objects.
skills.summary: Interfaces of solid colour fields, simple geometric shapes, bold sans-serif type and no gradients or shadows. It followed Microsoft Metro in 2010 and Windows 8 in 2012, and became the default after iOS 7 in 2013.

pack.why: Solid glyphs with no depth and no detail: the form alone carries the meaning.

ground.why: Flat design uses solid blocks of colour; the long hard shadow gives depth with no gradient.

skills.name: Minimalism Web
skills.thesis: Remove until only the need is left: space and restraint carry the message.
skills.summary: A page with one idea per screen: few elements, much space, one type family and one accent. Every part must earn its place; what stays is clear, calm and fast.

pack.why: A thin, neutral outline family that stays quiet next to plain type.

ground.why: Minimalism keeps the field almost empty: a faint dot grid and one small light of colour.

use_cases: fintech and tools that need trust

skills.name: Tumblr Soft Grunge
skills.thesis: A feed of reblogged scraps that feels like a teenager's wall: faded, tender and a little broken.
skills.summary: A pale, moody photo look from reblog blogs: faded pastel on a dark ground, film grain, light leaks, torn paper edges and small typewriter captions. It is sad and soft, not loud.

pack.why: A hand-drawn line family that matches doodled stars and hearts on a dark wall.

ground.why: The ground is a photocopied scrap wall: grain and uneven ink behind the photos.

skills.name: Vaporwave
skills.thesis: Nostalgia for a future that did not happen: use the dead gloss of 1990s corporate culture to question it.
skills.summary: Pink and cyan gradients, Greek busts, palm trees, Japanese text, 1990s desktop windows and a sunset grid. It came from online music scenes around 2011 and looks at 1980s and 1990s consumer dreams with irony.

pack.why: A pixel family from the era of the first desktop windows, with square terminals.

ground.why: Vaporwave stands on a grid floor that runs to a striped sunset on the horizon.

skills.name: Cyberpunk Web
skills.thesis: The future is crowded, dirty and bright: neon on dark, data everywhere.
skills.summary: A wet, neon city at night: dark ground, magenta, cyan and yellow signs, glitch, scan lines, grime, dense HUD panels and kanji or code on every edge. High tech with low life.

pack.why: A sharp, pixel-edged family that suits chamfered panels and HUD marks.

ground.why: Cyberpunk takes the neon grid floor and the city sky from eighties film posters.

skills.name: Health Goth
skills.thesis: Treat the body and the interface as one clean, dark machine: goth mood, gym function, no decoration that has no use.
skills.summary: Black, white and silver, 3D-rendered blades and mesh forms, sportswear and gym signs, with a cold, clean look. It grew from a 2013 online group that mixed goth, sport and net art.

pack.why: A sharp, grid-based enterprise icon set suits the cold, technical, sport-label look.

ground.why: Health goth sits on a black field with a fine grille, like a gym floor or a ventilation panel.

use_cases: fitness and wellness brands with a dark tone

skills.name: Normcore
skills.thesis: Choose sameness over difference: a look that blends in is a calm answer to a feed that rewards standing out.
skills.summary: Plain, unbranded clothes and plain pages: grey fleece, white trainers, dad jeans, default fonts and flat daylight snapshots. A trend report named it in 2013, and a magazine story spread it.

pack.why: A thin, neutral outline family that looks like a default system set.

ground.why: A normcore page shows no ground at all: a flat light grey, the colour of a plain fleece.

skills.name: Synthwave Web
skills.thesis: The 1980s as a dream: neon, chrome and a road to the horizon.
skills.summary: A neon sunset, a perspective grid, chrome type, pink and cyan on deep violet, and scanlines. It recalls the 1980s as film and games sold it, and it feels like a night drive.

pack.why: A smooth 2px line that takes a neon glow well.

ground.why: Synthwave is the outrun horizon: a striped sun over a neon grid that runs to the edge.

skills.name: VSCO Preset Look
skills.thesis: A preset, not a filter: the edit imitates a real film stock and must look as if no edit happened.
skills.summary: A quiet photo grade that copies film stock: matte blacks, soft contrast, muted greens and warm skin. A preset code such as A6 or HB2 sets it, and the app chrome stays pale and spare.

pack.why: A thin, quiet line family that suits sliders and tool icons on a pale editor screen.

ground.why: The ground is soft, even light: a flat matte field with no pattern.

skills.name: Brutalist Web (2014)
skills.thesis: A page is a document, not a product: show the raw structure and the web serves the reader without decoration.
skills.summary: Browser-default type, blue underlined links, grey or white ground, no polish and visible structure. It came from the 2014 Brutalist Websites collection and answers the smooth, templated web.

pack.why: A thin square line with butt terminals; the thinnest family that still reads as a plain pictogram.

ground.why: Brutalist pages show their structure: a default blue rule and a plain ruler at the edge.

skills.name: Flat Lay Feed
skills.thesis: A life laid flat on a table: choose objects, set them in order and shoot straight down so that the story reads like a diagram.
skills.summary: Objects arranged on a flat surface and shot from straight above: coffee, a notebook, flowers, a phone. Marble or linen fills the ground, light is soft, and props sit in neat clusters with empty space.

pack.why: A fine, even line family that suits quiet captions and tag rows on pale photos.

ground.why: The ground is the table: a pale linen or marble surface seen from above.

skills.name: Luxury Typography Web
skills.thesis: Luxury is restraint and craft: fine type, wide space and few words.
skills.summary: Large, high-contrast serif type on a calm ground, wide tracking on small caps, thin rules and few words. The letter is the main image, and space signals price and care.

pack.why: A thin outline family that matches hairline rules and fine serifs.

ground.why: Luxury print sits inside a hairline frame on heavy cream stock.

skills.name: Material Design
skills.thesis: Digital surfaces behave like sheets of paper with thickness and shadow, so that depth and motion explain the hierarchy of the interface.
skills.summary: A system of flat coloured surfaces that sit at defined elevations and cast shadows from a top-left key light, with bold colour, an 8dp grid and purposeful motion. Google announced it at I/O in June 2014.

pack.why: The filled system set of the style itself, on its 24dp grid.

ground.why: Material surfaces float above a quiet keyline grid lit from the top.

skills.name: Starter pack
skills.thesis: Describe a type of person as a kit of things you can buy, wear and say.
skills.summary: A white grid collage that lists the objects, clothes and habits of one type of person around a cut-out figure. It grew from Tumblr and Twitter in 2014 and became a general template for identity jokes.

pack.why: A solid object family that reads as a catalogue of small products.

ground.why: Evenly sized blocks echo the cells of a catalogue grid.

skills.name: Video Essay
skills.thesis: Treat the frame as a page of an essay: one claim, one piece of evidence, and a quiet layout that lets the argument lead.
skills.summary: A voice reads an argument over film clips, stills, quotes and maps. Clean type, a steady grid, slow zooms and a muted grade give the frame the calm of a printed essay.

pack.why: A thin outline family stays out of the way of quotes and clips.

ground.why: The ground is a dark page with thin rules, like the margin of a printed essay.

skills.name: Blob World
skills.thesis: Make the screen a toy world: soft, over-lit 3D bodies with odd textures carry the brand, and the interface stays plain around them.
skills.summary: Motion design and illustration made from strange 3D renders: soft blobs, surreal rooms, clay, fur, jelly and inflatable textures, sometimes uncanny. It is an illustration world, not a component style: glassmorphism and 3D UI style the controls; Blob World fills the picture.

pack.why: Soft, filled forms with round terminals match the volume of the renders.

ground.why: Blob world places soft round masses of colour behind the content.

skills.name: Conceptual Sketch UI
skills.thesis: The page shows thinking: a rough line says the idea is open and honest.
skills.summary: Pencil and ink lines, rough outlines, margin notes, arrows and annotations on a pale ground. It shows an idea before it is finished, and feels like a designer's notebook.

pack.why: A hand-drawn line family with a slight wobble that matches pencil lines.

ground.why: A sketch page is drawn on grid paper, with one marker stroke of colour.

skills.name: DeepDream Psychedelia
skills.thesis: A machine that looks for patterns finds them in everything: the picture shows what the network expects to see, and it shows it everywhere.
skills.summary: Photographs that a neural network fills with eyes, dog faces, pagodas and swirled fur at every scale. It started in 2015 when Google released the code that made the effect.

pack.why: A duotone family that keeps the caption icons light on a very busy image.

ground.why: The ground repeats the spiral fur and the wave fields that DeepDream grows from a photograph.

use_cases: explainers about how neural networks see

skills.name: Discord Server
skills.thesis: A community lives in a room that is always open, and the talk flows in real time instead of in threads.
skills.summary: A dark chat app for a community: a rail of round server icons, a list of text and voice channels, a stream of messages in time order with avatars, and emoji reactions under each message.

pack.why: Rounded filled icons match the channel and voice icons of the app.

ground.why: A soft dark ground in steps of grey, with no texture.

use_cases: community hubs for games and creators
chat tools for teams and classes

skills.name: Tweet screenshot meme
skills.thesis: Use the plain look of a social post as a frame, so that the text reads as a real voice.
skills.summary: A cropped screenshot of a short social post in its own interface: avatar, name, text and a row of counters. The joke lives in the words, and the crop and the interface give it proof and tone.

pack.why: A neutral outline family that matches interface counters.

ground.why: Thin rules between cards echo the feed list.

skills.name: Wabi-Sabi Web
skills.thesis: Imperfection is beauty: a worn, quiet surface shows time and honest craft.
skills.summary: Muted earth tones, rough textures, uneven edges, much quiet space and small, calm type. It finds beauty in what is imperfect, old and incomplete, and it is the slow side of minimal design.

pack.why: A fine, calm line that adds little weight to a quiet page.

ground.why: Wabi-sabi prefers the uneven grain of washi and clay to a clean surface.

skills.name: Anti-Design
skills.thesis: Polish is a lie: a page that breaks the rules on purpose shows that people made it.
skills.summary: Broken grids, clashing type, overlap, odd colour and deliberate roughness. It answers the polish of templated product sites and asks the visitor to notice the design.

pack.why: A loud, thick, slightly rough line that suits cut-out and sticker art.

ground.why: Anti-design stacks loud blocks off the grid with hard offset shadows.

skills.name: Cohesive Feed Grid
skills.thesis: The grid is the product: each photo serves the profile page, so tone, colour and spacing repeat until the feed reads as one brand.
skills.summary: A profile planned as one board: a 3-column grid of square photos with one preset, one palette and a fixed rhythm of image types. The viewer reads the whole grid before one photo.

pack.why: A clean linear family that fits a plain profile header and grid tabs.

ground.why: The ground is the tile grid: equal squares with thin gaps, as on a profile page.

skills.name: Dark-Mode Developer Tool
skills.thesis: A tool for experts is a dense, calm, dark instrument: show a lot, keep it quiet and make everything reachable from the keyboard.
skills.summary: Near-black surfaces, 1px hairline borders, one saturated accent, a monospace for data and keyboard hints on every action. It came from code editors and terminals and now defines software for engineers.

pack.why: A thin, even 1.5px line at 16px that sits beside 13px text without weight.

ground.why: Developer tools sit on a dark canvas with a dot grid and a glow of the brand colour.

skills.name: Lip-Sync Dance Short
skills.thesis: One person, one song hook and one move: the clip works when the body and the beat are the only content.
skills.summary: A vertical clip of one person who mimes a song or does a short dance in front of a phone, with a rotating record disc and a lyric line. It grew from the Musical.ly app in 2014 and moved to TikTok in 2016 and 2018.

pack.why: A filled, rounded icon family that matches the heart and share icons of a short-video rail.

ground.why: The ground is a dark frame with confetti-like colour flecks that echo the beat pulses of the dance clips.

skills.name: Surreal meme
skills.thesis: Drop the joke structure: let a strange picture and a calm caption make a mood with no answer.
skills.summary: An image with an odd crop, a strange cut-out or a calm, odd caption that has no clear punch line. It grew from Facebook groups and Reddit in 2016 and often breaks the old image-macro rules on purpose.

pack.why: A duotone family that gives a soft, slightly odd tone.

ground.why: Soft orbs give a calm odd glow behind a cut-out.

skills.name: Surrealism Web
skills.thesis: Put the impossible on a quiet page: strange images, clear controls.
skills.summary: Impossible scenes with plain, calm rendering: floating objects, odd scale, melting forms, clouds in rooms and shadows that disagree. Logic bends while the interface stays usable.

pack.why: A friendly outline family that stays plain over strange scenes.

ground.why: Surrealist painting puts calm clouds in a clear sky over a flat horizon.

skills.name: VTuber Avatar
skills.thesis: The host is a character: a tracked avatar gives a person a face that is safe, stable and designed, and the frame is dressed to match.
skills.summary: A drawn anime-style character takes the place of the host. A face tracker moves the eyes, mouth and head in real time. Pastel panels, sparkle and cute rounded frames hold the scene.

pack.why: A soft, solid family with round terminals suits the cute panels and the sparkle marks.

ground.why: The ground is a pastel sky of soft bubbles, the room of a virtual character.

skills.name: 3D Avatar Emoji
skills.thesis: The emoji copies the face of the sender: a mask with a voice, not a fixed picture.
skills.summary: A rendered 3D head, an animal or a user cartoon, that copies the face of the user in real time. Apple showed Animoji with the iPhone X in 2017, and Memoji followed in 2018.

pack.why: A duotone family gives each glyph a soft second tone like the rendered heads.

ground.why: A rendered head floats in a soft lit space, so the ground shows blurred, lit spheres.

use_cases: friendly onboarding with a talking mascot

skills.name: Corporate Memphis
skills.thesis: Friendly, abstract people with unreal bodies make a corporate product feel human and inclusive without the risk of a specific face.
skills.summary: Flat vector illustrations of people with oversized limbs and tiny heads, drawn in a bright palette of 4 to 6 hues with no outlines. Facebook's Alegria system set it in 2017, and many software firms copied it.

pack.why: A friendly round line with one flat tint: the same two-tone logic as the illustrations.

ground.why: Corporate Memphis decorates the page with small floating shapes in friendly colours.

skills.name: Deep-fried meme
skills.thesis: Show the damage as the joke: a picture so copied and boosted that its own decay is the style.
skills.summary: A meme picture pushed through many rounds of saving, sharpening and colour boost until it shows heavy JPEG blocks, burnt reds and yellows, lens flares and glowing emoji. It spread on Reddit and Tumblr in 2017.

pack.why: A solid, bold family that matches chunky emoji-like marks.

ground.why: The ground is a raw, burnt picture with JPEG blocks.

skills.name: Deepfake Face Swap
skills.thesis: The face in the frame is a layer, and the layer shows its seam: the style marks where a real image ends and a made image starts.
skills.summary: Video in which a face region is replaced by a generated one, with a soft blend seam and a check overlay of landmark dots. The form spread after 2017 through open code and phone apps.

pack.why: A thin line family that matches analysis tools and keeps the face visible.

ground.why: The ground is a plain tool panel: the footage is the content and the panel adds only marks.

skills.name: Label meme
skills.thesis: Let a famous picture act as a diagram: the labels give the roles, and the pose gives the joke.
skills.summary: A known photo or still where each person or object carries a small text label that gives it a role. The reader maps the roles and finds the joke. The form took off in 2017 with stock photos and cartoon stills.

pack.why: A neutral outline family for the small arrows and pointers.

ground.why: The ground is the raw photograph; labels sit on it.

skills.name: Terminal / TUI Web
skills.thesis: The terminal is the honest interface: a fixed character grid, text only and a keyboard make a tool fast and trustworthy.
skills.summary: A monospace grid, box-drawing borders, a dark or phosphor ground and keyboard hints. It borrows from command-line tools and text user interfaces to make web pages that feel like a terminal.

pack.why: A pixel family made on a strict square grid that fits a character-cell page.

ground.why: A terminal is a phosphor screen: scan lines, a green glow and a dark bezel.

skills.name: Aurora Gradient UI
skills.thesis: Colour is atmosphere: a blurred field of light makes a product feel alive without any picture of it.
skills.summary: Soft, blurred mesh gradients in 3 to 5 hues behind clean sans-serif type, with glowing edges and grain. It came from fintech and AI product pages and replaced the flat hero.

pack.why: A thin, round line that stays light on a glowing, blurred ground.

ground.why: Aurora interfaces put large soft lights of colour on a near-black sky.

skills.name: Cottagecore
skills.thesis: Pick the slow, handmade country day as a refuge from the feed that carries it.
skills.summary: A dream of rural life: wildflowers, baking, linen, embroidery, hand-drawn herbs and soft window light. It grew on Tumblr in 2018 and reached a wide audience on TikTok in 2020.

pack.why: A hand-drawn print line that suits a handmade country look.

ground.why: Cottagecore sits on cream linen and paper, the cloth of a country table.

skills.name: Duet Split-Screen
skills.thesis: The frame is a conversation: one original clip, one answer, both visible at the same time.
skills.summary: Two video panels side by side in one vertical frame: the source clip on one half and a new reaction or performance on the other. TikTok added the Duet tool in 2018.

pack.why: A filled rounded family that fits the toolbar icons of a short-video app.

ground.why: The ground is two flat blocks that echo the two panels of the frame.

skills.name: GAN Portrait
skills.thesis: A face that nobody owns: the model averages thousands of faces into one believable head, and its faults are the signature.
skills.summary: A square headshot of a person who does not exist: the eyes sit at a fixed height, the background is a soft swirl, and small faults show in teeth, ears and glasses. It spread from 2018 with StyleGAN.

pack.why: A quiet 1.5px line that keeps the faces as the only content.

ground.why: The ground copies the soft, diffuse backdrop that the model draws behind each face.

use_cases: design tools that need anonymous faces

skills.name: Scrapbook UI
skills.thesis: The page is a handmade album: warm, imperfect and made by a person.
skills.summary: Cut-out photos, tape, stickers, torn paper, handwritten notes and slight tilts on a paper ground. It makes a page feel like a handmade album and a personal object.

pack.why: A hand-drawn, sticker-like family with a thick round line.

ground.why: A scrapbook page has tape, cut paper and the grain of copied pictures.

skills.name: Dark academia
skills.thesis: Treat study as a dark, romantic rite: books, old stone and candlelight make the learned life feel fated.
skills.summary: Old libraries, candlelight, tweed, leather books, Latin and brown-green gloom in a romantic dream of a classical college. It spread on Tumblr and TikTok after 2019 and takes much from The Secret History.

pack.why: A fine linear set whose thin strokes sit well beside serif type and engravings.

ground.why: Dark academia stands on a dark, paper-like ground, the page of an old book in low light.

skills.name: Dreamcore
skills.thesis: Show a memory as a dream does: soft, glowing and slightly wrong, with the details out of focus.
skills.summary: Soft, hazy images of childhood rooms, pastel skies, old toys and stairways, with a faint glow and blurry text. It looks like a half-remembered dream and grew on Tumblr, Reddit and video sites.

pack.why: Thin, rounded line icons match the light, soft look of a dream image.

ground.why: Dreamcore sits in soft light with no hard edge, so the ground is a haze of overlapping soft gradients.

use_cases: wellness and sleep apps with a soft tone

skills.name: Glitchcore
skills.thesis: Overload the signal: show the fault, the repeat and the flash until the error becomes the style.
skills.summary: Fast, crowded edits with split colour channels, repeated frames, datamosh, bright flash and old web clutter. It grew with the digicore music scene on SoundCloud, Discord and short-video apps.

pack.why: Pixel icons match the bitmap stickers and old window frames of a glitch edit.

ground.why: Glitchcore shows a broken screen, so the ground is a scan-line field with noise.

skills.name: Get Ready With Me
skills.thesis: Share a real routine in real time: the talk matters more than the result.
skills.summary: A creator talks to a close phone camera while she or he does make-up or picks an outfit, with soft light, a mirror, jump cuts and a line of captions. The form grew from YouTube make-up tutorials of the 2000s.

pack.why: A thin outline family that suits a soft, personal feed.

ground.why: The ground is a soft warm wash that echoes window light in a bedroom.

skills.name: Hyperpop Visual
skills.thesis: Make pop too sweet and too bright: take cute and chrome so far that they look artificial and strange.
skills.summary: Shiny chrome, candy colours, cute 3D shapes, Web 2.0 gloss and crowded collage, with pixel type and stickers. It links the PC Music look to a 2019 playlist and to short-video culture.

pack.why: Filled, round icons suit the candy, sticker-like forms of the style.

ground.why: Hyperpop scatters stickers and sparks over a pastel ground, so the ground is confetti.

use_cases: fashion and beauty drops for young buyers

skills.name: Kidcore
skills.thesis: Treat the childhood bedroom of the 1990s as a design system: bright, crowded and joyful on purpose.
skills.summary: Primary colours, rainbows, stickers, toys, cartoon animals and 1990s kid-show graphics, stacked in dense collage. It uses the childhood of the 1980s and 1990s as a happy, loud look.

pack.why: A fat, rounded fill family that matches sticker shapes.

ground.why: Kidcore stands on scattered confetti, like the floor of a party or a toy box.

skills.name: Liminal spaces
skills.thesis: An ordinary place with no people and no purpose feels strange: the viewer meets the unease of a threshold.
skills.summary: Empty rooms of transit and routine: office corridors, pools, car parks and malls under flat light, with no people. A 2019 image of yellow rooms started the look, and the Backrooms spread it.

pack.why: A plain technical outline family that looks like signage and system icons.

ground.why: Liminal spaces stand on a grid of ceiling and floor tiles that runs toward one vanishing point.

skills.name: Neumorphism
skills.thesis: An interface can be tactile without imitating objects, if every control is moulded from the same material as the page behind it.
skills.summary: Monochrome surfaces that look extruded from or pressed into the background, made with a light shadow and a dark shadow on opposite corners. It appeared on Dribbble in late 2019 as a soft answer to flat design.

pack.why: A thin round line that does not compete with the soft relief of the surface.

ground.why: Neumorphism lifts one soft disc out of the same material as the page.

skills.name: Cybercore Web
skills.thesis: The page is a machine interface: sharp, labelled, cold and dense with data.
skills.summary: Black grounds, acid-green or cyan accents, chrome, angular cuts, HUD frames, small caps data labels and glitch. It mixes 1990s cyber fiction with techwear, and it feels like a machine interface.

pack.why: A technical, square-cap line family that matches clipped panels and HUD labels.

ground.why: Cybercore renders a wireframe floor that runs to a hard sun on the horizon.

skills.name: Glassmorphism
skills.thesis: Layers are readable when each one is a pane of frosted glass: it shows what lies beneath it and still keeps its own plane.
skills.summary: Translucent panels that blur the colourful shapes behind them, edged with a thin light border. It spread after macOS Big Sur in 2020 and revives the glass of Frutiger Aero with real backdrop blur.

pack.why: A light round line that stays legible on a blurred, bright surface.

ground.why: Frosted glass needs bright orbs of colour behind it, or the blur has nothing to show.

skills.name: Goblincore
skills.thesis: Find beauty in mud, rot and clutter: the untidy forest floor is a better home than a clean showroom.
skills.summary: A look for the small wild and the overlooked: moss, mushrooms, frogs, snail shells, bones, soil, old jars and crumpled earth-tone clothes. It spread on Tumblr and TikTok after 2019.

pack.why: A rough, hand-printed line that fits finds, field notes and torn paper.

ground.why: Goblincore stands on a grainy, dirty ground like soil, a photocopied field note or a damp page.

skills.name: Green-Screen Short
skills.thesis: Put the speaker in front of the evidence: the image is the set, the creator is the commentator.
skills.summary: A person stands in front of a screenshot, a map or a photo that fills the whole vertical frame, and talks about it. The creator cuts out the background with the chroma-key tool of a short-video app.

pack.why: A clean outline family with pointer and arrow shapes.

ground.why: The ground is a raw, flat plate, like a screenshot that fills the frame.

skills.name: Neo-Brutalism UI
skills.thesis: An interface earns trust by showing its structure openly and being loud about it, because every border and shadow is a stated fact.
skills.summary: Flat, loud colour fields with thick black borders and hard, unblurred offset shadows. It grew from product sites such as Gumroad and from Figma community kits as a deliberate reply to corporate softness.

pack.why: A heavy line with a blunt weight that matches the thick borders.

ground.why: Neo-brutalism uses flat colour blocks with a thick border and a hard black shadow.

skills.name: Photo Dump
skills.thesis: The opposite of the curated grid: show the camera roll as it is, so that the poster looks relaxed and real.
skills.summary: A carousel of 6 to 20 casual photos in one post: blurred, flash-lit, off-centre, with a screenshot, a meal and a mirror selfie in a row. It looks careless on purpose.

pack.why: A soft, solid family that matches the round buttons of a phone carousel.

ground.why: The ground is a stack of mixed-size blocks: images of different ratios side by side.

use_cases: brand posts that need a human voice

skills.name: POV Short
skills.thesis: Make the viewer the second person in the scene: the caption names the situation, the lens is the viewer.
skills.summary: A short clip that shows a scene as if the viewer is a character: the camera is the viewer's eyes and the actor talks straight to the lens. A text line that starts with "POV:" sets the scene.

pack.why: A filled, neutral family that looks like the default app rail.

ground.why: The ground is a raw, flat dark room that holds the frame of a phone video.

skills.name: Velocity Edit
skills.thesis: Let time bend to the music: slow on the strong beat, fast on the rest.
skills.summary: A short vertical montage with speed ramps: the clip slows to slow motion, then jumps to fast play on the beat, with glow, zoom shake and a colour grade. Editors make it with the velocity tool of CapCut.

pack.why: A bold family with heavy shapes that fit a high-contrast edit.

ground.why: The ground is a ray burst that echoes the light flares of the edit.

skills.name: Weirdcore
skills.thesis: Make a familiar thing wrong in one small way, and let the poor image quality carry the unease.
skills.summary: Low-quality photos of empty places, red warning text, black voids, faceless shapes and old 3D or web fragments. The mood is a strange dream memory. It grew on Tumblr, Reddit and Twitter.

pack.why: Pixel icons match the low-resolution, old-computer fragments of the style.

ground.why: Weirdcore uses raw, degraded images, so the ground is a flat field with visible noise and no polish.

skills.name: Word Caption Clip
skills.thesis: Make every word visible at the moment it is spoken: the caption is the main picture, and the viewer reads and hears the same beat.
skills.summary: A talking head in a vertical frame, with the speech shown as huge captions, one to three words at a time. Each word pops in at the beat, and the current word takes a bright colour.

pack.why: A heavy, solid family matches the thick caption letters and the emoji accents.

ground.why: The ground is raw footage with no decoration, since the words are the only design layer.

skills.name: Claymorphism
skills.thesis: The interface is a toy: soft, inflated forms with colour make the screen friendly and touchable.
skills.summary: Puffy, rounded 3D shapes in soft pastel colour with double inner shadows and a soft outer shadow, like modelling clay. It followed neumorphism and flat illustration and turns the interface into toys.

pack.why: A bold, round, filled family that looks inflated, like clay, inside a pastel disc.

ground.why: Clay surfaces are soft puffed shapes in pastel colour with a deep soft shadow.

use_cases: consumer wellness and finance for young users

skills.name: Editorial Serif Revival
skills.thesis: Voice beats neutrality: a serif with character makes a brand sound like a person, as in a magazine.
skills.summary: Large expressive serif headlines, warm off-white paper, a small sans for labels and a restrained palette. It came back as a reaction to the geometric sans-serif default of the SaaS web.

pack.why: A thin, even, humanist line that does not compete with the serif headlines.

ground.why: Editorial pages are set on a column grid with a rule of ink across the masthead.

skills.name: Ethereal Web
skills.thesis: Lightness is luxury: haze, glow and space make a quiet, weightless world.
skills.summary: Pale, glowing pastels, soft focus, thin serif or light sans type, translucent layers and air. It aims at a calm, dreamlike, weightless mood and reads as light rather than as object.

pack.why: A thin, round line that stays quiet on a pale, soft ground.

ground.why: Ethereal pages sit in a pale haze of soft light in pastel colour.

skills.name: AI Avatar Portrait
skills.thesis: One face, many costumes: the pack turns a selfie into a character sheet, and the glow is the reward.
skills.summary: A set of 20 stylised portraits of one face in many looks: fantasy, anime, space and painting. Phone apps made the form common at the end of 2022.

pack.why: Filled icons in circles match the round, friendly app look of an avatar pack.

ground.why: Soft glow orbs echo the radial light that sits behind each head in an avatar tile.

use_cases: photo app marketing and store pages
social posts that show a pack

skills.name: AI Chat Interface
skills.thesis: The interface is a conversation: one box to speak into, and everything else appears in the reply.
skills.summary: A single centred column, one large input at the bottom, streaming text, suggestion chips and almost no chrome. It came with ChatGPT in 2022 and makes language the main control.

pack.why: A thin, neutral 1.5px line at 16px to 20px that stays quiet next to running text.

ground.why: Chat interfaces keep a calm field with one warm light at the top.

skills.name: Barbiecore
skills.thesis: Make the whole world one pink, and play with it: toy gloss and total colour turn a doll into a dress code.
skills.summary: One hot pink on everything: pink dresses, pink plastic, pink houses and glossy toy shine. Photos of a Barbie film set in 2022 started the trend, and a pink season in fashion followed.

pack.why: A filled, rounded family that matches glossy toy shapes.

ground.why: Barbiecore stands on glossy bubbles and sparkles, the shine of moulded pink plastic.

skills.name: Bento Grid UI
skills.thesis: A page is easiest to scan when every idea sits in its own compartment and the compartments tile one tight, regular grid.
skills.summary: A rectangular grid of rounded cells of mixed spans, each holding one idea, with equal small gaps between them. Apple feature pages made it the default product layout from 2022.

pack.why: A plain round line at one weight: quiet in a cell, the default of current product interfaces.

ground.why: Bento layouts sit on a quiet grid, and the cells give all the structure.

skills.name: Clean girl
skills.thesis: Show effortless order: a polished, neutral surface suggests a calm life, and the routine is the product.
skills.summary: A look of dewy skin, a sleek bun, gold hoops, neutral clothes, white tiles and tidy shelves. It grew on TikTok and Instagram in 2021 and 2022 and sells wellness, skin and routine.

pack.why: A very thin line set that matches the soft, light feel of the look.

ground.why: The clean girl look stands on a soft, near-white ground with a faint warm glow, like a bathroom in morning light.

skills.name: Diffusion Gloss
skills.thesis: Everything is lit, sharp and finished: the model gives each surface the same expensive sheen, and the sheen is the style.
skills.summary: A smooth, over-detailed image with a perfect rim light, a teal and amber grade and a soft bokeh ground. It became the default look of text-to-image models from 2022.

pack.why: Filled icons in circles sit well over a dark gradient scrim and a glossy image.

ground.why: The ground is a soft teal and amber glow, like the haze and the rim light of the rendered images.

use_cases: AI product pages and model demos

skills.name: Dual Camera Snapshot
skills.thesis: Proof of a real moment: two cameras fire at once, there is no edit, and the late mark shows that the poster did not stage it.
skills.summary: One post made of two photos from one moment: the back camera fills the frame and the front camera sits in a small inset. A time stamp and a late mark show that it was not planned.

pack.why: A solid, bold family that reads well on a black camera screen.

ground.why: The ground is a plain black field: a camera viewfinder with nothing behind the photo.

skills.name: Mini-Diffusion Meme
skills.thesis: The joke is the gap between a plain prompt and a soft, wrong picture; the smudge is the format.
skills.summary: A 3x3 grid of small, smudged images that answer a silly text prompt, with warped faces and soft shapes. It went viral in 2022 from a free, low-resolution image model.

pack.why: A square, pixel family suits the blocky, low-resolution output of the format.

ground.why: The ground is a plain cream page, like a simple web form that holds a prompt box.

use_cases: posts about early AI image tools

skills.name: Photo Carousel Slideshow
skills.thesis: Slow the feed down: one idea on each still slide, one swipe at a time.
skills.summary: A set of 4 to 10 still images that the viewer swipes, with one line of text on each slide and a hook on the first slide. Instagram added carousels in 2017, and TikTok added photo mode in 2022.

pack.why: A thin, neutral outline family for save, share and arrow icons.

ground.why: The ground is plain paper, like a printed card in a stack.

skills.name: Spatial UI (visionOS)
skills.thesis: An interface in space should be a physical presence in the room, so it uses glass that takes light from the real scene and respects the person's field of view.
skills.summary: Translucent glass windows that float in the user's room at a set distance, lit by the surrounding scene and controlled by eye gaze and hand pinch. Apple introduced it with Vision Pro in 2023.

pack.why: Thin, round system glyphs in the platform manner, made for a round glass container.

ground.why: Spatial interfaces float glass panels in front of a soft, lit room.

use_cases: web marketing pages for spatial devices

skills.name: AI Slop
skills.thesis: The image exists to fill a feed: it has a high finish, no author and no point, and its small errors show the lack of care.
skills.summary: Mass-made generated images in social feeds: a plastic gloss, a generic subject, warped hands, false text and a bait caption. The word slop for such content spread in 2024.

pack.why: A common thin line set that matches a standard feed card and its reaction row.

ground.why: A soft light feed with one warm glow stands for the plain, even field around a glossy image.

use_cases: examples in articles about feed quality

skills.name: Liquid Glass
skills.thesis: Controls are a transparent lens above the content: the interface floats, refracts the page and stays out of the way.
skills.summary: Clear, curved glass that bends the content behind it, with specular edges, tint that adapts to the ground and floating controls. Apple introduced it in 2025 and it goes beyond frosted glass.

pack.why: An iOS-style family with round forms and a medium weight that matches a system sans on glass.

ground.why: Liquid glass bends the colour behind it, so the ground holds bright shapes for the lens.

skills.name: Gothic
skills.thesis: A building is a stone skeleton that lifts the eye to heaven: the thrust of each vault is caught by a buttress, so that walls can dissolve into light.
skills.summary: Pointed arches, ribbed vaults and flying buttresses turn the stone wall into a skeleton, and the freed walls become coloured glass. Chartres, Reims and Amiens set the height record that every later cathedral tried to beat.

storey_height.note: A nave rises 25 to 45m; the domain stops at 8m per storey.

glazing_ratio.note: The nave wall is mostly glass; the west front is mostly stone.

skills.name: Renaissance
skills.thesis: Beauty is number: a building is right when each part is a simple ratio of the whole, as in the human body and in music.
skills.summary: The Roman orders, the round arch and the dome return, set by number. Brunelleschi, Alberti and Palladio made proportion into a rule: each part is a simple fraction of the whole, and the building is a calm, symmetric order.

skills.name: Baroque
skills.thesis: Architecture should move the viewer: curve, depth, light and ornament make one dramatic effect, in the service of church and crown.
skills.summary: Classical orders bent into curves: oval plans, convex and concave fronts, doubled columns and light that drops from hidden windows. Bernini, Borromini and the court architects built it as theatre to move the viewer.

roof_pitch.note: The range covers a dome on a drum and a mansard roof.

skills.name: Neoclassicism
skills.thesis: Architecture should be reasoned: build from the first principles of the Greek temple, and let the plain wall and a true order carry the dignity of the state.
skills.summary: A clear, pure classicism drawn from Greek and Roman ruins: a temple front, plain wall surfaces and a strong cube. It answered the excess of the Baroque with reason, and gave the new states their museums, parliaments and banks.

skills.name: Arts and Crafts
skills.thesis: A building should be made by skilled hands from local material, planned for the life inside it, and its construction should be seen and enjoyed.
skills.summary: Houses built by honest craft from local brick, oak and tile. Webb, Voysey and Baillie Scott planned from the inside out and let steep roofs, deep porches and hand work show how the house was made.

skills.name: Beaux-Arts
skills.thesis: A great building is planned first: the parti is a clear sequence of axes, rooms and routes, and classical ornament and sculpture crown the plan.
skills.summary: A grand classical system taught at the École des Beaux-Arts in Paris: a clear plan on axes, a rich sculpted front with paired columns and a mansard roof. It made the opera house, the station and the city hall into public palaces.

roof_pitch.note: The range covers a low dome and a mansard roof.

skills.name: Art Nouveau
skills.thesis: A building should grow like a plant: structure, ornament and furniture follow one organic line, and iron and glass are shown as the new materials of the age.
skills.summary: Whiplash curves, plant forms and exposed iron on the street front and in the stair hall. Horta in Brussels, Guimard in Paris and Gaudí in Barcelona made the total work of art: one line from the facade to the door handle.

roof_pitch.note: A flat roof is only permitted behind a curved parapet.

skills.name: Prairie School
skills.thesis: A house should belong to its land: low horizontal lines, a free plan around the hearth and honest materials make an American architecture of the prairie.
skills.summary: Long low houses with broad overhanging roofs, ribbon windows and a central hearth. Frank Lloyd Wright and the Chicago architects built for the flat Midwest: the horizontal line rules, and rooms flow into each other.

roof_pitch.note: A pitch of 1:6 to 1:4 is about 9 to 14 degrees.

skills.name: Organic Architecture
skills.thesis: A building should grow from its site and its use as a living form: the whole and the parts belong together, and the plan flows with the land.
skills.summary: A building grows from its site like a plant. Wright, Aalto and Goff set the plan, the structure and the material in one flowing whole that opens to the land, with no fixed façade or box.

skills.name: Expressionist Architecture
skills.thesis: A building should carry an inner feeling in its form: the architect sculpts one dynamic mass, and the plan and the facade follow that gesture.
skills.summary: Buildings shaped as one plastic gesture of feeling. After the First World War, Mendelsohn, Taut, Poelzig and Höger used brick, concrete and glass to make crystals, caves and flowing masses.
use_cases: film set and game environment design

roof_pitch.note: The range covers a stepped crown, a dome and a spire.

skills.name: Bauhaus Architecture
skills.thesis: Form follows use: each function gets its own volume, and the plan is the generator of the building, not the facade.
skills.summary: A functional building of asymmetric wings, each wing sized by its use, joined by bridges and glazed on the work side. Gropius and Meyer taught building as the last step of a workshop education that joined art, craft and industry.

glazing_ratio.note: The glass wing and the dwelling wing have different glazing.

skills.name: Art Deco
skills.thesis: Modern technology deserves luxury: the machine age should look glamorous, symmetric and expensive.
skills.summary: Stepped towers, zigzag and chevron relief, and rich materials in a symmetric frame. It came from the Paris exhibition of 1925 and made the skyscraper and the cinema into the pictures of the machine age.

roof_pitch.note: The crown steps back in tiers; the roofs behind the parapets are flat.

skills.name: International Style
skills.thesis: A building is a volume enclosed by a thin skin, and industrial methods make one rational form valid in every place.
skills.summary: Light rectilinear volumes of steel, glass and white render, with flat roofs, ribbon windows and free plans. The Bauhaus, Le Corbusier and Mies van der Rohe defined it in the 1920s, and it became the global language of the office tower.

glazing_ratio.note: Early white villas have 30 to 40% glass; later curtain walls reach 90%.

skills.name: Nordic Modernism
skills.thesis: Modern architecture should serve the whole person: use natural materials, scarce daylight and a human scale to make function warm.
skills.summary: Modern architecture softened for a cold, dark climate: white plaster and brick, warm timber, daylight shaped with care and plans that bend to the site. Alvar Aalto, Arne Jacobsen and Sigurd Lewerentz made function humane.

skills.name: Mid-century Modern
skills.thesis: Modern architecture can be warm: the free plan and the glass wall serve everyday life, and the house belongs to its garden.
skills.summary: A low house of post-and-beam timber or steel, with glass walls to the garden, a flat or low-pitched roof and a warm palette. It made the International Style domestic and suited it to climate, family and the car.

glazing_ratio.note: The street front is closed; the garden front is open.

skills.name: Googie
skills.thesis: A roadside building must be a sign: it must show a driver at 50 km/h what it sells and why it is new.
skills.summary: The roadside style of the American car age. Coffee shops, motels and car washes got upswept roofs, bright signs and space-age shapes to catch a driver at speed.

skills.name: Brutalism
skills.thesis: A building is honest when its material, its structure and its use are legible from the street.
skills.summary: Heavy masses of board-marked concrete with the structure, the services and the circulation shown on the outside. It grew from Le Corbusier's late work and from British post-war housing, and it built the universities and town halls of the welfare state.

skills.name: Metabolism
skills.thesis: A city lives like an organism, so its long-life cores must stand fixed and its short-life cells must change.
skills.summary: A Japanese style of fixed concrete cores that carry replaceable capsules. Its architects drew the city as a living body that grows, changes and renews its cells.

skills.name: Adaptive Reuse
skills.thesis: An existing building has value in its fabric and its memory, so keep it, change its use and let the new work be clearly new beside the old.
skills.summary: Old buildings given a new use. Scarpa, Aulenti and Herzog and de Meuron keep the shell of a castle, station or power plant, and add a clear new layer that tells old from new.
use_cases: housing and offices from old factories

storey_height.note: Old halls and warehouses keep their tall storeys.

roof_pitch.note: The old roof stays, so the pitch is the pitch of the host building.

skills.name: Postmodernism
skills.thesis: Architecture is communication: a building should carry meaning, memory and irony, and a decorated shed is better than a blank box.
skills.summary: A building that quotes history in a joke and in colour: split pediments, giant keystones, pastel stone and a facade that works as a sign. Venturi, Graves and Johnson used it to answer the blank box of the Modern Movement.

skills.name: Radical architecture
skills.thesis: The drawing is the act: if the real city serves the market, the architect must draw a city that no market can build.
skills.summary: Architecture that lives on paper, in collage and in film. Groups in London, Florence and Moscow drew endless grids, walking cities and impossible houses to attack the market and the state.

skills.name: High-tech
skills.thesis: A building is a machine of parts: structure, services and circulation are tools to see and to change, and open floors let the use change.
skills.summary: A lightweight steel frame, with the services, the bracing and the lifts shown in colour on the outside. Rogers, Piano and Foster made the machine aesthetic of the 1920s into a flexible, kit-of-parts building.

structural_grid.note: Floor spans reach 48m; the domain stops at 30m.

skills.name: Critical Regionalism
skills.thesis: A building should use modern means to answer a specific place: its climate, its materials and its craft give the form, and universal style and nostalgia are both refused.
skills.summary: Modern form rooted in a place. Utzon, Moneo, Bawa, Piano and Zumthor keep the rigour of modernism but take their light, climate, materials and craft from the site, and they refuse both the universal box and the historical joke.

skills.name: Deconstructivism
skills.thesis: The pure form is already flawed: distort the grid, collide the volumes and let the building show that order is unstable.
skills.summary: Skewed, fractured volumes that collide at sharp angles, with a facade that seems to tear itself apart. Gehry, Hadid, Libeskind and Coop Himmelb(l)au used distortion to disturb the pure box of the Modern Movement from inside.

structural_grid.note: The spans have no regular module.

skills.name: Mass Timber
skills.thesis: A building can be made of engineered timber panels and beams, and so store carbon, build fast off site and show the warm grain of its own structure.
skills.summary: Buildings of engineered wood. Cross-laminated and glued timber panels and beams make floors, walls and frames, and tall buildings of 6 to 25 storeys with warm interiors and a low carbon footprint.

skills.name: Parametricism
skills.thesis: A design is a system of linked parameters, so every part can differ and follow the others in a smooth gradient: one fluid field replaces the rigid, repeated element.
skills.summary: Buildings drawn by algorithm: continuous curved skins, smooth transitions and no repeated part. Zaha Hadid Architects and Patrik Schumacher made one flowing field of the façade, roof and floor, built with digital fabrication.

structural_grid.note: Column-free spans reach 90m; the domain stops at 30m.

roof_pitch.note: The roof is part of a curved skin, so the pitch changes along the surface.

skills.name: Georgian
skills.thesis: A room is good when its proportions obey the classical rules and each wall answers the wall opposite it.
skills.summary: The British and colonial room of the four Georges. Walls follow a classical order of dado, field and cornice; a chimneypiece on the centre line, paired doors and sash windows set one axis; mahogany furniture stands against the walls, and the centre of the floor stays clear.

ceiling_height.note: Below about 2.4 m the proportions of the orders fail.

skills.name: Shaker
skills.thesis: A room is beautiful when each object in it is useful, well made and in its place.
skills.summary: The rooms of the United Society of Believers in Christ's Second Appearing in New England, New York and Kentucky. Built-in storage, a peg rail around the walls, light wood furniture and bare floor give a room that is ordered for work and easy to clean.

skills.name: Victorian
skills.thesis: A home shows the taste, the travels and the respectability of its family; more objects and more pattern mean more comfort.
skills.summary: The middle-class room of the industrial century. Machine-made pattern covers walls, floors and furniture; dark, saturated colours, heavy curtains and many objects make a dense, enclosed parlour around the hearth.

skills.name: Arts and Crafts
skills.thesis: A room is honest when every piece is made by hand from local materials and shows how it is made.
skills.summary: The craft reform of the Victorian room. Handmade oak furniture shows its joints, a deep inglenook holds the hearth, and one stylised plant pattern runs on the walls or the textiles; low beams and built-in settles make the room honest and warm.

ceiling_height.note: Beams and a plate shelf keep the room low and close.

skills.name: Art Nouveau
skills.thesis: Nature gives the only true line; one designer must draw every part of a room so that it grows as one plant.
skills.summary: The room as one living organism. Whiplash curves of plant stems run from the furniture into the panelling, the door frames and the light fittings; stained glass, carved fruitwood and bronze make each room a total work of art by one designer.

skills.name: Bauhaus interior
skills.thesis: A room is a machine for daily life, and industry can make each of its parts well and for everyone.
skills.summary: The rooms that the Bauhaus workshops in Weimar and Dessau designed and furnished. Tubular steel, glass, lacquer and woven wool stand in white rooms with one primary-colour wall; each object is a prototype for industry, and the room is a tool for living.

light_temperature.note: Neutral light shows the primary colours true.

skills.name: Art Deco
skills.thesis: Luxury and the machine meet in one bold geometric order of rare materials and high contrast.
skills.summary: The luxury room of the machine age. Symmetric plans, stepped and fan geometry, black lacquer, exotic veneers and polished chrome or brass give high contrast; a mirror or a mural on the axis and cove light in the ceiling make the room a stage.

ceiling_height.note: The stepped cove and the tall mirror need height.

skills.name: Hollywood Regency
skills.thesis: A room is a stage set: bold colour, gloss and symmetry make the people in it look their best.
skills.summary: The decorator's room of the film stars. Regency and neoclassical forms meet lacquer colour, bold stripes and mirror; a symmetric plan around a centre piece, white plaster and gilt make each room ready for a camera.

skills.name: Mid-century modern interior
skills.thesis: The modern home joins the room to the landscape, and good design made in series can be warm as well as rational.
skills.summary: The open-plan post-war home of the United States and Europe. Low teak and moulded-plywood furniture on tapered legs stands in front of a glass wall to the garden; a stone fireplace or the view is the focal point, and a few saturated accents warm a neutral room.

ceiling_height.note: The low horizontal line of the room needs a modest ceiling.

skills.name: Scandinavian interior
skills.thesis: A home for a long dark winter must be bright, warm in material and made of few good things that last.
skills.summary: The bright, light-wood room of Denmark, Sweden, Norway and Finland. White walls and pale floors catch the short northern daylight; solid-wood furniture with visible joints and wool textiles stand in small groups, and many small lamps replace one ceiling light.

skills.name: Industrial loft
skills.thesis: The building tells of its past as a factory; leave the structure and the services in view and live among them.
skills.summary: The converted factory floor. Exposed brick, concrete, steel columns and ducts stay in view; large steel windows light one open plan, and salvaged furniture of wood, leather and steel stands in zones on a bare floor.

ceiling_height.note: A low ceiling loses the factory volume that defines the style.

skills.name: Memphis interior
skills.thesis: Function is not the only meaning of an object; colour, pattern and irony are functions too.
skills.summary: The rooms of the Milan design group around Ettore Sottsass. Furniture is a stack of primary solids in plastic laminate, printed with squiggles and terrazzo chips in clashing colours; each piece stands alone like a sculpture, and no axis or rule of good taste orders the room.

skills.name: Coastal interior
skills.thesis: A house by the sea takes its colours from sand, water and weathered wood, and its comfort from loose, washable fabric.
skills.summary: The airy summer-house room by the sea. White and sand-coloured walls, white-washed or grey-oiled wood, linen slipcovers and woven rope or rattan; one sea blue carries the accents, and the room opens to the water and the light.

skills.name: Minimalist
skills.thesis: Remove every thing that is not necessary, so that space, light and material can be seen.
skills.summary: The room reduced to space, light and surface. White or pale stone walls, one floor material throughout, hidden storage and flush details leave only one or two pieces in view; daylight on a plain wall is the main event.
use_cases: homes of collectors of one object

skills.name: Japandi
skills.thesis: Calm comes from emptiness and from a few natural things made by hand and placed with care.
skills.summary: A blend of the Scandinavian room and the Japanese room. Low, heavy wood furniture in pale and dark tones stands in a warm off-white room with wide empty floor; paper light, linen, stoneware and slatted screens give texture, and the tatami ratio of 1:2 orders the plan.

skills.name: Grandmillennial
