skills.thesis: Comfort and memory beat the cool, empty room: inherited, pretty and patterned things make a home.
skills.summary: A young generation takes back the rooms of its grandparents. Chintz, ruffles, needlepoint, skirted tables, wicker and blue-and-white porcelain return with a fresh, light palette and a sense of humour; pattern meets pattern and inherited pieces meet new ones.

skills.name: Neo-deco
skills.thesis: Deco glamour without the hard edges: curves, ribs and warm metal make luxury feel soft and personal.
skills.summary: Art Deco after a century, made soft. Curved bouclé and velvet seats, fluted wood, arches, ribbed glass and brushed brass keep the geometry and the glamour of the 1920s, but in warm, muted colours and rounded forms.

skills.name: Dopamine decor
skills.thesis: Colour and play in the home lift the mood, and a room must show the joy of the person who lives in it.
skills.summary: A room built for joy after the years at home of 2020 and 2021. Saturated hues drench walls, trim and ceiling; curved, inflated furniture in velvet and bouclé stands on patterned rugs; objects are personal and sorted by colour.

skills.name: Quiet luxury
skills.thesis: Real luxury is the quality of the material and the work, and it does not need to show a name.
skills.summary: A tonal room of costly materials and no logos. One hue family in cream, oatmeal, taupe and chocolate covers walls and seats; texture, not colour, gives the variety; pairs of chairs and lamps mirror about the fireplace, and hidden light washes the plaster.

skills.name: Pictorialism
skills.thesis: A photograph is art when the maker's hand shows in the image, so the print must look made and not recorded.
skills.summary: Photography that borrows the look of drawing and etching. Soft-focus lenses, hand-worked pigment prints and warm toning blur the line between a photograph and a painting, to claim the status of art.

grain.note: The plates were ISO 10 to 25; the domain floor is 25.

focal_length.note: This is the 35 mm equivalent of 305 to 406 mm on 8×10 in.

skills.name: Straight photography
skills.thesis: Photography is an art of its own when it shows the world with the full detail and tonal range that only a camera can record.
skills.summary: A sharp, unmanipulated print of a real thing, made on a large camera at a small aperture. The beauty comes from the medium itself: fine detail, a long tonal scale and exact focus from front to back.

focal_length.note: This is the 35 mm equivalent of 210 to 360 mm on 8×10 in.

aspect_ratio.note: The 8×10 in or 4×5 in negative is the frame.

skills.name: Group f/64
skills.thesis: Pure photography needs no borrowed look from painting; the large camera, the small stop and the full tonal scale are enough.
skills.summary: Sharp, rich black-and-white contact prints of rocks, plants, shells and faces, made on large cameras at the smallest stop. The group named itself after that stop.
use_cases: image prompts for monumental sharp scenes

focal_length.note: This is the 35 mm equivalent of 210 to 300 mm on 8×10 in.

aspect_ratio.note: The 8×10 in contact plate is the frame.

skills.name: New Objectivity photography
skills.thesis: The lens is exact and unsentimental, so the honest picture shows the structure of a thing at close range and in full detail.
skills.summary: Sharp, close, frontal pictures of plants, tools, faces and machines, made in Germany between the wars. The camera sees more than the eye, and it names things without comment.
use_cases: product catalogues with a scientific feel

focal_length.note: This is the 35 mm equivalent of 135 to 210 mm on a 9×12 cm or 13×18 cm plate, used close.

skills.name: Street photography
skills.thesis: Public life holds pictures that nobody can stage, and the photographer's job is to be in the right place and to see them in time.
skills.summary: Unposed pictures of public life, made with a small camera, a wide lens and quick reflexes. The photographer finds the frame and waits for the moment when gesture, light and geometry agree.
use_cases: campaign imagery with a raw feel

grain.note: Use ISO 400 by day; push to 1600 or 3200 at night.

skills.name: Documentary photography
skills.thesis: A photograph can be evidence and an appeal at once, if the maker stays honest about what happened and with whom.
skills.summary: Photographs that bear witness to people, work and events. The maker gets close, earns trust and shows what the sitter needs the viewer to see.
use_cases: image prompts for honest portraits at work

skills.name: New Colour
skills.thesis: Colour is the subject and not a decoration, and the everyday world is rich enough to need no drama.
skills.summary: Colour photography of the plain American scene: a car park, a kitchen, a tricycle. Saturated dye-transfer and slide colour carries the picture, and the composition looks casual and exact at the same time.

grain.note: Kodachrome 25 and 64 and Kodacolor 100 set this band.

skills.name: New Topographics
skills.thesis: The ordinary, man-made landscape deserves the formal care that the sublime wilderness once received, and the photographer's voice should stay out of it.
skills.summary: Flat, neutral, frontal views of suburbs, car parks and industrial sites, with no drama and no opinion. It shows the built landscape as a catalogue of facts, in a cool, exact, almost clerical style.

focal_length.note: This is the 35 mm equivalent of 150 to 210 mm on 4×5 in.

skills.name: Düsseldorf School
skills.thesis: Seen without drama and in great detail, an ordinary place becomes a map of the way we live.
skills.summary: Large, cool, frontal colour pictures of buildings, rooms, crowds and landscapes in fine detail. The method comes from the Bechers' typologies, and the scale comes from the museum wall.
use_cases: annual-report imagery with a cool authority
image prompts for flat, frontal, grid-based scenes

focal_length.note: This is the 35 mm equivalent of 90 to 150 mm on 4×5 in.

skills.name: Y2K digicam
skills.thesis: The flaws of a cheap early sensor are the style: they mark a moment in time and read as honest.
skills.summary: The look of a 2 to 5 megapixel CCD compact: deep focus from a tiny sensor, blown highlights, a hard on-camera flash, over-sharpened edges and clumsy white balance. It is a record of a device and now a deliberate nostalgia.
use_cases: fashion and music campaigns with a nostalgic tone

colour_temperature.note: Auto white balance drifts across this band.

focal_length.note: This is the 35 mm equivalent of a 3× zoom of 5.8 to 17 mm on a 1/2.7 in CCD.

skills.name: Cinematic teal and orange
skills.thesis: Two opposed hues, the warm skin and the cool environment, give a frame instant depth and a sense of cinema.
skills.summary: A staged, shallow-focus frame with warm orange skin against cool teal shadows, graded like a film still. It is a colour recipe from the digital intermediate, and it is now a default look of films, ads and image prompts.

aspect_ratio.note: For a 2.39:1 frame, use 16:9 and crop bars at the top and the bottom.

skills.name: Party flash
skills.thesis: The harsh direct flash is the honest light of a real night, and an image that looks unplanned and unflattering reads as truthful and as cool.
skills.summary: A night-out picture lit by one hard flash on the camera. The subject glows against a falling-off, dark background, skin shines and colour is bold; the image looks candid, tipsy and slightly rude.

skills.name: Film grain revival
skills.thesis: Grain and imperfection give a picture a body, so the viewer believes it was lived and not rendered.
skills.summary: Photographs with visible grain, soft halation and warm colour, made on 35mm film or graded to look like it. The look says that a real moment passed through a real roll.
use_cases: image prompts for a warm analogue look

skills.name: AI hyperreal image
skills.thesis: A generated image can pass for a photograph at a glance, and its tells are the numbers that no real camera and no real scene would give together.
skills.summary: A recognisable look of images made by generative models: smooth, evenly lit, over-detailed and glossy. The look is named here so that a brief can ask for it or, more often, avoid it.
use_cases: naming the look in a brief so that a team can avoid it
teaching how to spot generated images
a negative prompt block for real photo styles

grain.note: The look has no grain; a high ISO breaks the gloss.

skills.name: Architectural photography
skills.thesis: A building is judged in a picture, so the picture must keep its lines true and choose the light that shows its form.
skills.summary: Photographs of buildings with upright lines, clean light and a chosen hour. The picture shows the form, the material and the way a building sits in its place.
use_cases: image prompts for true-line building views

focal_length.note: A tilt-shift lens of 17 to 45 mm, or 90 to 135 mm on 4×5 in, gives this band.

skills.name: Fashion editorial photography
skills.thesis: Fashion sells a feeling before it sells a thing, so the photograph builds the whole world around the clothes.
skills.summary: Planned pictures of clothes, bodies and attitude for a magazine page. Light, set, pose and edit are all designed, so that the image sells a world and not only a garment.
use_cases: image prompts for styled studio scenes

skills.name: Film noir still photography
skills.thesis: Darkness holds the story, so the picture shows only as much light as the mood needs.
skills.summary: Black-and-white stills with one hard light, deep shadow and a figure caught in a graphic frame. The look comes from the 1940s crime film, and it stays alive in fashion, posters and portraits.
use_cases: image prompts for moody night scenes

grain.note: The default is Tri-X 400 pushed to 1600.

skills.name: Food photography
skills.thesis: Food is a sensation, so the picture shows texture, steam and light before it shows the plate.
skills.summary: Photographs of dishes made to look edible and honest. A window, a small set and a short lens give shape, steam and texture, and a few props tell where the meal sits.
use_cases: brand campaigns for drinks and snacks

skills.name: Scandinavian interior photography
skills.thesis: A room looks livable when the light is honest and the objects are few, so the picture shows the light first.
skills.summary: Calm, bright pictures of rooms: pale wood, white walls, a window and a few objects. The light is soft, the lines are straight and the space is allowed to breathe.
use_cases: property marketing with a calm look

skills.name: German Expressionist cinema
skills.thesis: The set, the light and the body show inner fear, so the picture is built as a state of mind and not recorded as a place.
skills.summary: A studio cinema of painted sets, hard single-source light and distorted perspective. The frame shows the mind of the character, not the street. Black-and-white prints are tinted by scene.
use_cases: horror and thriller titles and trailers
music video with a gothic set
video prompts for a haunted or dream scene

frame_rate.note: A hand crank sets the capture rate.

colour_temperature.note: The value stands for the tint of the print: amber near 2800K, blue near 8000K.

skills.name: Soviet montage
skills.thesis: Meaning comes from the collision of shots, not from the content of a single shot, so the edit is the author of the film.
skills.summary: A cinema made in the cutting room. Two shots meet and a third meaning appears. Fast cuts, steep angles and typed faces drive the argument of the film.
use_cases: music video with a hard rhythm
brand film about industry or labour

frame_rate.note: A hand crank sets the capture rate.

average_shot_length.note: Cinemetrics gives 2.1 s for Man with a Movie Camera and 2.8 s for Battleship Potemkin.

skills.name: Classical Hollywood
skills.thesis: A film serves its story, so every device (light, angle, cut and score) is invisible and keeps the viewer's eye on the character and the action.
skills.summary: A studio craft in which the camera, the light and the cut serve a clear story. Three-point light, a master shot with coverage and a smooth match cut. The style hides itself.
use_cases: video prompts for a studio-era scene
title sequences with a glamour tone

skills.name: Film noir
skills.thesis: One hard lamp, a low camera and a narrow strip of light turn a city into a trap, so the viewer feels the fate of the hero before the hero does.
skills.summary: A black and white crime film lit from one hard source. Venetian-blind bars, rain and smoke cut the frame. The camera sits low and tilts. A tired man tells the story in voice-over and the plot closes on him.
use_cases: music video in black and white

skills.name: Italian Neorealism
skills.thesis: A film earns its truth by going out of the studio and showing ordinary lives in the real place, at the real pace, with no star and no neat plot.
skills.summary: Ruined streets, ordinary people and a story with no hero. Real places, non-professional actors and light that the day provides. The camera stays at human height and records the time a thing takes.
use_cases: period films of poverty and work
video prompts for a postwar street scene

skills.name: The oner
skills.thesis: One unbroken shot holds the viewer in real time and space, so the viewer cannot look away and feels each mistake and each turn as the actors do.
skills.summary: A scene or a whole film in one unbroken shot. The camera follows people through rooms and streets, and the cut is hidden or absent. Time is real, and the crew must be perfect.
use_cases: music videos and brand films in one take

average_shot_length.note: A take can run for the full film, but the domain stops at 600 s.

colour_temperature.note: One white balance holds for the whole shot.

skills.name: French New Wave
skills.thesis: A film is a personal essay shot on location with light gear, so the director's eye and the street replace the studio and the script department.
skills.summary: Light 35mm cameras, fast black-and-white stock and real streets. A handheld camera, a jump cut and a director who shows the hand. The film talks about film.
use_cases: video prompts for a city walk

skills.name: Direct cinema and vérité
skills.thesis: Light gear and sync sound let the camera watch people in real time, so the film is made of what happens and not of what is staged.
skills.summary: A handheld 16mm camera and a synchronised tape recorder stay with real people. No script, no set and no lamps. The camera sits in the room and waits. The picture is rough, and the sound is complete.
use_cases: video prompts for a real-event look

colour_temperature.note: The crew left the light as found.

skills.name: Giallo
skills.thesis: Saturated gel light, a killer's-eye camera and a stylised set make the murder a piece of design, so fear comes from the look more than from the plot.
skills.summary: An Italian murder film in saturated colour. A killer in black gloves is seen only as a hand and a blade. The camera moves as the killer sees, and the set glows in red, blue and green gels.
use_cases: fashion and perfume films with a dark mood

colour_temperature.note: Coloured gels on tungsten make the hue, not the white balance.

skills.name: Spaghetti western
skills.thesis: An extreme close-up and an extreme wide shot, with a long wait between them, make a duel into a ritual and the land into a stage.
skills.summary: A western shot in Spain and Italy on a wide 2.35:1 frame. A face fills the screen in an extreme close-up of the eyes, then the frame opens to a vast desert. Time stretches, the cut is slow, and the score is a part of the scene.
use_cases: music video with a desert setting

average_shot_length.note: A duel cuts at 0.5 to 2 s.

skills.name: New Hollywood
skills.thesis: The studio picture is used for a director's personal, sceptical view, so the heroes are flawed, the places are real and the endings stay open.
skills.summary: A director's cinema inside the studios: location shooting, long lenses, a zoom, a wide anamorphic frame and flawed heroes. A story that ends without a lesson. The style looks lived in and tough.
use_cases: video prompts for a car and street scene

skills.name: Third Cinema
skills.thesis: A film made outside the studio and outside the art house is a weapon for a people in a struggle, so each image must serve an argument and each screening must start a debate.
skills.summary: A militant film that works as a tool, not as a show. It uses a light 16mm camera, black and white stock, real streets and factories, archive clips, slogans on screen and direct address. The picture is rough and the cut is an argument.

colour_temperature.note: The film is black and white; this sets the tint of a toned print only.

skills.name: Music video
skills.thesis: The song is the script, so images are cut to its beat and structure and a loud, memorable look sells the artist.
skills.summary: A picture built to a song. The cut falls on the beat, the set is a stage, and the grade is loud. Story and place are cues that give way to a hook, a dance and a look.
use_cases: short-form vertical clips on a track
video prompts for a dance or a performance

aspect_ratio.note: The 16:9 frame maps to 1.85:1; 4:3 is for the 1980s and 9:16 for a platform cut.

frame_rate.note: Slow motion runs at 48 to 120 fps.

colour_temperature.note: Gels from 2000K to 9000K colour the key.

skills.name: Neon noir
skills.thesis: Coloured signs and a synth score turn the noir trap into a glowing night city, so the viewer reads loneliness in a clean, still, stylised frame.
skills.summary: A night crime film in colour. A lone driver or a replicant moves through a wet city of signs. Magenta and cyan light hits glass, rain and chrome. The pace is slow, the score is synthesised and the symmetry is cold.
use_cases: night city and car video prompts

colour_temperature.note: Neon and gels set the range.

skills.name: Hong Kong action
skills.thesis: An action scene is a piece of choreography shot and cut for its rhythm, so the stunt is shown whole and the cut gives it speed and weight.
skills.summary: Action built in the cut and in the body: slow motion, wide anamorphic frames and a stunt shot in full view. Gunfights are choreographed like dance, and fights are made of clear, fast phrases.
use_cases: music video with a fight scene
video prompts for a duel or a chase

frame_rate.note: Slow motion runs at 48 to 96 fps.

average_shot_length.note: A fight cuts at 1.5 to 3 s.

colour_temperature.note: Blue gels and sodium lamps extend the range.

skills.name: Slow cinema
skills.thesis: Time is the material of film, so a shot is held until the viewer sees the place and the person and feels the hours pass.
skills.summary: A cinema of duration. Few cuts, a still or slow camera, ordinary tasks shown in real time and little plot. The viewer's attention does the work that the cut usually does.
use_cases: video prompts for a quiet scene

average_shot_length.note: Sátántangó has about 150 shots in 7 h, near 170 s per shot.

skills.name: Dogme 95
skills.thesis: A fixed set of prohibitions removes illusion, polish and the director's taste, so that the truth of the scene remains.
skills.summary: A film made under a written vow: handheld camera, real locations, available light and the sound of the scene. The rules remove the tools that fake the world, so the actors and the room carry the film.
use_cases: video prompts for a raw family scene

colour_temperature.note: Tungsten and daylight stay mixed and uncorrected.

skills.name: Planimetric symmetry
skills.thesis: A film is a constructed object, so the frame is composed as a flat, symmetrical tableau and the camera moves only at right angles to it.
skills.summary: A frame built like a diagram: one central axis, a flat back wall, pastel colour blocks and a camera that tracks or pans at right angles. Every object is placed. The look is a miniature world with a dry joke.
use_cases: video prompts for a boutique or a hotel
music video with a built set

frame_rate.note: Stop-motion for a miniature runs at 12 fps.

skills.name: Found footage
skills.thesis: If a character holds the camera, the frame shows only what that person can see, so the viewer cannot look away from the dark edge of the picture.
skills.summary: A film that claims to be real recordings of a camera, left behind by people who vanished. The camera is in the hand of a character. It shakes, loses focus, runs out of light and records the fear in real time.
use_cases: game and app teasers with a real look

aspect_ratio.note: The 4:3 camcorder frame or a 16:9 frame, which maps to 1.85:1.

colour_temperature.note: The camera sets the white balance and nobody corrects it.

skills.name: Mumblecore
skills.thesis: A cheap digital camera and a few friends are enough to film the small, awkward moments of a relationship, so the film trusts the talk and not the polish.
skills.summary: A no-budget film about young people who talk, fail to say what they mean and drift. It uses a small digital camera, friends as actors, real rooms and half-improvised speech. The picture is plain and the mood is awkward.
use_cases: brand films with a real, friendly voice

aspect_ratio.note: The 16:9 frame maps to 1.85:1, the nearest option of the domain.

grain.note: This is video noise, not added grain.

skills.name: Creator vlog
skills.thesis: A direct address from one person, tightened by the jump cut, builds more trust than a produced film, so the creator's pace is the style.
skills.summary: A person talks to the lens in a room or on the move. Every pause is cut out, and a title, a sound or a cut-away lands every few seconds. The creator is the set, the brand and the grade.
use_cases: video prompts for a day-in-the-life clip

aspect_ratio.note: The 16:9 frame maps to 1.85:1, the nearest option of the domain.

skills.name: Phone cinema
skills.thesis: A phone is light, cheap and always present, so a crew of 3 can shoot a feature in real streets and fix the look with an app and a grade.
skills.summary: A feature film or a brand film shot on a phone. The lens is wide and close. The camera slips into places a big rig cannot reach. Gimbal, clip-on lens and app give a controlled look at small cost.
use_cases: brand and product films that show a phone look
indie films and shorts on a low budget
video prompts for a close, wide-lens look

aspect_ratio.note: A crop or an anamorphic adapter gives the wide frame.

skills.name: Vertical short-form
skills.thesis: A viewer swipes in 1 to 2 s, so every second must earn the next: the hook, the cut and the caption are the whole design.
skills.summary: A full-screen 9:16 clip of 15 to 45 s, shot on a phone and cut every 1.5 to 3 s. A hook in the first second, burned-in captions and a sound that can loop. The feed decides each rule.
use_cases: video prompts for a vertical clip

skills.name: Cinematic FPV
skills.thesis: A camera that can go anywhere should not cut: one unbroken flight turns space itself into the story.
skills.summary: One continuous flight through a place: a small drone with an ultra-wide camera dives, banks and threads gaps at 15 to 35 m/s. The camera moves like a bird, and the cut hides inside a wipe.
use_cases: music video with a one-take flight
video prompts for a drone fly-through

aspect_ratio.note: The 16:9 frame maps to 1.85:1, the nearest option of the domain.

frame_rate.note: Capture at 60 fps and conform to 24 or 30 fps.

skills.name: Camcorder revival
skills.thesis: A flawed, low-resolution tape image looks like a real memory, so the defect is the proof of the moment.
skills.summary: A 4:3 picture with tape noise, a date stamp and a shaky hand. It looks like a home video from 1985 to 2005. Creators shoot on old Hi8 and MiniDV or add the look in post, to look near and unpolished.
use_cases: video prompts for a memory or a party

aspect_ratio.note: The 4:3 tape frame is the look.

frame_rate.note: NTSC tape runs at 29.97 fps and PAL tape at 25 fps.

colour_temperature.note: The auto white balance drifts between tungsten and daylight.

skills.name: Renaissance painting
skills.thesis: A picture is a window onto a measured space, and the ideal human body is the measure of that space.
skills.summary: A picture as a measured window onto the world: linear perspective, modelled figures, a stable geometry and a calm, idealised body. Florentine and Venetian workshops and Flemish oil painters set the rules.

brush_size.note: No visible stroke inside a figure is wider than 3mm.

skills.name: Mannerism
skills.thesis: A picture is most beautiful when it shows skill and invention, so the painter stretches, twists and crowds the ideal body past nature.
skills.summary: Elongated, twisting figures in crowded, unstable space, in acid colour. The painters took the Renaissance rules and bent them on purpose: grace and artifice replace calm balance.
use_cases: book and album covers with a strange, cold grace
portrait with a stylised, courtly look

canvas_ratio.note: The format is tall, from 2:3 to 1:2.

skills.name: Baroque painting
skills.thesis: A picture is a staged moment in which light decides what matters and the viewer feels the event.
skills.summary: Painting of the instant: strong chiaroscuro, diagonal movement, warm earth colour and a viewer who is pulled into the scene. It serves the church, the court and the new Dutch market for portraits and domestic life.

value_contrast.note: Tenebrism needs a near-black shadow against a bright light.

skills.name: Ukiyo-e
skills.thesis: A picture is a printed sheet in which the contour, the flat colour and the cropped viewpoint carry everything, and the moment is as fleeting as the city.
skills.summary: Japanese woodblock prints and paintings of the Edo city: a firm black contour, flat fields of colour, bold cropping and a high or tilted viewpoint. A team of artist, carver and printer makes each sheet, and publishers sell it to a mass market.

brush_size.note: The line is printed from a carved block, so no brush trace shows.

skills.name: Rococo
skills.thesis: A picture should give pleasure: it is a refined, light and intimate object that charms the eye, and it does not preach or overwhelm.
skills.summary: Light, playful pictures of love, leisure and ornament, in pale pastel colour and curving lines. The weight and drama of the Baroque give way to charm, intimacy and a soft, feathery touch.

value_contrast.note: Pastel colour on a light ground keeps the value span low to mid.

skills.name: Romanticism
skills.thesis: A picture should move the viewer by emotion and by awe, and so the painter puts feeling, nature and imagination above the cool rules of the academy.
skills.summary: Pictures of storm, sea, ruin, passion and distant lands, in which feeling comes before rule. Nature is vast and the person is small; colour and brush carry the mood.
use_cases: film poster for epic or sea stories

skills.name: Realism
skills.thesis: A picture should record the real world of its own time, and ordinary work and ordinary people are as worthy a subject as a king or a god.
skills.summary: Ordinary people, work and country in plain light and earth colour. The painter shows life as it is, at life size, with no myth, no ideal and no sweetness.
use_cases: farm, craft and food provenance identity
editorial on work, labour and the land
portrait with a plain, honest tone

skills.name: Impressionism
skills.thesis: A picture records the impression of light on a surface at one moment, not the object as it is known to be.
skills.summary: Painting of the first look: quick, broken strokes of pure colour that record changing light on a modern scene. The painters work outdoors, drop the outline and the black shadow, and let the viewer's eye mix the colour.

value_contrast.note: Form is built by colour temperature, so the value span stays narrow.

skills.name: Nordic national romanticism
skills.thesis: A picture can give a young nation a face by painting its own land, light, legends and home with the best methods of Europe.
skills.summary: Painting that builds a nation's image from its own land, myths and home life: pale northern light, lake and forest, folk legend and the farm room. Painters trained in Paris bring back plein-air method and apply it to Nordic subjects.
use_cases: Nordic heritage and tourism art direction
book illustration for myth and legend

skills.name: Pointillism
skills.thesis: Colour is a science: pure dots set side by side mix in the eye with more light than a mix on the palette, and a picture can be built by rule.
skills.summary: A picture made of small, separate dots of pure colour that the eye mixes at a distance. The scene is still and ordered, built by colour theory and not by blending.
use_cases: poster and cover with a luminous, dotted texture

brush_size.note: A dot of 2–5mm on a canvas of 1–3m is well under 1% of the width.

skills.name: Post-Impressionism
skills.thesis: A picture should do more than record a glance: colour, line and stroke build lasting form and carry the feeling of the painter.
skills.summary: Painters who kept the bright colour of Impressionism and gave it back structure, feeling and symbol. Cézanne builds solid form from planes of colour; Van Gogh and Gauguin use bold colour, thick stroke and flat shape for emotion.
use_cases: book and album covers with warm, thick texture

skills.name: Symbolism
skills.thesis: A picture should suggest an inner idea by symbol and mood, and should turn from the plain surface of the visible world toward dream and the spirit.
skills.summary: Pictures of dream, myth, death and desire, in which a figure or a form stands for an idea. The mood is quiet, strange and inward; line and colour are chosen to suggest, never to explain.
use_cases: perfume, tea and jewellery campaign art
music and theatre posters with a dream mood
editorial art on inner life and myth

skills.name: Synthetism
skills.thesis: A picture should join the thing seen, the feeling of the painter and the pure form of colour and line, and it should not copy the scene from the eye.
skills.summary: Flat areas of pure colour held by a dark outline, painted from memory and feeling. The painter combines the seen scene, the feeling and the pure form of line and colour into one simple, decorative picture.
use_cases: poster and label art with flat colour

skills.name: Expressionism
skills.thesis: A picture shows what the painter feels, not what the eye sees, so that form and colour are distorted until they carry the emotion.
skills.summary: Pictures that bend the world to show an inner state: harsh colour, jagged line, tilted space and mask-like faces. The city is a threat and the body is a nerve.
use_cases: editorial art on city life and anxiety
album and book covers with a raw mood
film titles with a tense look

brush_size.note: A stroke of 20–50mm on a canvas of about 1m is 2.5–5% of the width.

skills.name: Fauvism
skills.thesis: Colour is free from the object: the painter chooses a hue for its force and its relations, and so builds the picture and the feeling by colour alone.
skills.summary: Colour at full strength and not true to nature: a green face, an orange sky. Flat patches, bold contours and quick strokes make the picture an arrangement of colour first.
use_cases: poster, festival and summer campaign art
packaging for drinks, food and sport
editorial illustration with a bold palette

value_contrast.note: Fauve colour works by hue, not by dark and light, so the value span stays moderate.

skills.name: Cubism
skills.thesis: A picture is an object in its own right, and it shows what a thing is by combining several viewpoints on one flat surface.
skills.summary: A picture that shows an object from several sides at once. Analytic Cubism breaks the subject into faceted planes in a narrow brown-grey key; Synthetic Cubism rebuilds it from flat shapes, pasted paper and brighter colour.
use_cases: portrait illustration with a modern edge

skills.name: Futurism
skills.thesis: Modern life is speed and energy, so a picture should show movement itself: the form is cut and repeated in time and fused with its setting.
skills.summary: Pictures of speed, noise and the machine city. Forms repeat and break into lines of force, so that a dog, a train or a crowd seems to move through the picture.
use_cases: sport, transport and tech campaign art
event and festival posters about speed
editorial art on the modern city

skills.name: Rayonism
skills.thesis: What the eye sees is the sum of the rays of light that objects throw back, so the painter draws the crossing of the rays and not the objects.
skills.summary: Pictures built from lines that stand for rays of light thrown back by objects. The rays cross in sharp, coloured beams, and the object breaks into a spray of lines in a Cubist and Futurist space.
use_cases: poster and cover art with a sense of speed
editorial illustration of light and energy
pattern and textile with a sharp line

skills.name: Orphism
skills.thesis: Colour alone can build the form and the movement of a picture, so the painter makes new wholes from pure colour and no longer shows the object.
skills.summary: Cubist structure with the bright colour of the Fauves, pushed toward pure abstraction. Discs and arcs of pure colour set side by side make rhythm and light, and the subject melts away.
use_cases: poster and cover art with a bright rhythm

skills.name: Suprematism
skills.thesis: Art should free itself from the object: pure shapes in a limitless white field give the feeling of form and of space and nothing else.
skills.summary: Flat geometric shapes, such as a square, a bar, a circle and a cross, that float on a white field. The picture shows no object: it shows pure feeling and the sense of space.
use_cases: poster and cover with bold geometry
brand marks and icons from flat shapes

brush_size.note: Flat, even fills hide the stroke.

skills.name: De Stijl painting
skills.thesis: A picture shows universal order when it uses only the horizontal and the vertical, the three primaries and the three non-colours, balanced without symmetry.
skills.summary: A picture reduced to straight black lines, rectangles of primary colour and white or grey, in asymmetric balance. Mondrian and van Doesburg wanted a universal language of pure relations that could also order a room or a city.

brush_size.note: The fields are flat and masked, so no stroke shows.

skills.name: Surrealism
skills.thesis: A picture can show the mind below reason, and so it joins plain, exact things in a way that no waking logic allows.
skills.summary: Dream pictures in a clear, exact style: real objects in impossible places, meetings and changes of scale. The detail is precise and the logic is wrong, so the image feels both real and strange.
use_cases: album, book and film cover art
editorial illustration of a concept or a mind

skills.name: Abstract Expressionism
skills.thesis: A painting is the record of an act, and its scale, its marks and its colour put the viewer inside the feeling and not in front of an image.
skills.summary: Large abstract paintings in which the act of painting is the subject: gesture, drip and slash in one camp, large soft fields of colour in the other. The canvas is an arena for an event, and it is big enough to surround the viewer.

brush_size.note: A stroke of 50–200mm on a canvas of 2–5m is 2–8% of the width.

skills.name: Colour Field Painting
skills.thesis: Colour alone can carry feeling and space: a large, simple field of hue, with no gesture and no drawing, surrounds the viewer and acts at once.
skills.summary: Very large canvases of broad, even fields of colour with soft edges. The colour is the subject; it is stained into the cloth or floated in layers, and it fills the sight of the viewer.
use_cases: backdrops and gradients for calm interfaces
wellness, meditation and music cover art
wall art and hotel and lobby identity
title cards with one strong hue

brush_size.note: Poured and stained paint shows almost no stroke.

skills.name: Pop Art
skills.thesis: Everyday mass images are the subject of the age, and a painting can take their look, their flat colour and their repeat, without comment and without the artist's hand.
skills.summary: Pictures made from the images of the mass market: comics, adverts, packaging and stars. Flat colour, hard outline, repeats and printing marks show that the picture is a product, not a vision.
use_cases: poster, campaign and packaging with a loud, playful voice

brush_size.note: Fields are flat and screened, so no stroke shows.

skills.name: Minimalism
skills.thesis: A picture is a plain object: what you see is what is there, so that form is reduced to the fewest parts and no illusion, gesture or story remains.
skills.summary: Flat, exact, repeated forms: stripes, grids and bare shapes in one or two colours. The picture is an object with no story and no hand, and the viewer sees what is there.
use_cases: interface and brand systems built on grids
packaging with one hue and one rule

brush_size.note: Rollers and masked edges leave no stroke in view.

skills.name: Photorealism
skills.thesis: A painting can match the camera: the artist works from a photograph, keeps its sharp focus and its flat modern light, and shows the city as the lens sees it.
skills.summary: Paintings that copy a photograph in every detail: glass, chrome, signs and street reflections, in sharp, even focus. The hand is hidden and the picture is as cool as a camera.
use_cases: automotive, retail and city campaign art
product scenes with exact glass and metal
book covers with a flat, modern look

brush_size.note: The paint is blended and airbrushed, so no stroke shows.

skills.name: Airbrush Surrealism
skills.thesis: A dream can be rendered as a polished object: the airbrush gives an impossible scene the smooth, lit surface of a photograph.
skills.summary: Surreal airbrushed illustration: supersaturated colour, floating or juxtaposed objects, chrome surfaces, lightning and X-ray cut-aways. It lived on album covers, pulp science fiction and fantasy, and pin-up chrome robots.
use_cases: science fiction and fantasy book covers

brush_size.note: The airbrush leaves no stroke, so the size stays near 0.

skills.name: Victorian trademark
skills.thesis: A mark earns trust when it shows a rich, finished picture and the full name of the maker, so the buyer sees the cost and the care behind the goods.
skills.summary: A pictorial trademark from the age of the first trademark registers. A figure, an animal or a scene sits in an oval or a cartouche, with engraved line shading, banners and three or more typefaces on one label.

colour_count.note: A chromolithograph can use up to 8 inks; the domain stops at 6.

stroke_weight.note: Hatch lines are near 0.5%; the main stems are 4 to 6%.

skills.name: Art Nouveau monogram
skills.thesis: The letters and the ornament are one drawing: a mark grows like a plant from one line, and the hand of the artist shows in each curve.
skills.summary: Interlaced initials and lettering drawn as one ornament, inside a frame of whiplash curves and plant forms. Publishers, societies and workshops used it as a vignette on books, journals and printed matter.

skills.name: Emblem and badge
skills.thesis: A mark that is a closed seal says membership and authority: the frame tells the viewer that everything inside belongs together.
skills.summary: A closed shape, a circle, a shield or a roundel, that holds a symbol and the name on a ring or a band. Agencies, clubs, transport lines and makers use it as a seal of membership or of origin.

skills.name: Swiss modernist corporate mark
skills.thesis: A mark is a tool of a system: it must be objective, reproducible in any medium, and the same at 5 mm and at 5 m.
skills.summary: A mark for a whole organisation: a reduced symbol on a grid, one or two colours, a neo-grotesque or a custom sans logotype, and a manual that fixes every size, space and colour. Railways, airlines and state agencies led the style.

skills.name: Geometric abstract symbol
skills.thesis: A pure form carries meaning by its structure alone: a square, a bar or a loop can say stability, growth or a cycle in every language.
skills.summary: One abstract shape, built from squares, circles, bars or loops, that stands for the organisation with no letters. The shape implies a direction, growth or a cycle, and is strong enough to stand alone on a sign or a coin.

stroke_weight.note: Bands are 12 to 25% of the symbol height; the domain stops at 20%.

skills.name: Wordmark-led minimal
skills.thesis: The name is the mark: one carefully spaced word, with one detail of its own, is clearer and more durable than any symbol.
skills.summary: The name alone, set or drawn in one weight of a sans, with a single detail that makes it own: a cut stroke, a hidden arrow, a joined pair of letters. No symbol and no frame.

skills.name: Gradient 3D and glass
skills.thesis: On a screen a mark can be a lit object: gloss, depth and reflection make it feel new, touchable and alive.
skills.summary: A mark lit like an object: top highlights, gradients from light to deep colour, a glass bevel, a reflection under it and a soft drop shadow. The screen was now the main medium, and the mark imitated a polished button or a globe.
use_cases: app icons with a retro theme

stroke_weight.note: The mark has no line stroke; the value sets the light rim and the swoosh.

skills.name: Flat 2010s mark
skills.thesis: On a screen honesty is flat colour: a mark is a set of clean shapes that read at icon size and scale with no loss.
skills.summary: The gloss goes away. A simple symbol or a geometric sans word in 2–4 bright flat colours, with no gradient, no shadow and no bevel, drawn to work as a 24 px app icon first.

stroke_weight.note: A stroke is 1/12 of the icon size.

skills.name: Pixel icon
skills.thesis: An icon is a set of square pixels on a fixed grid, and the grid is part of the look, not a limit to hide.
skills.summary: Icons drawn on a hard pixel grid, one square at a time. Each pixel is on or off, edges are stairs, and the set has 1 to 16 colours. The style began with low screen resolution and returns now as a retro choice.
use_cases: developer tools with a playful voice

stroke_width.note: A line is a run of whole pixels, not a vector stroke.

corner_radius.note: A corner is a stair of whole pixels, never a curve.

skills.name: Isometric icon
skills.thesis: An icon can show an object as a solid in space and keep it exact, because parallel projection keeps every edge at a true angle.
skills.summary: Icons drawn as small objects in a parallel isometric view: three faces at once, edges at 30° to the horizontal, no vanishing point. Flat colour fills give each face its own tone.

fill_mode.note: Each face takes one flat tone; the light sets the tone, not a gradient.

skills.name: Skeuomorphic icon
skills.thesis: An icon is a small picture of a real object, and the material tells the user what the function is.
skills.summary: Icons that look like small real objects: leather, glass, metal and paper, with light from the top, gradients and a soft cast shadow. The style peaked with Mac OS X Aqua and iOS 1 to 6, and Tango gave it an open, semi-realistic form.
use_cases: brand illustrations with a tactile feel

grid_size.note: Below 32 px the texture and the light do not read.

skills.name: Flat icon
skills.thesis: An icon is a sign, not a picture, and flat shapes in clear colour carry the meaning faster than material and light.
skills.summary: Icons in flat, solid colour shapes with no gradient, no texture and no light model. A simple object sits on a coloured ground, often a circle or a rounded square. Flat icons replaced skeuomorphic icons in the early 2010s.

stroke_width.note: There is no stroke; shapes meet edge to edge.

skills.name: Solid glyph icon
skills.thesis: An icon is a single solid mark, and a silhouette with cut-out details reads best at small sizes and on any ground.
skills.summary: Icons as solid, one-colour silhouettes, like the glyphs of a bold typeface. Inner details are cut out of the fill as gaps. The style began with icon fonts and stays the default for small, high-contrast UI.
use_cases: buttons and small UI at 12–16 px
active state of an outline set

stroke_width.note: There is no stroke; the form is the fill.

skills.name: Outline icon
skills.thesis: An icon set is a typeface of objects: one stroke, one grid and one corner radius make hundreds of glyphs read as one family.
skills.summary: Icons drawn as one even stroke on a 24 px grid, with round caps and joins and no fill. The set reads like a light typeface: the same line weight, the same corner radius and the same live area for every glyph.

skills.name: Material Symbols
skills.thesis: An icon system is a set of tokens: one grid and four variable axes let one glyph serve every size, weight and state.
skills.summary: Google's open icon system: geometric glyphs on a 24 dp grid with keyline shapes. Material Icons (2014) gave five themes; Material Symbols (2022) is a variable font with axes for fill, weight, grade and optical size.
use_cases: design systems that need fill and weight states

stroke_width.note: The weight axis from 100 to 700 sets this band; weight 400 gives 2 px.

skills.name: Duotone icon
skills.thesis: One colour in two strengths gives an icon a figure and a ground, so the meaning reads first and the detail second.
skills.summary: Icons in two tones of one colour: a main shape at full strength and a secondary layer at 20–40% opacity. The second tone gives hierarchy and a little depth, but the icon stays a flat glyph.

skills.name: 3D clay icon
skills.thesis: After a decade of flat glyphs, an icon can have volume again if the forms stay simple, round and soft like a toy.
skills.summary: Icons rendered in 3D with soft, matte, clay-like materials, large round corners and a soft shadow. They bring depth back after the flat years, but with toy-like simplicity and no real texture.
use_cases: landing page heroes and feature cards
consumer and fintech apps with a soft voice

stroke_width.note: There is no stroke; light and the fillet make the edges.

corner_radius.note: The style uses a fillet of 48 px at 256 px; the domain caps the radius at 16 px.

skills.name: Blackletter
skills.thesis: A letter written with a broad nib held at a steep angle breaks each curve into straight strokes and makes a dark, even texture on the page.
skills.summary: The broken letter of the Gothic book hand: narrow, dark, with strokes that turn at sharp angles instead of curves. Gutenberg printed his Bible in textura; Fraktur stayed the German text face until 1941. Today it carries tradition, heraldry, metal and rebellion.

stroke_contrast.note: The o test misleads here; the value is the stem against the hairline.

tracking.note: Sperrsatz spaces one word by about 0.15 em for emphasis.

skills.name: Garalde old-style serif
skills.thesis: A text letter keeps the rhythm of the hand that wrote it, so the eye reads a page without effort.
skills.summary: The roman of the Renaissance book: moderate contrast, a diagonal stress from the broad-nib pen, bracketed serifs and a small x-height. It is the default text face of the long tradition and reads well for hours.

skills.name: Formal script
skills.thesis: A letter is one movement of a flexible pointed pen: pressure on the downstroke, a hairline on the upstroke, and every letter joined to the next.
skills.summary: Joined, sloped letters from the pointed pen of the eighteenth-century writing master. Pressure makes the downstrokes swell and the upstrokes become hairlines. It speaks of invitations, ceremony and romance, and reads well only in short lines.
use_cases: one signature line in a brand

x_height_ratio.note: Many scripts have an x-height below 0.35; the domain floor clips the range.

stroke_contrast.note: The o test misleads here; the value is the stem against the hairline.

tracking.note: Tracking breaks the joins of a connected script.

skills.name: Transitional serif
skills.thesis: A letter can be drawn by reason and still serve the reader: the pen gives way to the engraver's line, but not yet to the extreme.
skills.summary: The Enlightenment roman between the old style and the Didone: the stress turns nearly vertical, the contrast rises, and the serifs become flatter and sharper. It is precise but still warm, and it reads well in text.

x_height_ratio.note: Libre Baskerville raises the x-height for screens.

skills.name: Didone
skills.thesis: A letter is a geometric figure of thick and thin, cut as fine as the metal and the paper allow.
skills.summary: The extreme of the roman: a vertical stress, hairline serifs with no bracket, and a strong contrast between stem and hairline. At display sizes it is the voice of fashion and luxury; in small text it sparkles and tires the eye.

x_height_ratio.note: Playfair Display sits at the top; Bodoni and Didot sit near 0.40.

tracking.note: The top of the range is for letter-spaced capitals.

skills.name: Fat face display
skills.thesis: A letter for a poster is as black as the stem can be while the hairlines keep it readable.
skills.summary: The first type made only for display: a Didone pushed to extreme weight, with stems as thick as half the letter and hairlines kept fine. It shouts from posters and covers, and it fails in text.
use_cases: editorial hero titles on the web

skills.name: Slab serif
skills.thesis: A letter for a loud and busy world must be heavy, square and hard to break.
skills.summary: Heavy, square serifs on a sturdy letter with low contrast. Born on the poster in industrial Britain, it carries a loud, solid and practical voice, and modern text cuts serve screens and typewriters as well.

skills.name: Grotesque sans
skills.thesis: A letter without serifs is plain, and the plain letter is the strongest one at a distance.
skills.summary: The first sans serifs: plain, heavy letters for posters, with a little contrast, some quirks of width and a two-storey g. Later text cuts such as Akzidenz-Grotesk and Franklin Gothic gave the class a sober, workmanlike voice.

skills.name: Monospace
skills.thesis: When every character has the same width, columns align without a grid and each character is a unit the reader can count.
skills.summary: Every character takes the same width, as on a typewriter or a terminal. The narrow letters get serifs or wide arms and the wide letters are squeezed. It is the voice of code, data, forms and the typewritten document.

width.note: The advance is fixed, so the width moves only a little.

x_height_ratio.note: Courier sits near 0.42; code faces such as JetBrains Mono near 0.55.

tracking.note: Tracking breaks the columns of a monospace.

skills.name: Humanist sans
skills.thesis: A sans serif reads best when it keeps the proportions and the open forms of the written roman.
skills.summary: A sans serif on the skeleton of the Renaissance roman: open apertures, varied widths, a little stroke modulation and an angled cut on the terminals. It reads well at small sizes and in poor conditions, and sounds warm.
use_cases: product interfaces with a warm voice

skills.name: Geometric sans
skills.thesis: A letter is a construction of pure forms, free of the hand and of history.
skills.summary: A sans serif built from the circle, the square and the triangle: a round o, a single-storey a, pointed apexes and almost no contrast. It is the type of the modernist programme, clean and optimistic, with a small x-height in the classic cuts.

x_height_ratio.note: Futura sits near 0.40; Avant Garde and screen faces go higher.

skills.name: Neo-grotesque sans
skills.thesis: A typeface is a neutral vessel: it carries the message and adds nothing of its own.
skills.summary: The neutral sans of the grid: even widths, horizontal terminals, closed apertures, a large x-height and almost no contrast. It lets the layout speak and is the default voice of interfaces and corporate systems.

width.note: Univers spans condensed to extended cuts in one system.

x_height_ratio.note: Helvetica is about 0.52 and Inter about 0.55.

skills.name: Vector display arcade
skills.thesis: A world can be drawn with light alone: a few sharp glowing lines on black are enough for the eye to build space.
skills.summary: The beam of the tube draws lines, not pixels. Bright monochrome or colour outlines glow on pure black, with no fill, no texture and a world built from wire shapes.

render_resolution.note: The addressable field of the beam (1024 by 1024), not a raster.

texel_density.note: No texture: the floor of the range.

skills.name: 8-bit tile graphics
skills.thesis: A small grid and a small palette force each object into its clearest silhouette, so a house in 16 pixels reads at once.
skills.summary: A world drawn from 8×8 pixel tiles on a 256×240 screen, with 3 colours plus transparency in each sprite and a fixed hardware palette of about 54 colours. Black outlines and flat fills make each house and tree a small icon.

colour_depth.note: A 54-colour master palette, used through 2-bit sub-palettes.

skills.name: Isometric pixel world
skills.thesis: A fixed 2:1 diagonal gives depth with no perspective, so a room can be read whole like an architect's axonometric drawing.
skills.summary: The world is seen from above at a fixed angle with 2:1 pixel diagonals. Rooms become boxes cut open on two sides, so a player reads walls, floor and furniture at once.

skills.name: 16-bit sprite and parallax
skills.thesis: A richer palette and stacked layers let pixel art paint light, air and distance without a 3D engine.
skills.summary: Pixel art at 256×224 with up to 256 colours on screen from a 32,768-colour range. Several scrolling layers give parallax depth, sprites carry 15 colours and soft ramps, and skies get gradients made of colour bands.

skills.name: Four-shade handheld
skills.thesis: Four values of one colour are enough for a world, if the pattern and the outline carry the form.
skills.summary: A 160×144 screen with four shades of one olive-green hue. Every house and room is drawn from 8×8 tiles in light, two mid tones and dark, so form lives only in value and pattern.

skills.name: Pre-rendered backgrounds
skills.thesis: If the camera does not move, each view can be a finished render, composed like a film frame.
skills.summary: Rooms and streets are rendered offline in 3D software and shown as still images at fixed camera angles. The player moves as a low-poly figure, or as a cursor, over a scene with far more light and detail than the console can draw.

skills.name: Fifth-generation low poly
skills.thesis: A world of few polygons can still be entered: a box with a picture on each face becomes a room the camera walks into.
skills.summary: Real-time 3D at about 320×240: characters of a few hundred polygons, small textures of 64 or 128 px, vertex lighting and fog at the far plane. On one console the textures warp and the vertices jitter; on another they blur.

skills.name: Cel-shaded 3D
skills.thesis: Real-time 3D does not need to imitate a photograph; it can imitate a drawing and keep its clarity at any angle.
skills.summary: 3D models drawn to look like a cartoon or an animation cel: light falls in 2 or 3 flat steps, black outlines trace each shape, and colours stay bright and flat. A full 3D world looks hand drawn.

skills.name: Hand-painted texture
skills.thesis: A painter's hand can carry the light of a world, so a small engine budget still gives a warm, rich place.
skills.summary: Mid-poly models with textures painted by hand: light, shadow, wear and colour shifts are in the paint, not in the engine. Chunky, exaggerated buildings and bright, saturated colour read clearly at a distance.

skills.name: Seventh-generation desaturated bloom
skills.thesis: Realism is grit: a serious world is grey, worn and wet, and light blooms out of the dark.
skills.summary: The first HD consoles push normal maps, bloom and HDR light, and art direction answers with grey, brown and teal: desaturated ruins, heavy contrast, glowing windows and wet, specular surfaces.

skills.name: Voxel block world
skills.thesis: If the world is a grid of equal blocks, anyone can build in it, and the grid itself becomes the style.
skills.summary: The world is a grid of 1 m cubes, each with a 16×16 pixel texture on its faces. Every house, room and hill is built block by block, with nearest-neighbour pixels and simple face light.

skills.name: PBR photoreal
skills.thesis: If every material obeys the same physics of light, the world looks real from any angle and at any hour.
skills.summary: Materials follow physics: albedo, roughness and metalness answer one light model, so wood, stone and metal look right in any light. Scanned surfaces, global illumination and ray-traced reflections push game worlds close to architectural renders.

skills.name: Flat geometric isometric
skills.thesis: Architecture reduced to pure faces and an orthographic view becomes a calm puzzle that a hand can turn.
skills.summary: Clean geometric architecture in an orthographic isometric view, coloured in flat pastel faces with no texture. Stairs, arches and towers are built like a paper model, and the space can fold into impossible shapes.

texel_density.note: No texture: the floor of the range.

skills.name: HD-2D diorama
skills.thesis: Old pixel sprites inside modern light and depth of field read as a lovingly built miniature.
skills.summary: Pixel-art sprites stand in a 3D world built like a miniature model, seen from a high camera with strong depth of field, bloom and modern light. The world looks like a toy diorama lit at golden hour.

skills.name: Low-poly PS1 revival
skills.thesis: An old limit, chosen on purpose, makes a modern world feel like a half-remembered dream.
skills.summary: Small indie teams copy the limits of the first 3D consoles on purpose: low polygons, warped low-res textures, vertex jitter, dither and dense fog. The look serves dread and nostalgia, often in empty houses and night streets.

skills.name: Woodcut relief print
skills.thesis: A black line that stands on a block of wood can carry form, light and tone if the cutter swells, tapers and crosses it.
skills.summary: A picture cut into the side grain of a plank: the cutter leaves the lines standing and the press prints them black. In Nuremberg, Wolgemut and Dürer made the cut carry tone with parallel and crossed lines, so one block printed with the type of a book.

skills.name: Copper engraving
skills.thesis: A burin line that swells and tapers in polished copper gives the finest and most even tone that a hand can make.
skills.summary: A picture cut into a copper plate with a burin, inked into the grooves and printed under great pressure. Schongauer and Dürer made it an art; Goltzius made the swelling line a show of skill; for three centuries it reproduced paintings and maps.

skills.name: Drypoint
skills.thesis: A needle that scratches bare copper throws up a burr. The burr prints as a soft black line that no acid and no burin can make.
skills.summary: A steel or diamond needle scratches the plate and pushes up a burr of metal along each furrow. The burr holds ink and prints as a soft velvety black line that wears down after a few dozen impressions.
use_cases: stationery and invitations with a hand-made look

skills.name: Ottoman ebru marbled paper
skills.thesis: A pattern that the water and the comb make together, and that no plate can repeat, gives a sheet of paper a living surface.
skills.summary: Pigment floats on a thick bath of water. The marbler combs it into a pattern and lays a sheet on it for one monotype. Each sheet is unique, with flowing veins, combed curls and floral drops.

skills.name: Chiaroscuro woodcut
skills.thesis: Flat tone blocks printed in steps over a line block imitate a brush-and-wash drawing heightened with white, with no hatching.
skills.summary: A line block carries the drawing and one to three tone blocks are printed over it in flat washes of one hue. The flat steps from paper white to dark ground imitate a brush-and-wash drawing heightened with white.
use_cases: wine and spirits labels with a heritage look

skills.name: Etching
skills.thesis: A needle that moves through wax as easily as a pen gives the artist a free line, and the acid gives it depth.
skills.summary: The artist draws with a needle through a wax ground on a metal plate, and acid bites the lines. The line is free like a pen line. Callot made it exact; Rembrandt made it dark and alive, with tone from hatching and from ink left on the plate.

skills.name: Dong Ho folk woodblock painting
skills.thesis: A village can print a whole folk art from plant and mineral colour, one flat block at a time, on paper that shines with ground shell.
skills.summary: Villagers print a black outline block, then add flat colour blocks one by one on do paper that carries a coat of scallop-shell powder. The colours come from plants and minerals, so they are bright and flat.
use_cases: packs for Vietnamese food and craft

skills.name: Katazome and Ise katagami stencil print
skills.thesis: A pattern cut once in paper can be printed a thousand times as a sharp white shape on dyed cloth, if the stencil holds its islands with thin bridges.
skills.summary: A stencil is cut in layers of mulberry paper, and rice-paste resist is spread through it onto cloth. The cloth is then dyed. The result is a repeat pattern with sharp white edges and flat colour.

skills.name: Chinese nianhua New Year woodblock print
skills.thesis: A New Year picture works as a charm for the house, so it must be bright, full of good signs and cheap enough for every door.
skills.summary: Workshops print a key-block outline and fill it with colour blocks, and often add hand-painted colour. Yangliuqing sheets end with hand colour and painted faces. Other towns print bold and flat.
use_cases: Lunar New Year cards, packs and posters
packs for Chinese food and tea

skills.name: Ten Bamboo Studio polychrome block print
skills.thesis: A page of a painting manual can carry the soft colour of a scroll when the printer splits the picture into small blocks that fit like a jigsaw.
skills.summary: Hu Zhengyan's workshop cut many small blocks for one picture (douban) and printed them in turn on one sheet. Dry blocks pressed the paper (gonghua) and raised the outline of a petal or a cloud.
use_cases: gift cards with a blind emboss

skills.name: Mezzotint
skills.thesis: If the plate starts black, the artist works from dark to light and gets a tone as soft as paint, with no line.
skills.summary: The plate is rocked with a toothed tool until it holds a full, velvet black; the engraver scrapes and burnishes the lights out of the dark. Ludwig von Siegen made the first in 1642; London engravers used it to reproduce portraits in oil.
use_cases: editorial images on night or mystery

skills.name: Russian lubok folk print
skills.thesis: A coarse black key line and a few loose hand colours are enough to tell a story that anyone can read at a glance.
skills.summary: A cheap sheet cut in wood or engraved in copper, printed in black on thin paper and then coloured by hand. Pedlars sold it by the thousand. The line is coarse and the colour is flat and loose, because speed and price mattered most.

skills.name: Nishiki-e multi-block colour woodblock print
skills.thesis: A set of wood blocks, one for each colour, can make a full-colour picture when a printer rubs thin water-based colour into damp paper and keeps each block in register by hand.
skills.summary: A drawing is pasted on a cherry plank and cut by a carver. A printer rubs water-based pigment from one block for each colour onto damp washi with a baren. The colours are flat and soft, and the wood grain shows.

skills.name: Aquatint
skills.thesis: A bitten grain of rosin gives a copper plate the soft tone of a wash. An etched line can then sit on a brush-like ground.
skills.summary: Rosin dust is melted onto a copper plate, and acid bites round each grain. The print has a soft tone like a wash. The artist controls the tone with varnish and a burnisher, so the print has a grey speckled grain.
use_cases: album and book covers with a night mood

skills.name: Stipple (crayon-manner) engraving
skills.thesis: A plate built from dots and short flicks, with no hatching, gives flesh and drapery a soft tone that imitates a chalk drawing.
skills.summary: The plate is built up from etched and engraved dots and short flicks, so tone has no hatching. The print shows soft skin and flesh with pale dotted shading, and publishers often printed in red-brown (sanguine).
use_cases: portrait and decorative prints with a period look

skills.name: Surimono privately published print
skills.thesis: A print made for a closed circle of friends, not for the market, can spend its whole cost on material and on fine cut.
skills.summary: Poetry clubs paid for small woodblock prints as New Year cards and as notices of events. The patrons paid, so the printers used costly pigment, metal dust, embossing and burnish on thick paper.
use_cases: small editions for a private club

skills.name: End-grain wood engraving
skills.thesis: A burin on the end grain of boxwood cuts white lines in a black block, so that fine tone and exact detail print with type.
skills.summary: A burin cuts lines into a boxwood end-grain block, which is inked on the surface and printed with type. The cut becomes a white line on black, and fine parallel hatching gives the grey tones of Victorian magazines.
use_cases: magazine and newspaper features with a period look

skills.name: Senjafuda pilgrim name slip
skills.thesis: A name on a slip of paper can be a prayer, a signature and a small piece of art at the same time.
skills.summary: Pilgrims pasted small woodblock name slips on shrine gates. Collectors later swapped decorated slips in clubs, and artists such as Hiroshige designed slips in many colours. Each slip is 58 mm by 173 mm.

skills.name: Battala woodcut
skills.thesis: A cheap wood block with a bold line can put a sacred or comic story in the hands of a bazaar crowd.
skills.summary: A cheap woodcut sheet from the Battala bazaar quarter of Calcutta. Local craftsmen cut a bold black outline, often to copy a painted original, and printed it with type on thin country paper.
use_cases: book and album covers with a Bengali theme
editorial images for South Asian history

skills.name: Steel-engraved banknote and stamp
skills.thesis: Fine engraved line and machine-turned rosettes on steel are hard to copy. The print is then the proof that a note or a stamp is real.
skills.summary: Hardened steel plates carry portraits, vignettes and geometric rosettes, printed from a transfer press. Dense fine lines and machine-turned patterns are hard to copy. The print has a tight frame of line work in green or black, with a coloured tint.
use_cases: bank and fintech brand marks with a heritage look

skills.name: Crayon lithograph
skills.thesis: A greasy crayon on a grained stone keeps the pressure of the hand, so that a drawing prints as drawn, with no engraver between.
skills.summary: The artist draws with greasy crayon directly on a grained limestone, and the grain catches the crayon as speckled black. The print keeps the drawing's pressure, from pale grain to dense black, with no engraved line.
use_cases: political posters with a drawn look

skills.name: Wood-type poster
skills.thesis: A poster is a stack of words, and each line takes the largest and boldest type that fits the width.
skills.summary: A bill set in large letters cut from end-grain wood, printed on a hand or a job press in one or two flat inks. Darius Wells made the type cheap in 1828; the auction, the circus and the theatre filled walls with stacked lines of fat faces and slabs.

skills.name: Qajar lithographed book
skills.thesis: A printed book can keep the hand of the scribe and the page of the manuscript, and still be cheap to copy.
skills.summary: A book printed from stone. A scribe wrote each page in nastaliq with greasy ink, and the press copied the page as it was. The book looks like a manuscript, with a frame of ruled lines and small painted pictures.

skills.name: Collotype
skills.thesis: A light-hardened gelatin film that takes ink in proportion to tone prints a photograph with true continuous tone and no dot screen.
skills.summary: A glass or metal plate is coated with light-hardened gelatin, which swells with water to take ink in proportion to tone. The print has continuous tone with only a fine reticulation, and is often a warm brown or black on matt paper.

skills.name: Chromolithograph poster
skills.thesis: A few bright inks, drawn by the artist on stone, can make a sheet on a wall as bright and as alive as a painting.
skills.summary: A large poster drawn in crayon and brush on stones, one stone for each colour. Jules Chéret opened his own press in Paris in 1866 and printed colour posters with a few strong inks; Mucha, Toulouse-Lautrec and the Beggarstaffs made the street a gallery.

skills.name: Meiji kosen-ga and aniline-red woodblock print
skills.thesis: A woodblock print can show the new Japan, with its trains, brick streets and gas light, if it takes the hard colour and the deep shadow of the West.
skills.summary: Early Meiji prints used imported synthetic (aniline) dye in hot reds and purples. Kiyochika's kosen-ga later added Western light and shadow to night scenes of gas lamps, trains and ships.
use_cases: posters on Meiji and railway history
game and film art for a modernising Japan
record sleeves with a hot, night palette

skills.name: Photogravure
skills.thesis: A photograph etched into copper through an aquatint grain prints as continuous tone in a deep ink. The photograph then reads as an original print.
skills.summary: A carbon-tissue positive is transferred to a copper plate, which is etched through a dusted aquatint grain. The plate prints continuous photographic tone as deep, rich ink on thin tissue, with no visible screen.

skills.name: Posada broadside
skills.thesis: A flat black picture cut in metal, with a hard white line and set type under it, can tell a news story or a joke to a reader who has little money and little time.
skills.summary: A cheap sheet that carries a hard black picture and set type. José Guadalupe Posada cut or etched the picture in a metal plate for the press of Antonio Vanegas Arroyo, and the sheet sold in the street.
use_cases: labels for mezcal and craft beer
book covers for Latin American history

skills.name: Private-press book
skills.thesis: A book is one object: the type, the page, the paper, the ink and the ornament are made together and by hand.
skills.summary: A book printed by hand on handmade paper, in a heavy type cut for the press, with woodcut borders and initials, in black and red. William Morris started the Kelmscott Press in 1891 against the grey, thin books of the steam press; the Doves Press made the same craft plain.

skills.name: Ravi Varma oleograph
skills.thesis: A lithograph in many colours can copy the smooth oil painting of a god and put it in every home for a few annas.
skills.summary: A god picture printed by stone lithography in many colours, for the home shrine and the shop wall. The oil-like gloss, the saturated colour and the smooth blend copy the paintings of Raja Ravi Varma.

skills.name: Ben-Day comic print
skills.thesis: Four inks, a black line and a few fixed tints of dots can colour a whole world for a cent.
skills.summary: A comic or a newspaper picture printed on cheap newsprint in four flat inks, with tints made of fixed dots from Benjamin Day's films. The Sunday supplement of the 1890s and the comic book of the 1930s–1960s made black lines, primary colours and dots a mass look.

skills.name: Mir iskusstva book graphics
skills.thesis: A single firm line and flat tints, set inside an ornamental frame, make a fairy-tale page that reads as a unit with its border and letters.
skills.summary: A firm, even black pen outline, in the manner of a woodcut, is filled with flat watercolour tints. The key line and the tints print in separate runs. Folk ornament frames each page.

screen_ruling.note: The style makes no tone; the screen stays at zero.

skills.name: Cordel xilogravura
skills.thesis: One woodcut on a cheap cover can tell the whole story of a verse in a single bold picture.
skills.summary: A woodcut for the cover of a cordel chapbook, a cheap booklet of verse that hangs from a string. The cutter works in a soft wood, with bold white lines, flat shapes and one black ink.

skills.name: Shanghai yuefenpai calendar poster
skills.thesis: A calendar that a shop gives away can sell a product through the face of a modern woman, in smooth, warm colour that a lithograph can copy.
skills.summary: Artists drew a beauty in rubbed charcoal and tinted it with watercolour. Printers copied the result by chromolithography for tobacco, medicine and cloth advertisers. A calendar band runs along the foot.
use_cases: retro posters and packs for Shanghai themes
film and game art for 1930s Shanghai

skills.name: Sosaku-hanga creative print
skills.thesis: A print is art when one person makes the whole of it, from the drawing to the last rub of the baren.
skills.summary: The artist draws, cuts and prints the block alone, and so rejects the three trades of the ukiyo-e shop. The result is a bold cut, an individual block, abstract shape and visible tool marks.
use_cases: editorial art with a personal voice

skills.name: Die Brucke woodcut
skills.thesis: A plank cut with a few hard strokes and printed by hand keeps the cut and the grain. The print shows a raw inner state, not a clean picture.
skills.summary: Planks are cut with a few bold gouge strokes, and the grain and the cut marks stay visible. The artists often hand-print on cheap paper with a spoon or a press. The ink is uneven, with flat black masses and sharp angular white.
use_cases: editorial illustration with a raw edge

skills.name: Pochoir plate
skills.thesis: A stencil and a brush give a flat, opaque and luminous colour that no press can match.
skills.summary: A plate coloured by hand through a set of stencils, each one for a colour, in gouache and watercolour on a printed key line. Iribe and Lepape made the Poiret albums in 1908 and 1911; Barbier and the Gazette du Bon Ton made it the look of Art Deco fashion.

skills.name: Narbut Ukrainian Baroque graphics
skills.thesis: A dense black pen line and Baroque lettering can make a modern cover that looks like a page from an old Ukrainian book.
skills.summary: A black pen drawing with Baroque capitals and heraldry, printed from zinc line blocks, sometimes with one or two flat tints. The dense ornament and the hand lettering imitate old engraved Ukrainian books.

skills.name: Shin-hanga new print
skills.thesis: The old Edo craft of block and baren can serve a new subject, a landscape with weather and light, when a publisher keeps the three trades apart.
skills.summary: The publisher Watanabe Shozaburo revived the ukiyo-e split of designer, carver and printer for foreign buyers. The prints show Western light and atmosphere, with many tonal blocks for rain, snow and dusk.

skills.name: ROSTA Window stencil poster
skills.thesis: A news poster that artists can paint in one night must use few flat colours, a heavy contour and a rhyme that a passer-by reads in seconds.
skills.summary: A strip of cartoon panels with short rhymed captions, cut as paper stencils and painted by hand, then copied for shop windows. The flat colour, thick black contour and fast brush work follow from the speed of the news.

screen_ruling.note: The style makes no tone; the screen stays at zero.

skills.name: Constructivist photomontage poster
skills.thesis: A poster made of real photographs, set on strong diagonals and printed in a few hard colours, speaks as a fact and not as a picture.
skills.summary: Cut-out photographs are pasted with drawn shapes and big type, then copied by photo-lithography or by halftone blocks in two to four flat inks. The diagonals, the red and black blocks and the sans-serif capitals come from the montage and the spot colour.

skills.name: Expressive linocut
skills.thesis: Linoleum has no grain, so a gouge cuts a smooth curve, and flat opaque colour layers can carry rhythm and speed.
skills.summary: A sheet of linoleum is cut with a V-gouge and printed by hand, so the cut has smooth curves and no grain. Flat opaque colour layers overlap in bold rhythmic shapes, as in the Grosvenor School prints of 1929-1938.
use_cases: transport and sports branding with a hand-made look

skills.name: Chinese modern woodcut
skills.thesis: A cheap block of wood and one knife can give a poor and angry public a picture of its own life and its own fight.
skills.summary: In 1931 Lu Xun urged young artists to learn the European expressionist woodcut of Kollwitz and Masereel. They cut black-and-white prints on cheap wood and printed many on thin paper, bold and rough.
use_cases: posters and covers on social themes
editorial images on history and labour

skills.name: Taller de Gráfica Popular linocut
skills.thesis: A print that a collective cuts quickly in cheap material can serve a political cause and reach a wide public.
skills.summary: A black-and-white print cut in linoleum or wood. The Taller de Gráfica Popular made leaflets, posters and portfolios for workers, unions and the state, in large black masses and white gouge lines.

skills.name: Pop screen print
skills.thesis: A mechanical image, repeated and coloured by hand in loud inks, makes the familiar new.
skills.summary: A photograph or a found image pulled through a silk screen in flat, bright inks, often with the black photo layer off register. Warhol made it a studio process in 1962; Corita Kent printed text and colour; the look stands for pop art.

skills.name: Psychedelic concert poster
skills.thesis: A poster that makes the viewer stop and decode it brings them into the dance before they read the date.
skills.summary: An offset-litho poster for a dance at the Fillmore or the Avalon, with lettering that melts to fill the shape and complementary colours that vibrate. Wes Wilson, Victor Moscoso, Rick Griffin and Mouse and Kelley made the run in 1966–1968.

skills.name: Xerox zine
skills.thesis: If a copier is the press, anyone can publish, and the rough marks of the copy are proof of independence.
skills.summary: A fanzine made with scissors, glue, a typewriter and a photocopier, in black toner on white office paper. Sniffin' Glue started in London in 1976; punk, hardcore and riot grrrl made the copy shop a press anyone could use.

skills.name: Chicha poster
skills.thesis: A fluorescent poster with big hand-drawn letters can call a crowd to a street concert at a very low cost.
skills.summary: A concert poster in fluorescent ink for chicha music. The maker draws big outlined letters and a tight border by hand, and prints in 2–5 loud flat colours on cheap paper.
use_cases: album covers for cumbia and psychedelic music

skills.name: Risograph print
skills.thesis: Bright spot inks that mix where they overlap, with a soft grain and a small shift, give a cheap print the warmth of a hand process.
skills.summary: A print from a stencil duplicator: a thermal head cuts a master and the drum pushes soy ink through it, one drum and one bright spot colour for each layer. Riso Kagaku sold it for schools and offices from 1986; from the 2000s, studios made its grain and misregister an art look.

skills.name: Victorian Web
skills.thesis: Ornament is value: every surface carries pattern, rule and flourish.
skills.summary: Dense ornament, engraved borders, high-contrast serif type, deep jewel colours, gold, dark wood and old paper. It recalls the 19th century and gives a page a proud, collected and gothic mood.
