pack.why: A thin, fine line family that pairs with fleuron ornaments.

ground.why: Victorian print put each page inside ruled borders, and the double rule in two inks is that frame.

skills.name: Art Nouveau (web)
skills.thesis: Ornament is not decoration added to a thing: the line of the plant grows into the structure of the page.
skills.summary: Whiplash curves, plant forms and hand-drawn lettering inside framed panels. It came from Paris, Brussels, Vienna and Glasgow around 1900. On screen it suits heritage, craft and botanical brands.

pack.why: A thin, even, round-ended line that follows the flowing stroke of a plant drawing.

ground.why: Art Nouveau posters and book pages hold the picture in a thin drawn frame on warm paper.

skills.name: De Stijl (web)
skills.thesis: Reduce form to the straight line and the primary colour, and a universal, harmonious order appears.
skills.summary: Horizontal and vertical black lines, flat fields of red, yellow and blue, and white space. It came from the Dutch group around Mondrian and Van Doesburg and reduces form to its basic parts.

pack.why: A strict, even line on a square grid with butt terminals: straight lines only, like the style itself.

ground.why: De Stijl divides the plane with black bars into fields of primary colour and white.

use_cases: bento-like dashboards with a strong identity

skills.name: Bauhaus
skills.thesis: Form follows function, and a small kit of circle, square and triangle in three primary colours is enough to make any object for mass production.
skills.summary: Primary-colour geometry, sans-serif lower-case type and strict horizontal and vertical axes with bold diagonals. It came from the Bauhaus school in Weimar, Dessau and Berlin, and it fused craft with industrial production.

pack.why: Solid forms with square corners and no round terminal: the cut-paper geometry of the workshop.

ground.why: The workshop kit is circle, square and triangle in the three primaries, with one black bar for direction.

skills.name: Constructivism (web)
skills.thesis: The page is a machine for persuasion: every element is a lever, and the diagonal gives it energy.
skills.summary: Diagonal compositions, heavy sans-serif type, photomontage and flat red, black and cream blocks. It came from the Soviet avant-garde and treats the page as a poster that makes a call to action.

pack.why: A solid, sharp-cornered family with butt terminals that reads as a stamp on a red block.

ground.why: Constructivist posters cut the page with a red wedge and a black diagonal beam.

skills.name: Art Deco (web)
skills.thesis: Luxury is order: the machine age gives ornament a strict, symmetric geometry that looks rich and modern at once.
skills.summary: Symmetric geometry, stepped forms, fan and sunburst motifs and gold lines on a dark ground. It came out of the 1925 Paris exposition and stands for luxury and speed.

pack.why: A thin, even line with sharp joins that matches the gold rule and the chamfered frame.

ground.why: Deco ornament is the sunburst: gold rays and stepped arcs that rise from one point.

skills.name: Mid-Century Modern
skills.thesis: Modernist form can be warm and humane when abstract shapes, natural materials and a small earth palette serve everyday life.
skills.summary: Organic and geometric shapes in mustard, teal, orange and walnut, with slab and geometric type and wide margins. It grew from Bauhaus in postwar America and Scandinavia, and it added warmth and play to modernist order.

pack.why: Solid forms with soft corners: the organic silhouette of the period, with no outline.

ground.why: Mid-century print sits on warm uncoated stock, with flat colour that soaks into the grain.

skills.name: Swiss International Style
skills.thesis: Design is a neutral carrier of information, and a mathematical grid makes that neutrality visible.
skills.summary: Asymmetric layouts on a mathematical grid, one neo-grotesque sans serif, flush-left text and objective photography. It came out of Zurich and Basel in the 1950s and became the default language of corporate modernism.

pack.why: A thin, even line on a strict grid with butt terminals: the icon as neutral information.

ground.why: The Swiss poster shows its column grid, and one red field marks the start of the read.

skills.name: Japanese Graphic Modernism
skills.thesis: A single symbolic form on a quiet grid carries the whole message, and Japanese and Latin letters share the page as equal graphic material.
skills.summary: Flat geometric forms in red and black, symbolic circles and triangles, soft colour bands, and dense kanji and katakana set against Latin type. It grew from the Japan Advertising Artists Club of 1951 and the Tokyo 1964 Olympic posters.

pack.why: Solid forms with square terminals and mitre corners: the circle, bar and triangle of a Gothic grid, with no soft edge.

ground.why: Japanese post-war posters use one large disc of red as the whole composition.

skills.name: Rams Functionalism (UI)
skills.thesis: Good design is as little design as possible: the product should be useful, understandable and honest, and then step back.
skills.summary: Quiet matt surfaces, a muted grey palette, one orange signal colour and controls that show what they do. It follows Dieter Rams and Braun and appears again in calculators, audio and phone interfaces.

pack.why: A thin, even line with a plain pictogram form, always shown with a label.

ground.why: The Braun product face is a field of speaker holes and one orange control.

skills.name: Pop Art (web)
skills.thesis: Mass culture is the subject: the comic, the ad and the label become art when you make them big, flat and loud.
skills.summary: Flat, saturated colour, thick outlines, halftone dots and repeated mass-media images. It came from Britain and the USA in the 1950s and 1960s and treats advertising and comics as high art.

pack.why: A bold outline with a flat fill that looks like a comic panel.

ground.why: Pop art enlarges the Ben-Day dots of comic print until the dots become the picture.

skills.name: Space Age Design
skills.thesis: The future is a place that people will visit, and a clean, rounded, machine-made form shows that the trip is safe and near.
skills.summary: White rounded forms, orbit rings, starbursts and wide extended type in cobalt, orange and silver. It started with Sputnik and peaked at Expo 67 Montreal and EXPO '70 Osaka, and it shows a confident future of monorails and rockets.

pack.why: Solid forms with round terminals on a circle tile: the moulded plastic of a capsule window, and metaphors (rocket, planet, satellite) that the era knew.

ground.why: Space-age graphics show a launch: rays and orbits that leave one point on the horizon.

use_cases: product launches with a playful future theme

skills.name: Psychedelic
skills.thesis: Design should alter perception, and a page that vibrates, flows and resists easy reading puts the viewer in an expanded state of mind.
skills.summary: Vibrating complementary colours, melting hand-drawn lettering and symmetrical swirls that fill the whole sheet. It came from San Francisco concert posters of 1966 to 1968, and it set out to reject the order of Swiss modernism.

pack.why: Heavy, swollen solid forms with no straight terminal: the weight of the poster lettering.

ground.why: Psychedelic posters fill the field with colour that turns around one centre until the eye moves with it.

skills.name: Georgian neoclassical manufacture
skills.thesis: A factory can make an object that looks like a work of antiquity: the form comes from the classical model, and the mould, the lathe and the die repeat it with a fine finish.
skills.summary: The household goods of the first English factories: mahogany furniture, creamware and jasperware, ormolu and Sheffield plate, all made in series from the classical models of the architect and the pattern book.
use_cases: period hardware for a Georgian or Regency house
a reissue of a classical lamp or vase
a still life with creamware and mahogany
a hardware schedule for a listed building

era_blend.note: A contemporary reinterpretation keeps the style when it keeps the forms and the materials.

skills.name: Shaker object
skills.thesis: An object that serves its use well is beautiful; the maker adds no ornament, shows each joint and makes each piece with honest care.
skills.summary: The plain household goods of the Shaker communities: ladder-back chairs, peg rails, oval boxes and chests of pine, maple and cherry, built for use with no applied ornament.
use_cases: a plain, handmade kitchen or hall
a reissue of a peg rail, a box or a chair
a still life of useful objects
a hardware schedule for a farmhouse

era_blend.note: A contemporary reinterpretation keeps the style when it keeps the forms and the materials.

skills.name: Victorian manufacture
skills.thesis: The machine makes ornament cheap, so each object can carry rich pattern, deep colour and heavy form as a sign of comfort and rank.
skills.summary: The household goods of the machine age in Britain: cast iron, pressed glass, deep-buttoned velvet and dark polished wood, with ornament added to each surface by the machine.
use_cases: period fittings for a Victorian terrace
a dark, rich library or parlour
a reissue of a roll-top bath or a pillar tap
a still life of pressed glass and brass

era_blend.note: A contemporary reinterpretation keeps the style when it keeps the forms and the materials.

skills.name: Arts and Crafts object
skills.thesis: A good object shows the hand and the material that made it: the joint, the hammer mark and the grain are the ornament, and the maker is a free craftsman.
skills.summary: The handmade household goods of the reform movement: oak furniture with exposed joints, hammered copper and iron, stoneware and wool, made in small workshops against the machine ornament of the age.
use_cases: hardware and furniture for an Arts and Crafts house
a handmade, earthy kitchen or study
a reissue of a copper lamp or an oak settle
a still life of stoneware and copper

era_blend.note: A contemporary reinterpretation keeps the style when it keeps the forms and the materials.

skills.name: Art Nouveau object
skills.thesis: An object grows like a plant: its structure and its ornament are one curved line, made by a craftsman from the best material.
skills.summary: Lamps, glass, furniture and fixtures drawn from the line of a plant stem: cast bronze, art glass, carved fruit wood and porcelain, with one long curve that joins structure and ornament.
use_cases: lighting and glass for a period or reissue interior
a still life for an antiques catalogue
hardware schedules for a restored townhouse
a brief for a hand-finished reissue

era_blend.note: A new object that quotes the curve and the glass keeps the style.

skills.name: Industrial utility product
skills.thesis: A tool-like object earns its form from the job it does and the strain it takes; any surface that does no work is left off.
skills.summary: Fixtures made for work, not for show: enamel shades, cage lamps, cast iron, steel lockers, conduit and brass ship hardware. The form follows the duty, and the finish is hard and repairable.
use_cases: lighting and hardware for a loft or a kitchen
a brief for reissued factory fixtures
a still life for a workshop-style shop
hardware schedules for a warehouse conversion

ornament_level.note: A trace of ornament comes only from repeated parts, such as a row of rivets.

era_blend.note: A contemporary object in the same duty and material keeps the style.

skills.name: Bauhaus product
skills.thesis: An everyday object is a model for the factory: its form comes from plain geometry, its material and its use, and ornament has no place on it.
skills.summary: The workshop objects of the Bauhaus: lamps, tea sets and chairs built from the sphere, the cylinder and the cone in nickel, chrome, opal glass and bent steel tube, as models for mass production.
use_cases: lighting and hardware for a modernist interior
a still life for a design museum shop
hardware schedules for a period flat

ornament_level.note: A trace of ornament comes only from repeated parts, such as rivets.

era_blend.note: A reissue or a new object in the same geometry keeps the style.

skills.name: Art Deco product
skills.thesis: Luxury can be geometric: a rare material, a precise machine line and a bold pattern make an object that looks rich and modern.
skills.summary: Rich, geometric objects of the jazz age: stepped forms, fans and sunbursts in chrome, ebony, lacquer, mirror and Bakelite, made by hand and by machine for a city luxury.
use_cases: lighting and hardware for a hotel or a cocktail bar
a brief for a deco reissue
a still life with mirror and chrome
hardware schedules for a period flat

era_blend.note: A contemporary object that quotes the fan, the step and the gloss keeps the style.

skills.name: Scandinavian modern product
skills.thesis: A good object is a plain tool for a person: it is made of local wood and wool, shaped to the hand and the body, and built to last for decades.
skills.summary: Everyday objects of bent birch, teak, oak and wool from the Nordic workshops: low, soft in outline and made for use. Craft joints are kept, and makers sell to ordinary homes.
use_cases: furniture and lamps for a warm modern home
a hardware and surface schedule for a Nordic flat
a still life of wood, wool and glass
product briefs for a reissue of a mid-century classic

ornament_level.note: A woven seat or a brass sleeve is the most that the style allows.

era_blend.note: A contemporary object may keep the joint and the taper and change the proportion.

skills.name: Streamline Moderne product
skills.thesis: A mass-made object should look as if it moves through air: a smooth shell, round corners and long lines show progress and sell.
skills.summary: Smooth, rounded objects that look fast: toasters, radios, lamps and chairs in chrome, aluminium, Bakelite and enamel, with long horizontal lines and speed stripes, made in mass series.
use_cases: kitchen objects and lighting for a retro-modern interior
a brief for a reissued appliance
a still life of chrome and enamel objects
hardware schedules for a diner or a station

era_blend.note: A contemporary object with the same shell, radius and stripe keeps the style.

skills.name: Mid-century modern product
skills.thesis: New materials from the war economy make a new kind of object: light, curved, bright and cheap enough for the new suburban home.
skills.summary: Post-war household objects of moulded plywood, fibreglass, steel rod and enamel, in organic curves and bright accents, made by American furniture firms and small Italian workshops.
use_cases: furniture and accessories for a retro-modern home
a still life with a shell chair, a clock and a pendant lamp
product briefs for a mid-century reissue
a hardware schedule for a period house

era_blend.note: A new object in a moulded shell on a slim base still belongs to the style.

skills.name: Japanese modern craft product
skills.thesis: A useful object made with skill from a local material is beautiful without ornament; the maker's hand and the material leave the only decoration.
skills.summary: Japanese household objects of bamboo, paper, clay, iron and plain wood: the mingei idea of beauty in ordinary things, joined to post-war modern design and light industrial series.
use_cases: objects for a calm, craft-led interior
a still life of bowls, paper and wood
product briefs for a craft collection
a hardware schedule for a Japanese-influenced flat

ornament_level.note: A trace of pattern comes only from the weave or the throwing rings.

era_blend.note: A contemporary piece may quote the method with a machine.

skills.name: Ulm and Braun functionalism
skills.thesis: A product is a system: it is as little design as possible, it explains its use, and it fits with its neighbours on a common grid.
skills.summary: Systematic household products of the Ulm school and the Braun firm: grey and white cases of aluminium and plastic, built on a grid, with controls that explain the object.
use_cases: product briefs in the style of a design-led electronics firm
a clean, grey and white object set for a modernist flat
a still life of shelf, radio, clock and lamp

ornament_level.note: Only a printed scale or a dial ring is allowed.

era_blend.note: A contemporary object may keep the grid and the plain case.

skills.name: Space Age pop product
skills.thesis: The new plastics free the form: one mould makes a whole object in one piece, and its colour and curve show a hopeful, fast, technical future.
skills.summary: The objects of the plastic age: chairs, lamps and tubs moulded in one piece from fibreglass, acrylic and ABS, with chrome and bright colour, in rounded forms that look like capsules, eggs and pods.
use_cases: product briefs for plastic furniture reissues
a still life for a design museum shop
a prop list for a 1960s film set

era_blend.note: A reissue keeps the style; a new object keeps only the one-piece mould and the colour.

skills.name: Memphis product
skills.thesis: An object is a toy for the mind: it joins cheap, bright materials with symbols and jokes, and it refuses the rule that good taste is quiet.
skills.summary: The objects of the Memphis group: bookcases, tables, lamps and ceramics built from bright laminate, terrazzo and coloured glass, in stacked geometric shapes with loud patterns.
use_cases: product briefs for a Memphis-inspired collection
a prop list for an 1980s set
a pattern study for a laminate range

era_blend.note: A reissue keeps the style; a new object keeps the stack of solids and the pattern.

skills.name: Contemporary craft product
skills.thesis: A good object is made by a person from one real material, and it gains value with use: its marks, its tone and its slow wear are the ornament.
skills.summary: The handmade object of the quiet home: stoneware with a speckled glaze, solid oak with an oiled finish, washed linen and unlacquered brass, made in small batches and left with the marks of the hand.
use_cases: a calm home or hotel moodboard
a product brief for a craft collection
a styled shelf or table for a still life
material schedules for a quiet interior

era_blend.note: A new object in this style is the norm; a reissue of a craft original is the faithful case.

skills.name: Super Normal product
skills.thesis: A good object is one that nobody notices: it does its job, it fits the hand and the room, and it needs no explanation or signature.
skills.summary: The anonymous everyday object: a chair, a clock, a kettle or a shelf in matte white plastic, pale wood and steel, drawn so that it looks right and leaves no trace of the designer.
use_cases: a calm flat or office moodboard
a clean still life for a catalogue
hardware schedules for a rental unit

era_blend.note: A contemporary object in this style is the norm; a reissue of a 1980s piece is the faithful case.

skills.name: Whalebone Stays
skills.thesis: A lady stands straight because her stays hold her straight, and the gown above shows the cone that they build.
skills.summary: The rigid bodice of the long eighteenth century. It was linen and silk stiffened with strips of whalebone and laced at the back. It pressed the torso into an upright cone under the gown.
use_cases: a costume brief for a period film
a museum label or object study
a historical reconstruction of court dress

ornament_level.note: Working stays are plain; court stays carry silk embroidery.

skills.name: Georgian Jewellery
skills.thesis: In candlelight a jewel must return the flame. A sheet of foil under the stone and a closed setting make a small gem glow like a large one.
skills.summary: Jewels of the Hanoverian reigns: foil-backed gems and paste in closed silver and gold settings, bright cut steel, pierced bows and flower sprays. They were made by hand to shine in candlelight.
use_cases: costume design for a Regency or Georgian drama
a museum label for a jewel of 1714 to 1837
an image prompt for a candlelit period portrait

ornament_level.note: Foil and cut steel give the ornament; plain mourning pieces sit at the low end.

skills.name: Rococo court dress
skills.thesis: A court gown shows rank by the width of the skirt, the weight of the silk and the hours of hand work in the trim.
skills.summary: The court dress of Louis XV: a wide-hipped silk gown with Watteau back pleats, lace ruffles and flower brocade, copied at the courts of Europe.
use_cases: a period costume brief for a film about Louis XV or Louis XVI
a museum label for an 18th century gown
a fashion image prompt for a Rococo ball

ornament_level.note: A day gown is lightly trimmed; a court gown carries lace and embroidery on every edge.

skills.name: Breguet classical watch
skills.thesis: A fine watch shows its worth by exact work and a quiet face, so each part is plain, thin and cut by hand.
skills.summary: The plain, exact gold watch that Abraham-Louis Breguet made in Paris from 1780. It has an engine-turned silver dial, blued steel hands with an open tip and a coin-edge case. Its movement set the rule for the dress watch.
use_cases: a period prop for a drama of the 1790s
a dress watch brief in the classical mould
a museum note on early precision watches
an image prompt for a gold pocket watch

skills.name: Empire line dress
skills.thesis: After the Revolution, a dress drops the hoop and the stays and shows a light, straight line from a waist under the bust.
skills.summary: The high-waisted dress after the French Revolution: a light, straight muslin gown that falls from a seam under the bust, like Greek dress.
use_cases: a period costume brief for a Regency film or play
a bridal dress with a high waist
a fashion image prompt for a 1810 ball
a museum label for an early 19th century gown

ornament_level.note: A day dress carries white embroidery at the hem only; an evening gown may carry metal thread.

skills.name: English bespoke tailoring
skills.thesis: A man's suit is drafted for one body, built inside with canvas, and shown outside by a plain surface and a line with no fuss.
skills.summary: The cut of the London tailor: a plain, dark suit in fine worsted, drafted for one body and built by hand on hair canvas.
use_cases: a brief for a made-to-measure menswear label
a period costume brief for a Victorian or Edwardian gentleman
a fashion image prompt for a tailor's atelier
a study note on the history of the suit

ornament_level.note: The suit is plain; a lining, a button or a pocket square carries the colour.

skills.name: Victorian Sentimental Jewellery
skills.thesis: A jewel carries a memory: it holds a lock of hair, a name or a likeness close to the body.
skills.summary: Jewels that hold a person or a feeling: lockets, hair work, cameos, snakes, hearts, and black jet for mourning. They were made in gold, jet and pearl in Britain after 1837.
use_cases: costume design for a Victorian drama
a museum label for a mourning or love token
a heritage locket for a modern wearer
an image prompt for a Victorian portrait

ornament_level.note: A mourning piece is plain black; a love token carries more carving and pearls.

skills.name: Victorian Corsetry
skills.thesis: The dress is only as good as the foundation: a firm, shaped corset gives the hourglass that the outer cloth then covers.
skills.summary: The factory-made corset of the Victorian age. It has coutil cloth, a steel busk, metal eyelets and spring-steel bones, shaped with gussets into an hourglass. It was worn under the crinoline and the bustle.
use_cases: a museum label or object study

ornament_level.note: The day corset is plain; the evening corset carries lace and flossing.

skills.name: Victorian millinery
skills.thesis: A hat completes a lady's dress, and the trim shows the skill of the milliner.
skills.summary: The women's hats and bonnets of Queen Victoria's reign. A wire and buckram frame carried silk, velvet, felt or straw, trimmed by hand with ribbon, flowers and feathers. The shape followed the dress, from deep poke bonnet to small tilted hat.
use_cases: a costume brief for a Victorian drama
a hat design study or a museum label
a fashion image prompt for an 1860s woman

ornament_level.note: A plain walking hat has one bow; an evening bonnet carries flowers, lace and beads.

skills.name: American pocket watch
skills.thesis: A watch is a public tool. Each part is made to a gauge, the face is clear and the case lasts for decades.
skills.summary: The plain, tough pocket watch that American factories made from 1850 with machine-cut interchangeable parts. It has a white enamel dial with black Arabic numerals and a gold-filled or silver case. The rail grade movement kept time for the railroads.
use_cases: a prop for a western or a railway drama
a collector guide to antique watches
a vintage object prompt for a pocket watch

skills.name: Victorian boot
skills.thesis: A Victorian woman covers the ankle, so the boot is the shoe of every day and the cloth upper shows the cut of the last.
skills.summary: The ankle boot of Victorian dress. It has a kid or cloth upper, a row of buttons or a lace front, an elastic side gusset, and a small stacked heel.
use_cases: a period costume brief for a Victorian film
a museum label for a 19th century boot

ornament_level.note: Day boots are plain; evening boots carry embroidery or a cloth top.

skills.name: Malletier luggage
skills.thesis: A trunk is a small room that a traveller trusts, and each part of it serves a use.
skills.summary: The travel trunks of the French malletier. A light wooden frame carries coated canvas or leather, bound with brass and fitted to its use. The flat lid stacks in a ship's hold or on a train.
use_cases: a costume prop for a period film
a luggage design brief with a heritage look
a museum label for a travel trunk

ornament_level.note: A plain grey trunk is the base; stripes and a monogram add pattern.

skills.name: Crinoline and bustle dress
skills.thesis: The skirt is the dress: a steel cage and then a bustle carry yards of silk, and the couture house sets the shape each season.
skills.summary: The dress of the Second Empire: a vast bell skirt on a steel cage from 1856, then a bustle from 1870, in strong silk.
use_cases: a period costume brief for a Victorian drama

skills.name: Power dressing
skills.thesis: Dress is a uniform of authority. A woman at work wears the wide shoulder and the sharp line of the man's suit, and so claims the same standing.
skills.summary: The working woman's suit of the 1980s. It has a tailored jacket with wide padded shoulders, a skirt or trousers in wool and a silk blouse with a bow. The colour is strong and plain.
use_cases: a costume brief for a 1980s office drama
a study note on gender and dress at work

skills.name: Streetwear
skills.thesis: Dress comes from the street and the club: the wearer joins a group by a plain, comfortable garment that carries a mark.
skills.summary: The casual dress that grew from surf, skate, hip-hop and sport clubs from 1980. It has the graphic T-shirt, the hoodie, the baggy jean, the nylon trouser and the cap, sold in small drops.
use_cases: a casual clothing line and drop
a costume brief for a youth film
a study note on subculture and brands

skills.name: Japanese avant-garde fashion
skills.thesis: A garment is a space around the body, not a copy of it: it can be loose, torn, uneven and black, and still be beautiful.
skills.summary: The black, loose and torn clothes that Rei Kawakubo, Yohji Yamamoto and Issey Miyake showed in Paris from 1981. The clothes are oversized, asymmetric and unfinished, with no wish to show the body.
use_cases: a costume for a dark, quiet film
a collection brief with sculptural cut
a study note on 1980s Paris fashion

skills.name: Designer Logo Underwear
skills.thesis: A basic garment gains value from its maker's name: the plain brief stays plain, and the label on the band carries the brand.
skills.summary: Plain cotton underwear with the name of a fashion designer on the waistband. In 1982 a fashion house put its name on a basic brief, and underwear became a branded, advertised object.
use_cases: a flat product shot of branded basics
a museum label or object study

ornament_level.note: The name on the band is the only ornament.

skills.name: Swiss plastic pop watch
skills.thesis: A watch can be a fashion accessory that one wears for a season. The maker sells colour and a pattern at a price that allows many watches.
skills.summary: A cheap Swiss quartz watch in a plastic case with a bright pattern. The maker sells it as an accessory and changes it each season. The Swatch line of 1983 set it.
use_cases: a prop for a film set in the 1980s
an image prompt for a stack of plastic watches

skills.name: Underwear as Outerwear
skills.thesis: What was hidden is now the dress: a corset, a bra or a slip shown in the open gives the body a built, public form.
skills.summary: Designers of the 1980s and 1990s took the corset, the cone bra and the slip out of the wardrobe and put them on the street. The bodices were boned satin and wool, worn as tops, jackets and dresses.
use_cases: a runway or editorial fashion brief
a museum label or exhibition study
a fashion image prompt for a corset look

ornament_level.note: A tailored corset is plain; a couture one carries beads, lace and embroidery.

skills.name: Logomania
skills.thesis: The mark of the maker is the ornament, and the wearer shows a place in the world by it.
skills.summary: Accessories that carry a brand mark on the whole surface. Examples are a monogram repeat on coated canvas, large metal letters on a belt and a logo on a scarf. The mark is the design, and it shows status.
use_cases: a fashion image prompt with a 1990s status look
a brief for a logo repeat on leather goods
a study of brand marks in dress
a street-fashion collection with custom logo prints

ornament_level.note: The mark covers the whole surface; a quiet version keeps one letter on the clasp.

skills.name: Sneaker culture
skills.thesis: In this style the shoe is a signal: colour, release and story matter more than function, and an owner shows taste by what is rare.
skills.summary: The sneaker as a badge. It is a leather high-top in team colours with a bold brand mark, an air-cushioned sole and a limited release. Players, rappers and collectors wear it.
use_cases: a costume brief for a 1980s or 1990s street scene
a product image prompt for a collector shoe
a note on resale and drops

ornament_level.note: Ornament is a mark and a colour block; no other decoration is needed.

skills.name: Biodesign Car
skills.thesis: A car for everyday life has the forms of a plant or an animal. It is round, smooth and friendly, with no hard edge and no sign of a machine.
skills.summary: The soft, organic car of the 1990s. A rounded one-box body with an oval face, body-colour bumpers and large clear lamps. The cabin is soft cloth and curved plastic.
use_cases: an image prompt for a small rounded car
a design lesson on soft form

ornament_level.note: The form is the ornament: round shapes and one bright colour.

skills.name: Minimalist fashion
skills.thesis: After the show of the 1980s, dress is plain: a perfect cut in fine cloth needs no ornament.
skills.summary: The plain, quiet dress of the 1990s. It has clean lines, fine cloth in grey, black and white, no logo and no trim, and a cut that does all the work.

skills.name: It bag
skills.thesis: A single bag can carry the whole fashion of a season, and its scarcity is part of its design.
skills.summary: The handbag that a house makes as the object of one season. It has a new shape in a bold material, a small run and a waiting list. A star carries it, and the street copies it within months.
use_cases: a fashion image prompt for a 2000s star look
a brief for one hero accessory in a collection
a study of the launch of a handbag
a window display of a seasonal bag

ornament_level.note: A plain version has gilt hardware only; the full version is covered in beads or skin.

skills.name: Retro Revival Car
skills.thesis: A new car can borrow the face of a loved old one. It must keep the key shapes and add the comfort and safety of today.
skills.summary: A new car with the shape of an old one: a round Beetle, a small Mini or a long-bonnet Mustang. It has chrome trim, round lamps and a painted dashboard.
use_cases: a lifestyle advertisement for a heritage-inspired car
a car interior concept with a painted dash
an image prompt for a retro new car
a design history lesson on nostalgia

ornament_level.note: Chrome and paint panels carry the old look; keep the rest plain.

skills.name: Shapewear and Seamless
skills.thesis: Shaping can be soft: a knit with elastane holds the body without bone and leaves no line under the cloth.
skills.summary: Smooth, bone-free underwear of stretch nylon and elastane: control-top tights, high-waist briefs and bodysuits. They are made seamless or with bonded edges, so that they hold the body and show no line under the dress.
use_cases: a product page for smooth underwear
a technical specification of a knit
a history of the girdle to shapewear

ornament_level.note: The style is plain; a small print or lace edge is the limit.

skills.name: Techwear
skills.thesis: The city is a hard environment. Dress for it as for a mountain, with a shell, a system of pockets and straps, and a black, sealed surface.
skills.summary: City dress made of technical outdoor cloth. A black membrane shell with taped seams, many pockets, straps and quick buckles, with a cut for motion in the street.
use_cases: a product brief for a technical city jacket
an image prompt for a night city scene
a costume brief for a near-future film
a study note on gear in dress

ornament_level.note: Hardware, straps and pockets serve as ornament; the cloth stays plain.

skills.name: Quiet luxury fashion
skills.thesis: Real luxury is quiet. It shows in the touch of the cloth and the fit of the cut, and only a person who knows will see it.
skills.summary: The logo-free, high-cost dress of the 2000s and after. It uses cashmere, loden and fine wool in neutral colours, with perfect cut and hand finish. The price is in the cloth and not in a mark.
use_cases: a luxury knitwear or coat line brief
a fashion image prompt for a calm, rich look
a styling guide for a wardrobe
a study note on the turn from logos

skills.name: Stealth luxury accessory
skills.thesis: True luxury has no mark: the quality of the material and the work is the only sign.
skills.summary: Plain, unmarked accessories of the finest leather and cashmere: a tote with no logo, a slim wallet, a raw-edged scarf. Only those who know the cloth, the cut and the stitch can read the price.
use_cases: a fashion image prompt for a quiet-luxury look
a brief for leather goods with no logo
a shop display of fine basics

ornament_level.note: The surface stays bare; the stitch is the only detail.

skills.name: Electric Minimal Car
skills.thesis: An electric car has no engine to show. It is a smooth, quiet shell with a bare cabin, and a screen holds all of the controls.
skills.summary: The quiet electric car. A smooth, closed body with no grille, flush handles and a glass roof. The cabin is bare, in recycled cloth, with one large screen in place of dials.
use_cases: a launch image for an electric car
a car interior concept for a minimal cabin
an image prompt for a modern EV
a product page for a charging service

ornament_level.note: The style has almost no ornament; a thin lamp line is the only mark.

skills.name: Smartwatch
skills.thesis: A watch is the screen on the wrist. It shows the time, messages and health data. The user changes the face as often as a shirt.
skills.summary: A watch that is a small touch screen computer. It has a rounded case in aluminium or steel, a glass screen, a digital crown and a soft strap. The Apple Watch of 2015 set the type.
use_cases: a product shot of a wearable device
an image prompt for a smartwatch on a wrist

skills.name: Gorpcore
skills.thesis: The best dress is the kind you would take on a hike: it looks plain, it is tough, and its colours come from the trail.
skills.summary: Trail and camp gear worn in the city as fashion. A fleece, a bright shell, a down vest and ripstop trousers, with no wish to look polished.
use_cases: a styling brief for an outdoor-gear collaboration
an image prompt for a street-style scene
a trend note on outdoor dress in the city
a product brief for a fleece line

ornament_level.note: Colour blocks and gear details carry the ornament; the cloth stays plain.

skills.name: Jōmon pottery
skills.thesis: A pot is a coiled and fired form that carries the marks of its making: the cord, the cut and the clay itself are the ornament.
skills.summary: The oldest pottery of Japan. Hunter-gatherers coiled a coarse clay into deep pots, pressed twisted cord into the wet wall, and fired the pots in an open bonfire.
use_cases: a museum label for prehistoric Japanese ware
a sculptural vessel with a strong cord texture
a prompt for an archaeology scene with fired clay

wall_thickness.note: Jōmon walls are thick and uneven; they are never thin.

skills.name: Greek black-figure pottery
skills.thesis: A pot is a surface for story: black silhouettes on red clay, made sharp with incised lines, tell a myth in frieze after frieze.
skills.summary: Greek vases in which the painter draws figures in a black gloss slip on the red clay and cuts the details with a sharp point. A three-stage firing makes the black and the red.
use_cases: a museum or educational plate on Greek pottery
a myth scene on a vessel
an amphora or krater in a classical interior prompt

skills.name: Babylonian glazed brick
skills.thesis: A mud-brick city wall becomes a royal image when each brick is moulded, glazed blue and fired, so that the animals of the gods stand in a row along the road.
skills.summary: Moulded bricks of fired clay that Neo-Babylonian builders glazed in blue, yellow and white. They set the bricks into walls of lions, bulls and dragons on the gates and the Processional Way of Babylon.
use_cases: a museum label or a reconstruction image of the Ishtar Gate
a gate or wall design with a repeated animal frieze
a prompt for an ancient city in glazed blue brick

wall_thickness.note: A whole brick is about 100 mm thick; the knob counts the glazed face layer up to its top of 40 mm.

skills.name: Greek red-figure pottery
skills.thesis: A vase is a field for the drawn human body: the figure stays the colour of the clay and the brush line gives it weight, movement and feeling.
skills.summary: Greek vases in which the background is black gloss and the figures keep the red of the clay. The painter draws the inner lines with a brush, so the figures look rounder and freer.
use_cases: a museum label for classical Greek vases
a figure scene on a cup or a krater
an educational image of Greek daily life on pottery

skills.name: Qin terracotta warriors
skills.thesis: An emperor takes an army of clay into the grave, and a factory system of standard parts and hand finish makes each soldier a different man.
skills.summary: Life-size grey terracotta soldiers, horses and officials that the workshops of the First Emperor made for his tomb. Each body is built from standard parts, and the head is finished by hand.
use_cases: a museum label or exhibition text
a prompt for a life-size clay soldier
a game asset in unglazed grey terracotta
a sculpture brief for a rank of figures

wall_thickness.note: The torso wall is 2 to 4 cm; the legs are solid.

skills.name: Roman terra sigillata
skills.thesis: A fine slip, not a glaze, gives the red shine: the potter sorts the clay by particle size, paints the thin top layer on the pot, and fires it in clean air.
skills.summary: Red-gloss tableware of the Roman world. Potters at Arezzo press fine clay into stamped moulds, coat the pieces with a slip of very small particles, and fire them to a glossy coral red.
use_cases: a museum label on Roman tableware
a set or scene prompt for a Roman dining room

wall_thickness.note: Thin walls are the sign of good sigillata.

skills.name: Tang sancai figures
skills.thesis: A tomb figure shows the luxury of the living court in clay, and a lead glaze in three colours makes the animal or the lady glow.
skills.summary: Tomb figures of white earthenware under lead glazes in amber, green and cream that run into each other. Court ladies, Sogdian grooms, camels, horses and guardians show the life of the Silk Road.
use_cases: a prompt for a glazed horse or camel
a decorative figure in warm lead glaze colours
a game asset of Tang tomb goods

skills.name: Abbasid lustreware
skills.thesis: A cheap clay pot can shine like metal when a white tin glaze and a thin film of reduced silver and copper turn into a mirror of gold.
skills.summary: The first pottery with a metallic sheen. Potters in Abbasid Iraq painted copper and silver oxides over an opaque white tin glaze and fired them in smoke to a gold-brown shine.
use_cases: a museum plate on early Islamic ceramics
a bowl or tile with a gold-brown metallic shine
a prompt for a medieval Near Eastern interior

skills.name: Ding white ware
skills.thesis: A white body and a clear ivory glaze are enough: the beauty is the thin wall, the carved line and the quiet tone.
skills.summary: Thin ivory-white porcelain of the Northern Song court. The potters of Ding carve or mould fine plant designs under a clear glaze and fire the bowls rim down, so they bind the bare rim with metal.
use_cases: a museum label on Song white ware
a minimal plating prompt for a tasting menu

wall_thickness.note: The thin wall is the mark of the style.

skills.name: Jian tenmoku ware
skills.thesis: A bowl for whisked white tea must be dark, so that the foam shows; the kiln, not the brush, makes the pattern in an iron-rich glaze.
skills.summary: Dark stoneware tea bowls of the Song dynasty. A thick iron-rich glaze runs down the cone-shaped bowl in streaks and spots and pools in a bead at the foot.
use_cases: a still-life prompt with a dark tea bowl
a glaze brief for iron-rich reduction glazes
a museum label for a Song tea bowl

wall_thickness.note: Jian bowls are thick for the size; the wall holds the heat of the tea.

skills.name: Goryeo celadon
skills.thesis: A pot is a clear green lens over a drawing: the glaze is almost transparent and the inlaid slip line shows through it like ink in water.
skills.summary: Korean celadon of the Goryeo kingdom. A thin, clear grey-green glaze covers a fine body, and potters inlay white and black slip into incised lines to make a pattern under the glaze.
use_cases: a vase with an inlaid pattern for a quiet interior
a museum label on Korean medieval ceramics
a prompt for a crane motif in green glaze

skills.name: Longquan celadon
skills.thesis: A vessel reaches beauty when the glaze alone makes it: a thick, quiet green like jade that hides all other ornament.
skills.summary: Green-glazed stoneware and porcelain from the kilns of Longquan. Potters built up thick layers of glaze that fire to a soft jade-green, with a plain form that gives the glaze all the beauty.
use_cases: a quiet vase for a calm interior
a museum label on Song and Yuan celadon
a prompt for a pale green glaze study

skills.name: Islamic tile mosaic
skills.thesis: A building surface becomes a woven pattern of light and colour when many small tiles in turquoise, cobalt and black are cut to fit one geometric plan.
skills.summary: Wall and dome cladding that the Seljuk and Timurid potters made from glazed tiles in one colour. They cut each tile into small shapes and set the pieces together in a geometric or calligraphic pattern.
use_cases: a mosque or madrasa portal in tile
a geometric tile pattern brief with a closed colour set
a museum label on medieval Islamic tile work

wall_thickness.note: Cut tesserae are 8 to 20 mm thick; a lustre wall tile is about 12 mm.

skills.name: Hispano-Moresque lustreware
skills.thesis: A plain earthenware dish can serve a king when a white glaze, a gold lustre and a heraldic crest cover it in one dense pattern.
skills.summary: Spanish tin-glazed earthenware with a gold-copper lustre, made first by Muslim potters and later by Christian ones. Heraldic shields, plant scrolls and cobalt blue cover large dishes and tall jars.
use_cases: a large wall dish with heraldic pattern
a museum label on Spanish medieval ceramics
a prompt for a gold and blue dish in a castle interior

skills.name: Zellige
skills.thesis: Hand-cut pieces of one-colour glazed clay make a pattern that is exact in its geometry and alive in its surface.
skills.summary: Moroccan tile work in which a potter glazes a square tile in one colour, fires it, and then chisels it by hand into small pieces. A worker sets the pieces face down to make a geometric mosaic.
triggers: glazed clay tile in plain colours
use_cases: a kitchen or bathroom wall in plain hand-made tile
a courtyard or fountain brief in Moroccan style
a geometric mosaic brief with an 8-point star

ornament_level.note: Plain field tiles keep the low end of the range.

skills.name: Yuan and Ming blue-and-white porcelain
skills.thesis: Cobalt blue painted straight on white porcelain and sealed under a clear glaze gives a lasting picture that cannot rub or fade.
skills.summary: White porcelain painted in cobalt blue under a clear glaze. Jingdezhen potters made it in the Yuan dynasty and refined it for the Ming court into the best-known ceramic of the world.
use_cases: a vase or jar with a blue pattern on white
a museum label on Chinese export and court porcelain
a prompt for a classical Chinese interior

skills.name: Joseon buncheong
skills.thesis: A plain grey stoneware gains life when a white slip is brushed, stamped or carved on it by a free hand with no fear of the rough.
skills.summary: Korean grey stoneware covered with white slip and a thin clear glaze. Potters stamp, carve, brush and paint the slip with bold and free patterns. The result is rustic, direct and lively.
use_cases: a rustic jar or bottle with a slip pattern
a museum label on early Joseon ceramics
a prompt for a free brush pattern on grey clay

skills.name: Rhenish salt-glaze stoneware
skills.thesis: A dense stoneware pot needs no lining, because a handful of salt thrown into the hot kiln gives it a skin that keeps out water and does not taste of lead.
skills.summary: Hard grey stoneware that the potters of the Rhineland fired to about 1250 °C and glazed with salt. The jugs, bottles and storage jars are tough, waterproof and ready for the cellar.
use_cases: a period prompt for a cellar, a tavern or a kitchen of the 16th century
a museum label on German stoneware
a brief for a rustic jug with relief and salt glaze

wall_thickness.note: Stoneware holds a thin wall; a Bartmann jug is thinner than earthenware of the same size.

skills.name: Liuli glazed roof tile
skills.thesis: A roof tile is a sign of rank: its colour, its ridge figures and its curved line tell the viewer which hall is for the emperor.
skills.summary: Glazed roof tiles in yellow, green and blue that the imperial kilns made for the palaces and temples of Beijing. Rank and meaning decide the colour: imperial yellow covers the main halls of the Forbidden City.
use_cases: an image of a Chinese palace or temple with the right roof colour
a tile or roof-detail brief with glazed ridge animals
a label on Ming and Qing glazed architectural ceramics

ornament_level.note: The rank of the hall sets the colour and the number of ridge figures.

wall_thickness.note: Tile thickness is 2 to 3 cm; a ridge beast has a thicker wall of 3 to 4 cm.

skills.name: Della Robbia relief
skills.thesis: Sculpture in clay becomes lasting and bright when a white tin glaze covers it, so that a church relief shines and resists rain like marble.
skills.summary: Glazed terracotta reliefs that Luca della Robbia and his family made in Florence. White figures stand on a blue ground inside a frame of painted fruit and leaves.
use_cases: a museum label or an image brief for a Renaissance glazed relief
a church or loggia front with a glazed roundel
a plan for a modern relief in white glaze on blue

ornament_level.note: The relief is white on blue; add colour only in the frame.

wall_thickness.note: Relief clay is 30 to 50 mm thick and hollow at the back; the knob stops at 40 mm.

skills.name: Albarello apothecary ware
skills.thesis: A drug jar must tell a clerk which drug it holds, so the label is part of the pot: a painted cartouche on a clean white tin glaze.
skills.summary: Tin-glazed earthenware jars and jugs that Italian potters made for the shelf of the pharmacy. The waisted albarello holds dry drugs, and the label names the drug in a painted cartouche.
use_cases: a set dressing for a pharmacy or a still life of the Renaissance
a museum label on Italian maiolica
a kitchen jar set that borrows the albarello waist

skills.name: Iznik pottery
skills.thesis: A bright garden of flowers can be painted flat and sharp on a white body, and it stays fresh under a clear glass-like glaze.
skills.summary: Ottoman court pottery with a white quartz body, a white slip and a clear glaze. Painters used cobalt, turquoise, green and a thick tomato red for tulips, carnations and saz leaves.
use_cases: a bright floral dish or plate
a museum label on Ottoman ceramics
a prompt for a flower motif in blue, turquoise and red

skills.name: Istoriato maiolica
skills.thesis: A dish can be a painting: the whole surface becomes a scene of myth, scripture or history, painted in many colours on white tin glaze.
skills.summary: Italian tin-glazed earthenware painted with a whole story, called istoriato. Painters copied scenes from prints and fresco and filled the full surface of a dish with figures in colour.
use_cases: a large wall plate with a story scene
a museum label on Renaissance Italian ceramics
a prompt for a mythic painted dish

skills.name: Yixing zisha teapot
skills.thesis: A teapot for steeped tea needs no glaze: a dense, porous clay keeps the tea hot and the taste pure, and the pot improves with use.
skills.summary: Small unglazed teapots in the red-brown stoneware of Yixing. The potter builds them by hand, and the porous wall takes a patina from the tea that it holds.
use_cases: a product brief for an unglazed tea pot
a still-life with a tea set in earth tones
a label for a Qing teapot

wall_thickness.note: Zisha walls are thin; the wall stays under 5 mm.

skills.name: Iznik tiles
skills.thesis: A court tile is a garden in glaze: the painter shows tulips, carnations and leaves in clear colours on a white ground, and the glaze gives them depth.
skills.summary: Painted wall tiles that the Iznik kilns made for the Ottoman court. A white quartz body takes a white slip, a free painting of flowers in cobalt, turquoise, green and raised red, and a clear glaze.
use_cases: a mosque or palace wall in Ottoman tile
a floral tile pattern brief with a white ground
a museum label on Ottoman court ceramics

skills.name: Azulejo
skills.thesis: A wall becomes a picture when many square tiles are painted as one scene on a white tin glaze.
skills.summary: Painted tin-glazed tiles that cover the walls of churches, palaces and streets in Portugal and Spain. A painter works in blue or in many colours on a white glaze, and one scene runs across many tiles.
use_cases: a church, cloister or street facade clad in painted tile
a kitchen or stair wall in painted tile
a museum label on Iberian tile painting

skills.name: Kraak porcelain
skills.thesis: One cobalt blue on a white porcelain body, ordered in panels that a quick painter can repeat, makes a pattern that a whole continent wants to buy.
skills.summary: Thin blue-and-white export porcelain from Jingdezhen. Plates and bowls have a rim in 8 panels that frame plants and sacred objects, and a central scene. Merchants of Portugal and the Netherlands sold it across Europe.
use_cases: a pattern brief for a panelled blue-and-white plate
a Dutch Golden Age still-life prompt
a museum label on export porcelain

skills.name: Mino tea ceramics
skills.thesis: Japanese potters of the Momoyama period make their own tea ware: thick glaze, free brush and a form that is bent on purpose.
skills.summary: Japanese stoneware for the tea room from the kilns of Mino. The first white Shino glaze, the green Oribe glaze and the black Setoguro glaze go on bold forms with bold painted lines.
use_cases: a glaze brief for white feldspar and copper green glazes
a tea-room still life with bold Japanese ceramics
a catalogue entry for Momoyama stoneware

wall_thickness.note: Mino walls are thick enough to carry a glaze coat up to 2 mm.

skills.name: Raku tea bowl
skills.thesis: A tea bowl need not be thrown, round or bright: hand-built, a little uneven and fired fast, it can calm the mind and ask nothing of the eye.
skills.summary: Hand-built, low-fired tea bowls that Chōjirō made in Kyoto for the tea master Sen no Rikyū. The potter pulls each bowl from the hot kiln, and the glaze is black or red.
use_cases: a tea-room still life with a hand-built bowl
a glaze and form brief for a hand-built bowl
a museum label for Momoyama tea ware

wall_thickness.note: The raku wall is thick on purpose; it keeps the tea hot and holds in the hand.

skills.name: Delft tiles
skills.thesis: A cheap square tile and a quick brush make a clean, washable wall that still holds a small picture in each unit.
skills.summary: Small square tin-glazed tiles that Dutch potteries made by the million for walls, kitchens and fireplaces. Each tile holds one small picture in blue or purple and a corner motif, and a set of tiles makes a wall.
use_cases: a Dutch kitchen or fireplace wall in blue tile
a grid of small hand-painted tiles with a motif in each
a museum label on Dutch tin-glazed tiles

skills.name: Delftware
skills.thesis: A cheap local clay looks like Chinese porcelain when a white tin glaze covers it and a fast brush paints it in cobalt blue.
skills.summary: Tin-glazed earthenware that the potters of Delft made after 1640 to copy Chinese blue-and-white porcelain. A thin buff body takes a thick white tin glaze and cobalt painting in one firing.
triggers: blue and white tiles and plates
use_cases: a tableware pattern brief in Dutch blue and white
a still-life or interior prompt with period plates
a museum label on Dutch tin-glazed earthenware

wall_thickness.note: Earthenware plates are thicker than the porcelain that they copy.

skills.name: Joseon moon jar
skills.thesis: A form that is round and nearly empty, white and warm, can hold more than a painted jar because it shows the breath of its making.
skills.summary: A large round jar of white porcelain from Joseon Korea. Two bowls are thrown, joined at the waist and glazed milk-white, so the form is full, a little off-round and quite plain.
use_cases: a plain white vase in a quiet interior
a museum label on Joseon white porcelain
a sculptural jar in a calm still life

wall_thickness.note: The jar is thick for a porcelain; the wall stays at 6 to 10 mm.

skills.name: Kyo-yaki overglaze
skills.thesis: A Kyoto potter can make tea ware as rich as a screen painting: a thin body, a pale crackle glaze, enamel and gold.
skills.summary: Fine pottery from Kyoto that Nonomura Ninsei made at the kiln of Omuro. A thin crackle glaze takes enamel colours and gold in painted designs of flowers, hills and seasons.
use_cases: a brief for an ornate Japanese tea jar
a decorative object with seasonal flower painting
a museum label for Kyoto pottery

wall_thickness.note: Kyoto wares are thin; thicker walls break the line of the painted jar.

skills.name: Kakiemon and Imari export porcelain
skills.thesis: A white porcelain can carry two styles of decoration: a spare picture in the open white, and a crowded design in blue, red and gold.
skills.summary: Japanese export porcelain from Arita. Kakiemon ware has a milk-white body and a spare, asymmetric overglaze design; Imari ware is dense, with blue under the glaze and red and gold over it.
use_cases: a spare coloured plate on milk-white porcelain
a museum label on Japanese export porcelain
a prompt for a 17th-century collector's cabinet

skills.name: English slipware
skills.thesis: A country potter needs no costly colour: red clay, white slip from a quill, and a lead glaze give a bold picture.
skills.summary: Red earthenware that English country potters covered with a clear lead glaze and trailed with cream and brown slip. Large dishes, posset pots and jugs carry bold pictures and rhymes.
use_cases: a farm-kitchen set dressing of the 17th century
a museum label on a trailed dish
a rustic bowl or jug brief with a hand-drawn motif

skills.name: Famille rose (Qing)
skills.thesis: A white porcelain glaze takes opaque enamel like a canvas, and a pink from gold lets the painter model soft flesh, petals and clouds.
skills.summary: Qing porcelain painted in opaque enamels over a fired glaze. A pink made from gold gives the style its name. The imperial kilns of Jingdezhen made the finest vases and bowls.
use_cases: a vase or jar with delicate pink enamel painting
a museum label for Chinese overglaze enamel

wall_thickness.note: A porcelain vase of this style has a thin wall; a thick wall breaks the effect.

skills.name: Meissen baroque porcelain
skills.thesis: Once Europe can make porcelain, it shows the fact: a white body that is modelled in a sculptural mass and painted in every enamel colour.
skills.summary: The first true European hard-paste porcelain. The factory at Meissen paints it with a bright enamel palette, models it in full baroque relief, and gilds the edge, for the court of Saxony.
use_cases: a museum label on early European porcelain

skills.name: Rococo porcelain figures
skills.thesis: A porcelain figure is a toy for the table of a prince: white, glossy and light, it turns a scene of court play into a small, bright piece of theatre.
skills.summary: Small hand-painted porcelain figures of lovers, shepherds, harlequins and monkeys, made for the dessert table of the court. They are white, glossy and light, in S-curves with lace, flowers and gilt.
use_cases: a museum label for a Meissen figure
a table or dessert scene prompt
a collector's brief for a hard-paste figure
a set dressing prop for a court scene

skills.name: Georgian porcelain tea service
skills.thesis: English potters make a full tea table in porcelain for the new tea drinkers: a set of matched pieces, with a Chinese or a European look.
skills.summary: The first English porcelain tea services. A tea set of handleless bowls, a pot, jugs and slop bowls in soft-paste or bone china, with blue painting, enamel flowers and gilt rims.
use_cases: a period interior with a tea table
a set of matched porcelain for a product brief
a museum label for English porcelain

skills.name: Staffordshire figures
skills.thesis: A figure for every mantelpiece comes from a plaster mould and a clear glaze: flat, bold and cheap, it puts a hero, a king or a dog in a poor man's house.
skills.summary: Earthenware figures from Staffordshire: small folk figures, then Victorian flatbacks of heroes, royals and dogs. A lead glaze and bold enamel colours make a cheap mantelpiece figure for the home.
use_cases: an antique or interior set dressing prompt
a folk-art figure in a cheap, bold style

skills.name: Scandinavian tiled stove
skills.thesis: A white tiled stove is both a machine for heat and a piece of furniture: the glaze reflects the light of a dark northern room.
skills.summary: A tall stove clad in white glazed tiles that stores the heat of a short wood fire in a room. The Swedish kakelugn has thin tiles, a plain white face and a soft frame of mouldings.
use_cases: a Nordic interior with a white tiled stove
a heater or fireplace brief in white tile
a museum label on Swedish stove tiles

skills.name: Biscuit porcelain figures
skills.thesis: When the glaze and the colour are gone, only the form is left, so that a porcelain figure can look like fine marble in the hand.
skills.summary: Unglazed white porcelain figures that look like marble and show the form with no colour. Vincennes and Sèvres made them after the paintings of Boucher and the models of Falconet, for the dessert table and the shelf.
use_cases: a museum label for a biscuit figure
a prompt for a matt white porcelain figure
a collector's brief for French porcelain

skills.name: Sèvres rococo porcelain
skills.thesis: A soft, glassy body takes a deep, even ground colour that no hard paste can match; the painter then leaves white windows for the flowers.
skills.summary: Soft-paste porcelain of the royal factory at Sèvres. A glossy ground colour, such as bleu céleste or rose, frames white reserves that carry flowers and birds, with fine gilt edges. Louis XV and Madame de Pompadour were its patrons.
use_cases: a French court dinner service prompt
a museum label on Sèvres soft paste

skills.name: Creamware, neoclassical
skills.thesis: A light cream body and a clear glaze, in a plain classical form, outsell both porcelain and delftware, because the whole service is cheap, even and easy to match.
skills.summary: Cream-coloured lead-glazed earthenware that is light, cheap and strong. Potters in Staffordshire and Leeds make plain, classical forms with a feather edge or pierced work, and sell it to every table in Europe.
use_cases: a plain period dinner service brief
a museum label on English earthenware

skills.name: Mocha and banded ware
skills.thesis: A machine can turn the bands of a dipped jug in one pass, and one drop of acid colour on a wet slip makes a tree that no hand can plan.
skills.summary: Cheap pale earthenware for the tavern and the farm kitchen. Bands of coloured slip are turned on a lathe, and a drop of acid colour spreads into a fern or a tree.
use_cases: a tavern or kitchen set dressing of 1800
a museum label on mocha ware
a mug or jug brief that needs earth-tone bands

wall_thickness.note: A lathe can cut thin wall that earthenware slip does not allow by hand.

skills.name: Jasperware (Neoclassical)
skills.thesis: A matt coloured stoneware with white Greek and Roman reliefs lets an English factory make the antique world for the library table.
skills.summary: A fine, dense, unglazed stoneware that Josiah Wedgwood made from 1775. It is stained in pale blue, green or lilac and carries white relief figures in the classical manner.
use_cases: a neoclassical urn or vase for a Georgian interior
a pale blue and white product brief
a museum label on English stoneware of 1780

wall_thickness.note: The wall is thick compared with porcelain, because jasper is a dense stoneware.

skills.name: Blue willow transferware
skills.thesis: A copper plate puts a Chinese-style blue picture on cheap white earthenware, so that every household owns the pattern that once only a rich house could buy.
skills.summary: White earthenware that carries a blue pattern in the Chinese manner, printed from an engraved copper plate. The willow pattern, with a bridge, a tree, a boat and two birds, is the best known of the many designs.
use_cases: a blue pattern brief for a plate
a museum label on printed earthenware

skills.name: American stoneware crock
skills.thesis: A crock must hold butter, pickles or pork for a winter, so the body is dense stoneware and the only ornament is one quick blue brush stroke.
skills.summary: Straight-sided stoneware for the farm and the dairy: crocks, churns, jugs and jars. A salt or slip glaze makes the wall tight, and a swift cobalt motif marks the size.
use_cases: a farmhouse or an antique-shop set dressing
a museum label on 19th-century American stoneware
a brief for a rustic utensil crock with one blue motif

wall_thickness.note: A crock wall is 10 to 14 mm so that it resists frost and knocks.

skills.name: Regency gilded bone china
skills.thesis: Bone ash gives English potters a strong, white and warm body at a fair price, and they cover it in colour and gold to match the rich rooms of the Regency.
skills.summary: Bone china with rich painting and heavy gilding for the houses of the Regency. The body has about 40 per cent bone ash, so it is strong, white and translucent, and it carries bold Imari patterns, botanical flowers and wide gold bands.
use_cases: a museum label on early bone china

skills.name: Spongeware
skills.thesis: A sponge turns a cheap white pot into a coloured one in a few seconds, so that a worker without training can decorate a hundred pieces in an hour.
skills.summary: Cheap white earthenware that potters dabbed with a cut sea sponge dipped in colour. The soft blue or green mottle fills a bowl, a jug or a canister with little skill.
use_cases: a museum label on sponged earthenware
a mixing bowl brief with a loose blue dab pattern

skills.name: Victorian encaustic tiles
skills.thesis: A pattern that is part of the clay, and not a layer on it, does not wear off under a million feet.
skills.summary: Hard floor tiles with a pattern of clay in a second colour set into the face. Factories pressed them from dust and sold them to churches, halls and houses. The pattern is flat, geometric and mostly red, buff, black and blue.
use_cases: a Victorian hall or church floor
a hard-wearing floor with a medieval pattern

skills.name: Parian statuary
skills.thesis: Fine sculpture comes into the Victorian parlour when a white porcelain slip is cast in a mould and fired without a glaze: marble, but small and cheap.
skills.summary: Unglazed white porcelain that copies marble, cast in moulds as statuettes and busts. Victorian potters made it for the home, from copies of known sculpture to sentimental and literary figures.
use_cases: a museum or auction label for a parian figure
a prop of a white statuette on a shelf
a brief for a marble-look reproduction

skills.name: Porcelain insulator
skills.thesis: A wire needs a dry, hard, glazed surface between it and the earth, so the clay body is dense and the shape is a stack of rain skirts.
skills.summary: Glazed porcelain that holds a live wire away from a pole or a tower. The shape follows the electric field and the rain: a stack of skirts, a brown or grey glaze, and a cement joint to a metal cap.
use_cases: an industrial still-life with power line hardware
a technical brief for a glazed electrical part
a collector label for a telegraph insulator

wall_thickness.note: Large units for high voltage have thick walls; small pin insulators are thinner.

skills.name: Victorian architectural terracotta
skills.thesis: A smoky industrial city needs a facade that rain can wash: a glazed or hard-fired clay block gives rich ornament at a price that a mason cannot meet.
skills.summary: Fired clay blocks in buff, red and blue-grey that English makers pressed in moulds for museums, schools and town halls. Cheap in a smoky city, the clay kept its colour where stone turned black.
use_cases: a heritage or conservation brief on a terracotta facade
a render of a Victorian public building
a label on a moulded terracotta frieze

ornament_level.note: Ornament is the point of the style; keep it above 0.5 for a true Victorian facade.

wall_thickness.note: A hollow block has a wall of 25 to 50 mm; the knob stops at 40 mm.

skills.name: Victorian sanitary ware
skills.thesis: A new sanitary fitting must look like fine china, so that a family sees a clean, rich object in a room that was once hidden.
skills.summary: The first ceramic bathroom of the home. Basins, pans and cisterns of earthenware and early vitreous china carry blue, brown or polychrome transfer prints, moulded flowers and gilt lines.
use_cases: a period bathroom set for a film or a game
an interior brief for a Victorian house
a museum label on an early flush toilet

wall_thickness.note: Early earthenware basins are thicker than later vitreous pieces.

skills.name: Arts and Crafts art pottery
skills.thesis: A pot is a work of art when one person makes it from clay and glaze, and the hand is allowed to show.
skills.summary: Hand-made British art pottery after 1872. The potters of Lambeth, Chelsea and Fulham used salt glaze and ruby lustre, and made each piece one by one with a visible hand.
use_cases: a hand-made vase for an Arts and Crafts interior
a museum label on late Victorian art pottery

skills.name: American art pottery
skills.thesis: A pottery of artists can make a vase a painting or a leaf: one line paints in slip under glaze, and the other line builds the form in matt colour.
skills.summary: Art pottery from American potteries after 1880. Rookwood painted slip under a clear glaze, and Grueby made thick matt green glazes for vases with leaf forms.
use_cases: a hand-painted vase for a Craftsman interior
a museum label on American art pottery

skills.name: Fireclay butler sink
skills.thesis: A kitchen sink must be deep, heavy and glazed so hard that a pot, a brush and boiling water do not mark it.
skills.summary: A deep, square, white sink cast in fireclay. Thick walls, a rolled rim and a weir overflow make a sink that takes heat and weight, and it stays in use in kitchens today.
use_cases: a restoration spec for a period house
a prompt for a still-life scullery

wall_thickness.note: Fireclay is cast thick: a wall of 20 to 30 mm keeps the sink from warping in the kiln.

skills.name: Chicago School terracotta
skills.thesis: When a steel frame carries the load, the wall becomes a skin: a thin clay tile protects the steel from fire and carries the ornament.
skills.summary: Thin, fireproof terracotta cladding on the steel frames of early skyscrapers. Architects in Chicago used it for flat, white or cream walls and for flowing plant ornament.
use_cases: a render of an early skyscraper with terracotta skin
a conservation note on a terracotta tile facade
a spandrel panel design in low relief

ornament_level.note: The tile skin is thin and flat; the ornament does not carry load.

wall_thickness.note: A thin cladding tile has a wall of 5 to 12 mm in its ribs and 25 mm at the face.

skills.name: Art Nouveau ceramics
skills.thesis: A vase grows like a plant: its form follows one living curve, and the glaze flows over it in deep colour.
skills.summary: Vessels of 1893 to 1914 with flowing plant forms and deep glaze effects. French potters fired flambé stoneware, and Dutch and Danish works made thin porcelain with crystal and underglaze colour.
use_cases: a flowing vase for an Art Nouveau interior
a flambé or crystalline glaze brief
a museum label on French or Dutch pottery of 1900

wall_thickness.note: Eggshell porcelain reaches 1 mm; flambé stoneware is much thicker.

skills.name: Hungarian Secession ceramics
skills.thesis: A national style needs a national material: frost-proof, bright clay tiles with Hungarian folk flowers and Eastern patterns make a roof into the face of a building.
skills.summary: Colourful architectural ceramics of the Hungarian Secession. Ödön Lechner and the Zsolnay factory made frost-proof pyrogranite tiles and iridescent eosin glazes for roofs, domes and facades.
use_cases: a render of a Budapest building with a ceramic roof
a conservation note on pyrogranite tiles
a roof or finial design in folk colours

ornament_level.note: Roof colour and eosin lustre carry the style; ornament stays high.

wall_thickness.note: Roof tiles are thin; relief panels reach 25 mm.

skills.name: Art Nouveau tiles
skills.thesis: A factory tile can carry the line of a plant, if the mould and the glaze do the drawing.
skills.summary: Moulded earthenware tiles with a plant line in low relief and a deep, soft glaze. The tile joins a flowing stem, a lily or a woman's hair to a sea-green or plum ground. Factories made them for shop fronts, stairs, hearths and tube stations.
use_cases: a hearth or porch in the Art Nouveau style
a shop front or stair in plant relief
a museum label on a moulded tile

skills.name: Trencadís
skills.thesis: A broken tile is not waste: a wall of shards takes any curve, and the glaze colour of each piece joins into one bright surface.
skills.summary: A surface of broken tile and china that is set in mortar on a curved wall, bench or roof. Antoni Gaudí and Josep Maria Jujol made it a free, colourful skin for Barcelona buildings.
use_cases: a render of a Gaudí-style bench or roof
a mosaic design from waste tile
a label for broken ceramic architecture

ornament_level.note: The mosaic is a free pattern; low ornament breaks the style.

wall_thickness.note: The skin adds 10 to 25 mm of shard and mortar to the wall.

skills.name: Subway tile
skills.thesis: A white, shiny, small tile makes a wall that is clean, bright and easy to wash.
skills.summary: A small white rectangular wall tile with a glossy glaze and a bevelled edge, laid in a brick bond. It began as a clean, washable lining for tunnels and stations. It is now the default tile of the kitchen and the bathroom.
use_cases: a plain white wall with a strong grid

skills.name: Anglo-Oriental studio pottery
skills.thesis: A good pot joins the plain beauty of East Asian stoneware with the English craft of one person who makes, glazes and fires it.
skills.summary: British studio pottery that Bernard Leach started at St Ives in 1920. A potter made high-fired stoneware by hand, with ash and iron glazes after Chinese, Korean and Japanese pots.
use_cases: a hand-thrown stoneware bowl or bottle
an ash or tenmoku glaze brief
a museum label on British studio pottery

skills.name: Suprematist porcelain
skills.thesis: A pot is a Suprematist object when its form is built of cylinders, cubes and slabs, and the paint on it is a flat plane of colour.
skills.summary: Tea and coffee ware in white porcelain from the State Porcelain Factory in Petrograd. Malevich and his pupils turned the plain shapes of Suprematist painting into pots, cups and jugs in blocks, planes and bars.
use_cases: a product brief for a geometric tea service
a design-history exhibit on the avant-garde
a prompt for a still life in the style of the 1920s Russian avant-garde

skills.name: Cornishware
skills.thesis: A kitchen set looks right when every piece carries the same four blue stripes on white, so the shelf reads as one plain family.
skills.summary: White earthenware kitchen ware with four blue hand-banded stripes. It started as a set of storage jars and grew to jugs, mugs and egg cups, in a pattern that a lathe repeats by hand.
use_cases: a museum label on blue-banded earthenware
a canister or jug brief with a strict four-stripe pattern

skills.name: Art Deco ceramic figures
skills.thesis: The modern woman, the dancer and the fast animal are stylised into long lines and flat planes, then cast in clay and painted in hard, bright colours.
skills.summary: Slip-cast figures of dancers, bathers, birds and gazelles with long limbs, sharp planes and bold colour. Makers in Vienna, Turin and Bohemia made them in earthenware for the cabinet and the cocktail room.
use_cases: a 1920s interior or cabaret scene prop
a brief for a stylised dancer figurine
a product design reference for a deco mantel piece

skills.name: Art Deco faience facade
skills.thesis: A glazed, washable slab turns a commercial building into a bright sign: colour and geometry attract the eye from the street.
skills.summary: Glazed terracotta slabs in bright colours and gold that clad cinemas, shops and towers of the 1920s and 1930s. The ornament is flat and geometric: zigzags, sunbursts and stepped lines.
use_cases: a render of an Art Deco cinema or tower front
a conservation note on glazed terracotta slabs
a facade pattern with zigzag and sunburst in relief

ornament_level.note: Geometry carries the ornament; keep the relief flat.

wall_thickness.note: A hollow slab is 20 to 40 mm thick at the face; the webs behind it are not counted.

skills.name: Mingei folk craft
skills.thesis: The most beautiful pots are the plain tools of daily life that anonymous craftspeople make in large numbers, with local clay and no wish for fame.
skills.summary: A Japanese movement that began in 1926. Yanagi Sōetsu and the potters Hamada Shōji and Kawai Kanjirō praised plain pots by unknown village potters and made new pots of the same kind.
use_cases: a daily-use bowl, jar or bottle in the folk craft style
a museum label on mingei pottery

skills.name: Coloured bathroom suite
skills.thesis: Sanitary ware can be a colour of the room, and one even glaze on every piece makes a bathroom that matches.
skills.summary: A bath, a basin and a WC glazed in the same strong colour: pink, green, blue, yellow or later avocado. The even gloss glaze and the matching set make the bathroom a room of colour.
use_cases: a film set for a 1950s house
a retro bathroom brief with matching tiles

wall_thickness.note: The wall of a vitreous basin is thinner than the wall of a fireclay bath.

skills.name: Art Deco tableware
skills.thesis: A cheap white earthenware becomes modern when a painter puts strong flat colour in sharp geometry on a form with angles and cones.
skills.summary: Bright, hand-painted earthenware in angles, cones and bands. Painters in the potteries of Stoke-on-Trent put bold flat colour on a white ground, and the shapes copy the stepped and conical forms of the Paris fair of 1925.
use_cases: a museum label on Art Deco pottery

wall_thickness.note: Earthenware is thicker than bone china; the colour bands hide the weight.

skills.name: Bauhaus modern tableware
skills.thesis: A service is a tool for the table: it is a few simple solids, in white, that fit one another and give good use.
skills.summary: Plain white porcelain made for a factory, in simple solid forms. The designers drop the ornament and the gold, and shape a service that stacks, pours well and costs little to make.
use_cases: a museum label on 1930s German porcelain

wall_thickness.note: Thin and even; the wall is as thin as the casting allows.

skills.name: Fiesta colourware
skills.thesis: One simple, ringed shape in a set of strong glaze colours lets every buyer build a table of their own, one piece at a time.
skills.summary: Solid-colour dinnerware for the American home. A round Art Deco shape with concentric rings is glazed in one strong colour, and the buyer mixes the colours of the open stock. The first red glaze held uranium.
use_cases: a retro American kitchen or diner scene

wall_thickness.note: A semi-vitreous earthenware wall is thicker than porcelain.

skills.name: Organic modern tableware
skills.thesis: A table set is easy to live with when its forms flow like pebbles and its colours are the quiet colours of stone, leaf and sand.
skills.summary: Soft, curved dinnerware for the postwar home. The designers shape plates, shakers and pitchers like pebbles and leaves, and glaze them in muted, matt or satin colours of the earth.
use_cases: a mid-century kitchen or dining scene
a museum label on 1940s American design

skills.name: British modernist studio ceramics
skills.thesis: A modern pot is a precise form with a quiet surface, where the glaze and the clay do the work that ornament did before.
skills.summary: Fine studio ceramics from London after 1946. Lucie Rie and Hans Coper worked in a small studio and made thin bowls, bottles and sculptural forms with a quiet, textured surface.
use_cases: a refined bowl or bottle for a modern interior
a museum label on British modernist ceramics

wall_thickness.note: Rie porcelain walls are 2 to 3 mm thick; Coper stoneware is thicker.

skills.name: Artist ceramics of Vallauris
skills.thesis: A painter treats the potter's vase as a body and the plate as a canvas, and plays with the craft in a joyful, quick and plain way.
skills.summary: Ceramics by painters and sculptors at the Provençal potteries of Vallauris. Picasso made thrown vases into owls, bulls and women, and painted plates in engobe and wax resist, in editions of a few hundred.
use_cases: a museum or auction label for artist ceramics
a prompt for a painter's pottery plate or owl
a brief for a drawn, playful ceramic edition
